===FILE:.cursor/cursor-experiments/docs/forum_post.md===# Showcase: Multi-Agent Orchestration in Cursor - Coordinating Specialized Agents Hi everyone! I wanted to share a demonstration of how we can use Cursor's agentic framework to orchestrate multiple specialized agents to solve complex, multi-step tasks. ## The Concept: Orchestration Over Monoliths Instead of having one giant agent try to do everything, we can break down complex problems into specialized roles. In this demo, we use a hierarchical structure: 1. **Primary Agent (`@trip-planner`)**: Acts as the coordinator. It understands the high-level goal and delegates specific research tasks. 2. **Specialized Sub-Agents (`@flight-researcher`, `@hotel-researcher`)**: Experts in their respective domains. They don't need to know about the overall plan, just how to execute their specific task. ## How it Works The project is structured using the standard Cursor configuration folders: - **`.cursor/agents/`**: Defines the persona, instructions, and collaboration rules for each agent. - **`.cursor/skills/`**: Houses custom capabilities (Agent Skills) that agents can invoke. These skills can execute shell scripts to perform real-world actions like searching an API or processing data. ### The Execution Flow When you ask the `@trip-planner` to plan a trip from NYC to San Francisco, it doesn't just "guess." It systematically delegates: ```mermaid graph TD TripPlanner[Trip Planner Agent] --> FlightResearcher[Flight Researcher Agent] TripPlanner --> HotelResearcher[Hotel Researcher Agent] FlightResearcher --> ResearchFlight[Research Flight Skill] HotelResearcher --> ResearchHotel[Research Hotel Skill] ``` ## Real-World Application In this demo: - The **Flight Researcher** uses a script to retrieve airline options. - The **Hotel Researcher** uses a script to find accommodations. - The **Trip Planner** compiles these into a structured `trip_plan.md` and generates a detailed `task_logs.md` with a Mermaid orchestration diagram to show exactly how the work was distributed. ## Key Takeaways for Cursor Users - **Modularity**: Specialized agents are easier to maintain and refine. - **Delegation**: High-level agents can focus on logic and coordination, while sub-agents handle the "grunt work." - **Skill Integration**: Connecting agents to shell scripts opens up endless possibilities for automation beyond simple text generation. --- I'd love to hear how others are using multi-agent workflows in Cursor! Are you using delegation for your development tasks? What kind of custom skills have you built? Check out the full demo in this repo to see the configuration files and execution logs!
===FILE:.cursor/cursor-experiments/README.md===# Demo: Multi-Agent Orchestration in Cursor This project demonstrates how specialized AI agents can collaborate to solve complex, multi-step tasks within the Cursor IDE. ## Project Goal The primary goal is to showcase the **orchestration capability** of Cursor's agentic framework. By defining a high-level "Trip Planner" agent that coordinates with specialized "Flight" and "Hotel" researchers, we illustrate a modular and scalable approach to automated problem-solving. ![Screenshot](./docs/assets/task.png) ## Key Features - **Multi-Agent Collaboration**: Transparent delegation of sub-tasks from a primary agent to specialized sub-agents. - **Skill-Based Execution**: Integration of custom "Agent Skills" that execute shell scripts to perform specific actions (e.g., searching data). ## Subagents and Agent Skills ### Agents - [@trip-planner](.cursor/agents/trip-planner.md): Orchestrates the entire trip planning process by delegating tasks to specialized agents. - [@flight-researcher](.cursor/agents/flight-researcher.md): Researches flight options based on origin and destination. - [@hotel-researcher](.cursor/agents/hotel-researcher.md): Researches hotel accommodations at the destination. ### Agent Skills - [@research-flight](.cursor/skills/research-flight/SKILL.md): Executes flight search scripts to retrieve travel options. - [@research-hotel](.cursor/skills/research-hotel/SKILL.md): Executes hotel search scripts to retrieve accommodation details. ### Relationships across subagents and Agent Skills ```mermaid graph TD TripPlanner[Trip Planner Agent] --> FlightResearcher[Flight Researcher Agent] TripPlanner --> HotelResearcher[Hotel Researcher Agent] FlightResearcher --> ResearchFlight[Research Flight Skill] HotelResearcher --> ResearchHotel[Research Hotel Skill] ``` ## Usage Instructions To run the demonstration: 1. Open the Cursor IDE in this repository. 2. Open the Chat panel (`Cmd+L` or `Ctrl+L`). 3. Use the `@trip-planner` agent by typing its name or using the `/trip-planner` slash command (if configured). 4. Provide a prompt such as: ```text I want to go to San Francisco from NYC. Please write a trip report in @reports/plan_to_san_francisco/trip_plan.md and logs in @reports/plan_to_san_francisco/task_logs.md. ``` 5. Observe how Cursor orchestrates the sub-agents and generates the requested files. ## Directory Structure - **`.cursor/agents/`**: Contains agent definitions (YAML-frontmatter Markdown) defining their roles and capabilities. - **`.cursor/skills/`**: Defines custom skills that agents can use, including the scripts they execute. - **`reports/`**: The output directory for generated trip plans and task logs. - **`docs/`**: Project documentation and assets, including screenshots. ## Technical Implementation The orchestration follows a hierarchical pattern: 1. **Agent Definition**: Each agent is defined in `.cursor/agents/`. For example, `trip-planner.md` defines its ability to collaborate with `flight-researcher` and `hotel-researcher`. 2. **Skill Integration**: Agents use skills defined in `.cursor/skills/`. Each skill maps to a specific action, such as executing a shell script. 3. **Simulation Scripts**: For this demo, flight and hotel searches are simulated using Bash scripts (`research_flight.sh` and `research_hotel.sh`) that return randomized results to illustrate the data flow. 4. **Mermaid Generation**: The `trip-planner` is instructed to generate a Mermaid diagram in the task logs to visualize the actual execution path taken during the task. ## Example ### Prompt to Cursor IDE I submit the following prompt to Cursor IDE: ```text /trip-planner I want to go to San Francisco from NYC. Please write a trip report in @reports/plan_to_san_francisco/trip_plan.md . You have to comprehensively and precisely leave logs what and how you address the tasks with a diagram in Mermaid in @reports/plan_to_san_francisco/task_logs.md . You have to show a diagram of what you address the task in the plan. ``` ### Result - [Cursor plan](.cursor/plans/plan_nyc_to_san_francisco_trip_5268c15a.plan.md) - [Trip report](reports/plan_to_san_francisco/trip_plan.md) - [Task logs](reports/plan_to_san_francisco/task_logs.md)

setups. - Respect manual-approval defaults and blast-radius controls. - Keep plan epic-level (no deep implementation decomposition yet). - **Known Risks**: - Migration errors from deduping mirrored artifacts. - Inconsistent policy propagation across skill trees. - Security regressions if control plane hardening is incomplete. - Operational disruption if continuity/state contracts diverge during transition. ## Stage 2 — Scope and Acceptance Criteria ## Scope - **In Scope**: - Gap map from executable baseline (`flagship-foundry-work`) to listed repository areas. - Canonical ownership model (what lives where and why). - Epic-level remediation roadmap across runtime, knowledge, governance, continuity, and operations. - Verification gates and phased rollout checkpoints. - **Non-Goals**: - Immediate code refactors or file moves. - Full task-level breakdown and ticketization. - Rewriting all historical research artifacts. ## Glossary - **Executable baseline**: Production-capable code path in `flagship-foundry-work`. - **Source of truth**: Canonical location owning an artifact type. - **Drift**: Semantically equivalent artifacts diverging over time. - **Continuity state**: Machine-readable task/lifecycle state (`current-task.json`). - **Guardrail pack**: Policy/checklist bundle applied per domain. - **Knowledge pack**: Structured domain knowledge used by planning/orchestration. - **Parity projection**: Consistent doctrine rendered into Cursor/Codex/Claude variants. - **Simulation mode**: Run execution using mock/synthetic adapters. - **Operational readiness**: Security, observability, CI/CD, and reliability gates satisfied. - **Evidence bundle**: Test/build/run artifacts proving gate completion. ## Acceptance Criteria - Given the listed paths, when ownership mapping is applied, then each artifact type has one canonical source and documented sync direction. - Given duplicated research/state artifacts, when dedup policy is adopted, then stale mirrors are archived or regenerated from canonical sources only. - Given `.cursor/.codex/.claude` and `.foundry` divergence, when parity automation is executed, then schemas/skills/templates converge with compatibility tests. - Given control-plane/runtime hardening epics, when executed, then auth, validation, rate limits, and observability are enforced on critical APIs. - Given orchestration currently relies on simulation in places, when adapter hardening is complete, then at least one end-to-end real execution path is production-safe and evidenced. - Given no active continuity task-state, when continuity bootstrap epic is complete, then lifecycle stage, `nextCommandSet`, and `doneCriteria` are machine-readable and updated per phase. - Given CI/CD gaps, when pipeline epics are complete, then lint/test/build/e2e/sbom gates run automatically for affected changes. - Given knowledge gap reports, when ingestion and completeness remediation run, then required packs reach complete or policy-approved threshold. ## Rollback Plan - Apply a two-track rollout: preserve current baseline behavior while introducing canonicalization behind migration scripts and dry-run reports. - Keep reversible snapshots for all moved/deduped artifacts. - Gate each epic with smoke verification and fail-safe fallback to current baseline layout. - Defer destructive cleanup until at least one full release cycle passes with parity checks green. ## Stage 3 — Visualize (C4) ## System Context Diagram ```mermaid C4Context title SystemContext_FlagshipFoundryConvergence Person(platformEngineer, "Platform Engineer", "Maintains SDLC, runtime, and knowledge systems") Person(aiOperator, "AI Operator", "Runs orchestration and planning workflows") System(foundryCore, "Flagship Foundry Core", "Executable orchestration and control plane") System_Ext(repoArtifacts, "Repository Artifact Plane", "Rules, skills, research, state snapshots") System_Ext(externalTools, "Dev Tools and MCP", "Cursor, Codex, Claude, MCP servers") System_Ext(ciSystem, "CI/CD System", "Verification and release automation") Rel(platformEngineer, foundryCore, "Configures and governs") Rel(aiOperator, foundryCore, "Runs import, knowledge, plan, execute flows") Rel(foundryCore, repoArtifacts, "Reads/writes knowledge, state, and governance projections") Rel(foundryCore, externalTools, "Exposes/consumes agent and MCP capabilities") Rel(foundryCore, ciSystem, "Publishes evidence and quality gate results") ``` ## Container Diagram ```mermaid C4Container title ContainerDiagram_FlagshipFoundryConvergence Person(user, "Operator", "Initiates workflows") System_Boundary(foundryBoundary, "Foundry Boundary") { Container(controlPlane, "Control Plane API", "Node.js", "Imports, gaps, focus, plans, runs") Container(orchestratorCli, "Orchestrator CLI", "Node.js", "Pipeline orchestration commands") Container(mcpServer, "Foundry MCP Server", "Node.js stdio", "MCP tools/resources interface") Container(knowledgeEngine, "Knowledge and Gap Engine", "Node.js", "Ingestion, catalogs, completeness") Container(stateStore, "State Store", "File state (current)", "Plans, runs, approvals, manifests") Container(parityProjector, "Parity Projector", "Templates/scripts", "Syncs Cursor/Codex/Claude doctrine") } System_Ext(repoRoot, "Repository Root Assets", "Research docs, skills, rules, snapshots") System_Ext(ci, "CI/CD", "Automated gates and releases") Rel(user, orchestratorCli, "Runs workflows") Rel(orchestratorCli, controlPlane, "Invokes APIs") Rel(mcpServer, controlPlane, "Bridges tool requests") Rel(controlPlane, knowledgeEngine, "Computes coverage and gaps") Rel(controlPlane, stateStore, "Persists continuity and run state") Rel(parityProjector, repoRoot, "Projects canonical doctrine") Rel(ci, controlPlane, "Verifies quality and security gates") Rel(ci, repoRoot, "Checks drift and parity") ``` ## Stage 4 — Applicable Principles and Guardrails ## Applicable Principles - **complexity-budgets**: **yes** — scope includes cross-plane canonicalization; complexity must be constrained by clear ownership boundaries and phased migration. - **contract-first**: **yes** — schema/continuity/API contracts need to be standardized before sync automation and adapter hardening. - **observed-vs-declared-truth**: **yes** — runtime state in `state/` and report artifacts must be reconciled with declared governance/rules and canonical catalog definitions. ## Guardrail Packs - `guardrail:typescript-core` — strict typing, boundary-safe contracts, reliable tests for changed TypeScript/JS surfaces. - `guardrail:web-frontend` — applies to graph viewer/control-plane UI surfaces where relevant. - `guardrail:chrome-extension-mv3` — apply only to extension-related artifacts under iterative/cursor-extension paths if modified in later phases. - `guardrail:aws-serverless` — not primary for current baseline unless deployment architecture expands into serverless targets. ## Gap Analysis (Epic-Level) - **Epic A — Canonical Source-of-Truth Map** - Define ownership matrix for executable code, governance rules, skill packs, schemas, research outputs, and runtime state. - Publish sync-direction policy (canonical -> projections only). - **Epic B — Duplication and Drift Control** - Identify duplicate doc/report families (root vs package mirrors vs archives) and classify: canonical, generated, archive. - Add drift checks to detect divergent copies early. - **Epic C — Continuity Contract Unification** - Align `.codex` and `.foundry` task-state schemas (including lifecycle stage support). - Bootstrap active continuity state so lifecycle routing is machine-readable. - **Epic D — Skill/Rule Parity Pipeline** - Normalize `.cursor/.codex/.claude` shared doctrine projection with explicit compatibility tests. - Keep local environment overrides safe (detect-and-merge, no blind overwrite). - **Epic E — Runtime Security Hardening** - Harden control plane with authn/authz, validation, payload controls, and rate limiting. - Remove broad CORS defaults and enforce explicit trust boundaries. - **Epic F — Operational Reliability and Observability** - Add structured telemetry, timeout/retry policy, and error taxonomy across orchestration services. - Produce run-level evidence bundles for diagnosis and auditability. - **Epic G — Real Execution Adapter Path** - Replace simulation-default run path with at least one production-safe terminal/task adapter and rollback controls. - Enforce safe execution boundaries (worktree isolation, policy checks). - **Epic H — CI/CD and Quality Gates** - Introduce automated lint/test/build/e2e/security/sbom gates aligned to affected scope. - Tie release readiness to evidence-backed completion criteria. - **Epic I — Knowledge Coverage Completion** - Close remaining incomplete packs (notably environment parity) and codify pack freshness SLAs. - Ensure gap recommendations auto-feed personas/runbooks/guardrails updates. - **Epic J — Release and Operating Model** - Define phased rollout across discover->operate with explicit go/no-go gates. - Add incident and rollback playbooks for canonicalization migrations. ## Milestone Sequence 1. **M1 Foundation**: Epic A + C (ownership and continuity contracts). 2. **M2 Convergence**: Epic B + D + I (drift/parity/knowledge completion). 3. **M3 Production Core**: Epic E + F + G (security, observability, real adapter). 4. **M4 Industrialization**: Epic H + J (CI/CD gates and operational model). ## Stage 5 — Intent Packet Summary - **Phase**: ready for `plan` - **Primary Agent**: `@orchestrator` - **Next Action**: invoke `/scope-chunker` on this intent packet to decompose epics into bounded work orders with acceptance tests and gate commands. - **Key Decisions Pending**: - Final canonical home for root-level research artifacts (retain in root vs move under one docs namespace). - Archive retention policy for zip snapshots and iterative state copies. - Preferred auth model for control-plane APIs (local-only, token, or federated). - **Definition of Ready Met**: **yes** (problem, scope, constraints, risks, acceptance criteria, rollback, principles, guardrails, and milestone roadmap are defined).

===FILE:.cursor/rules/01-code-standards/error-handling-and-reliability.mdc===--- alwaysApply: true description: Error handling, retries, and reliability standards --- # Error Taxonomy, Propagation, Retries & Timeouts Define domain error classes, wrap third-party errors at boundaries, and retry only transient failures with capped backoff + jitter. **Justification:** Clear error semantics and disciplined retries improve resilience and reduce noisy failures. ## Domain Error Types Wrap third-party errors once at module boundaries; rethrow as domain errors. ```typescript export class TransientNetworkError extends Error { constructor(message: string, cause?: unknown) { super(message); this.name = 'TransientNetworkError'; (this as any).cause = cause; } } ``` ## Retries & Timeouts - Use capped exponential backoff with jitter for network calls - Never retry non-idempotent operations - Apply request timeouts and circuit breakers for unstable deps

===FILE:.cursor/rules/01-code-standards/node-platform-standards.mdc===--- alwaysApply: true description: Node platform standards for reliability and performance --- # Node Platform Standards Validate inputs, avoid blocking CPU on request threads, enforce request timeouts, and prefer streaming for large payloads. **Justification:** Prevents reliability and performance pitfalls in services and webhooks. ## Input Validation ```typescript const validate = ajv.compile(schema); if (!validate(body)) throw new Error('invalid'); ``` ## Concurrency & Timeouts - Reject long CPU work on request threads; offload to workers/queues - Enforce per-request timeouts and sensible connection pooling
===FILE:.cursor/rules/01-code-standards/separation-of-concerns.mdc===--- description: Separation of concerns for layering and responsibilities alwaysApply: true --- # Separation of Concerns (SoC) Ensure the codebase is divided into distinct layers: presentation (UI components), business logic (services), and data access (stores/adapters). Each layer should handle its specific concern without overlapping responsibilities. UI components should not contain parsing, storage, or network logic. **Justification**: Separation prevents tight coupling, making the SummerySky extension easier to maintain, test, and extend across portals and workflows. **Example**: Keep portal-specific parsing in `libs/summerysky/portal-*` and invoke it from the service worker, rather than parsing directly inside sidepanel components. **Related Rules**: [single-responsibility.mdc](mdc:.cursor/rules/01-code-standards/single-responsibility.mdc), [simplicity.mdc](mdc:.cursor/rules/01-code-standards/simplicity.mdc)
===FILE:.cursor/rules/01-code-standards/simplicity.mdc===--- description: Favor simple, maintainable solutions over complexity alwaysApply: true --- # Simplicity Favor simple, straightforward solutions over complex ones, avoiding unnecessary abstractions or over-engineering. **Justification**: Simplicity reduces technical debt and enhances maintainability. **Example**: Use basic hooks in `HomeTab.tsx` instead of complex state management unless needed. **Related Rules**: [separation-of-concerns.mdc](mdc:.cursor/rules/01-code-standards/separation-of-concerns.mdc), [single-responsibility.mdc](mdc:.cursor/rules/01-code-standards/single-responsibility.mdc)
===FILE:.cursor/rules/01-code-standards/single-responsibility.mdc===--- description: Single-responsibility guidance for functions and modules alwaysApply: true --- # Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) Each function, class, or module should have one, and only one, responsibility. This means focusing on a single task or concern. **Justification**: Reliability is critical, SRP reduces bug risk by limiting scope and simplifies debugging and refactoring. **Example**: `RecipeExecutor` should only handle recipe execution, while record export logic stays in `@ss/google-export` and storage logic stays in `@ss/patient-records`. **Related Rules**: [separation-of-concerns.mdc](mdc:.cursor/rules/01-code-standards/separation-of-concerns.mdc)
===FILE:.cursor/rules/01-code-standards/ts-standards-and-strictness.mdc===--- alwaysApply: true description: TypeScript strictness, imports, and public API standards --- # TypeScript Standards: Strictness, Imports & Public Surfaces Enable strict compiler options across all projects, avoid `any`, and restrict imports to stable public surfaces via path aliases. **Justification:** Strict typing and stable import surfaces reduce defects, improve editor tooling, and make refactors safer across shared code. ## Compiler Options Enable strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, noImplicitOverride, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, bundler module resolution, and isolatedModules for test compatibility. ```json { "compilerOptions": { "strict": true, "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true, "noImplicitOverride": true, "exactOptionalPropertyTypes": true, "moduleResolution": "bundler", "isolatedModules": true, "esModuleInterop": true, "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true } } ``` ### Test Environment Configuration For projects using ES modules in tests, ensure tsconfig supports both build and test environments: ```json // tsconfig.json (project root) { "extends": "../../tsconfig.base.json", "compilerOptions": { "isolatedModules": true, "esModuleInterop": true, "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true, "module": "ESNext" }, "include": ["src/**/*"], "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist", "coverage"] } ``` ⚠️ **Warning:** Do not disable strict mode in project tsconfigs; request waivers via ADR if absolutely necessary. ### tsconfig.json Path Calculation (NX Best Practice) When creating `tsconfig.json` files in NX libraries, the `extends` path must correctly reference `tsconfig.base.json` at the workspace root. **Count directory levels carefully** to avoid build failures. **Path Calculation Rules:** 1. Count the number of directory levels from the library's `tsconfig.json` to the workspace root 2. Use that many `../` segments in the `extends` path 3. Always verify the path exists before committing **Examples:** ```json // For libs/Google-Chrome-Extension-Library/core/runtime/tsconfig.json // Path: libs/ -> Google-Chrome-Extension-Library/ -> core/ -> runtime/ // Levels: 4 (libs, Google-Chrome-Extension-Library, core, runtime) { "extends": "../../../../tsconfig.base.json" } // For libs/Google-Chrome-Extension-Library/ui/shared-components/tsconfig.json // Path: libs/ -> Google-Chrome-Extension-Library/ -> ui/ -> shared-components/ // Levels: 4 (libs, Google-Chrome-Extension-Library, ui, shared-components) { "extends": "../../../../tsconfig.base.json" } // For apps/chrome-extensions/job-hunt-extension/tsconfig.json // Path: apps/ -> chrome-extensions/ -> job-hunt-extension/ // Levels: 3 (apps, chrome-extensions, job-hunt-extension) { "extends": "../../../tsconfig.base.json" } ``` **Verification Command:** Before committing, verify the path resolves correctly: ```bash cd <library-directory> ls -la <calculated-path>/tsconfig.base.json ``` **Common Error:** Using too many `../` segments (e.g., `../../../../../tsconfig.base.json` when `../../../../tsconfig.base.json` is correct) causes Vite/esbuild to fail with "Cannot read file" errors. 💡 **Tip:** When copying a `tsconfig.json` from another library, always verify the path depth matches your library's location. ## No `any` & Safer Assertions Disallow `any`. Prefer `unknown` with user-defined type guards. Use `as` assertions sparingly at boundaries. ```typescript function isLead(x: unknown): x is { id: string } { return typeof x === 'object' && x !== null && 'id' in x; } ``` ## Path Aliases & Public Surfaces Expose only `src/index.ts` from each library through path aliases. Internal files are not importable across libs. ```json { "compilerOptions": { "baseUrl": ".", "paths": { "@mm/*": ["libs/*/src/index.ts"] } } } ``` 💡 **Tip:** Create explicit barrel files per library to keep public APIs small and documented. ## Examples ```json { "rules": { "@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any": "error" } } ``` ## Related Rules - architecture-and-nx-boundaries - testing-strategy
===FILE:.cursor/rules/02-architecture/architecture-and-nx-boundaries.mdc===--- alwaysApply: true description: "Monorepo layout and boundary rules" --- # Architecture, Workspace Layout & Nx Boundaries Define a predictable Nx layout with strict domain boundaries and dependency constraints to keep the monorepo fast and modular. **Justification:** Clear layers and enforced constraints prevent accidental coupling, enable parallel work, and support safe refactors at scale. ## Workspace Layout Organize the monorepo into top-level directories: apps, libs, tools, e2e, and docs. Libraries follow <domain>/<type> where type ∈ feature, ui, data-access, util, config, testing. Every project declares Nx tags to enable lint rules for dependency constraints. - apps/: runnable applications and entry points - libs/: reusable libraries grouped by domain and type - tools/: repo automation, codegen, migration scripts - e2e/: Playwright-based end-to-end suites - docs/: ADRs, architecture diagrams, API references ## Cross-Initiative Reuse (SummerySky) Features for `apps/chrome-extensions/PMHNP-Administration-SummerySky` MUST be implemented as reusable libs first. The app should only wire UI, routing, and Chrome/MV3 entry points. - Place reusable code in `libs/summerysky/*` (or `libs/Google-Chrome-Extension-Library/*` for shared extension utilities). - Avoid portal-specific assumptions in shared libs; keep portal adapters in data-access libraries. - Expose clean public APIs via `index.ts`; do not import deep paths across libs. - If a feature is SummerySky-only today, still design it as a portable library so other initiatives can adopt it with minimal changes. ## Dependency Constraints Enforce domain and layer constraints using Nx and ESLint. Higher layers may depend on lower layers; never the reverse. Only import from a library's public surface (index.ts). ```json { "extends": ["plugin:@nx/typescript"], "rules": { "@nx/enforce-module-boundaries": [ "error", { "enforceBuildableLibDependency": true, "allow": [], "depConstraints": [ { "sourceTag": "type:feature", "onlyDependOnLibsWithTags": ["type:data-access","type:ui","type:util","type:config"] }, { "sourceTag": "type:data-access", "onlyDependOnLibsWithTags": ["type:util","type:config"] }, { "sourceTag": "type:ui", "onlyDependOnLibsWithTags": ["type:util","type:config"] } ] } ] } } ``` 💡 **Tip:** Prefer small, composable libraries over monolithic ones to maximize reuse and cache hits. ## Tagging Examples ```json { "name": "@mm/patients/data-access", "tags": ["scope:patients","type:data-access"] } ``` ## Examples ```json {"name":"@mm/pipeline/util","tags":["scope:eng","type:util"]} ``` ## Related Rules - ts-standards-and-strictness - dev-workflow-and-git - ci-cd-and-releases
===FILE:.cursor/rules/03-workflow/ai-sdlc-orchestrator.mdc===--- alwaysApply: true description: Repo-wide SDLC orchestrator driven by Codex continuity state and Flagship Foundry agent hierarchy --- # SDLC Orchestrator (Codex + Cursor + Claude Code) Use this rule to keep AI work aligned with the SDLC process defined in `/.cursor/rules/03-workflow/sdlc-setup.mdc` and to apply the practical feature/bug/hotfix workflows in `/.cursor/rules/03-workflow/ship-it-workflow.mdc`. When `.foundry/projects/**/current-task.json` exists (Flagship Foundry continuity, **ADR-011**), treat it as the phase source of truth for the matching project. If absent, legacy `.codex/projects/**/current-task.json` may still exist for Codex-only workflows: - Phase state: `sdlcPhase` (7-phase legacy) or `lifecycleStage` (11-phase Flagship) - Verification commands: `nextCommandSet` - Completion criteria: `doneCriteria` Specialist agents are defined in `.cursor/agents/` (Cursor) and `.claude/agents/` (Claude Code). Skills are in `.cursor/skills/` and `.claude/skills/`. Do not re-state every checklist item here — follow the existing SDLC and ship-it docs as canonical text, and use this file to orchestrate ordering, gates, and agent delegation. ## 1) Detect change intent (silent inference) Infer the closest workflow from the user request: - If the user asks for “new feature”, “add capability”, “implement X”, follow the Feature workflow in `ship-it-workflow.mdc`. - If the user asks for “bug”, “fix”, “regression”, “broken”, follow the Bug Fix workflow in `ship-it-workflow.mdc`. - If the user asks for “urgent”, “prod break”, “sev-1”, “hotfix”, follow the Hotfix Fast Path in `ship-it-workflow.mdc`. - If the request is documentation-only, follow the SDLC phases up to and including `document` and run the smallest relevant verification gates. Also map intent to Flagship 11-phase lifecycle stages via the `sdlc-phase-router` skill: - discover / define / visualize / architect → delegate to `@systems-architect` (with `@context-curator` for source packet) - plan → orchestrate directly (break architecture into bounded implementation slices) - implement → delegate to `@builder` with explicit file scope and contracts - verify → delegate to `@verifier` (independent validation, never the builder) - release → delegate to `@docs-release-agent` - operate → delegate to `@performance-reviewer` - diagnose → delegate to `@verifier` + `@security-reviewer` - improve → delegate to `@docs-release-agent` ## 2) Pick the SDLC state source Step A: Look for task-state continuity state (Foundry first) - Search for `.foundry/projects/**/current-task.json` (**ADR-011**). - If not found, search for legacy `.codex/projects/**/current-task.json`. - Choose the project whose `project.path` matches (or is closest to) the files being changed, mentioned paths, or the primary target app. - If no matching project exists: - Search for a task-state file at a recommended path like `.cursor/sdlc/task-state/<project>/current-task.json`. - If neither exists, treat the flow as generic and follow `sdlc-setup.mdc` phase ordering. Step B: If a task-state file exists, read: - `.foundry/projects/<project>/SDLC_CHARTER.md` or legacy `.codex/projects/<project>/SDLC_CHARTER.md` (project-specific SDLC sequence, guardrails, and quality gates) - the active task-state file for: - `sdlcPhase` - `currentPhase` - `nextCommandSet` - `doneCriteria` ## 3) Map task-state phase to SDLC checklists **Legacy 7-phase (`sdlcPhase`) mapping:** - `plan`: Phase 1 (Project Initialization & Planning) from `sdlc-setup.mdc` - `design`: Phase 2 (Quality Gates & Development Standards) + design decisions (ADR if needed) from `sdlc-setup.mdc` and “Design the Change” in `ship-it-workflow.mdc` - `implement`: Phase 3 + Phase 4 implementation checklist from `sdlc-setup.mdc` - `verify`: Phase 4 verification checklist from `sdlc-setup.mdc`, plus “Run Affected Targets” in `ship-it-workflow.mdc` - `document`: Phase 7 documentation checklist from `sdlc-setup.mdc` and ADR expectations from `documentation-standards.mdc` - `release`: Phase 5 deployment & release checklist from `sdlc-setup.mdc` and “Staging Deploy / Production Rollout” in `ship-it-workflow.mdc` - `operate`: Phase 6 observability & operations checklist from `sdlc-setup.mdc` **Flagship 11-phase (`lifecycleStage`) mapping (when present, takes precedence):** - `discover` → define problem, stakeholders, constraints (use `@context-curator`) - `define` → scope, acceptance criteria, non-goals (use `@systems-architect`) - `visualize` → C4 diagrams, system context, trust boundaries (use `@systems-architect`) - `architect` → ADRs, contracts, schemas, decomposition (use `@systems-architect`) - `plan` → task tree, implementation slices (orchestrator) - `implement` → bounded code/config changes (use `@builder` with explicit file scope) - `verify` → independent validation against criteria (use `@verifier`, never builder) - `release` → release notes, handoff, deployment guide (use `@docs-release-agent`) - `operate` → baseline metrics, monitoring (use `@performance-reviewer`) - `diagnose` → root cause, evidence timeline (use `@verifier` + `@security-reviewer`) - `improve` → learning records, continuity patches (use `@docs-release-agent`) If both fields exist, `lifecycleStage` takes precedence. If neither exists, use ordered SDLC phases from `sdlc-setup.mdc`. **Phase Gate Quick Reference**: `.cursor/skills/sdlc-phase-router/reference/phase-gate-matrix.md` ## 4) Verification command policy (Nx-first) If task-state `nextCommandSet` is non-empty: - Run commands from `nextCommandSet` in the given order. - After each command, confirm the specific gate it represents succeeded (typecheck/test/build/e2e slice). - Only proceed to the next SDLC phase when the completion criteria for the current phase are satisfied (use task-state `doneCriteria` when present, otherwise use the `sdlc-setup.mdc` quality gates). If task-state `nextCommandSet` is empty or task-state state is not present: - Prefer Nx affected pipelines: - `pnpm exec nx affected:lint --parallel` - `pnpm exec nx affected:test --parallel` - `pnpm exec nx affected:build --parallel` - Add the smallest targeted e2e/smoke verification that matches the change surface (UI vs service worker vs integration boundaries). ## 5) DoR / DoD gates (feature vs bug) Treat the “Definition of Ready (DoR)” and “Definition of Done (DoD)” as mandatory phase exit criteria: Feature DoR/DoD - DoR must include: one-sentence goal + clear acceptance criteria + identified risks + rollback strategy + test plan outline. - DoD must include: acceptance criteria pass + tests added and passing + documentation updated + staging smoke green + rollback plan validated, when applicable. Bug Fix DoR/DoD - DoR must include: a reproduction description and a failing test plan. - DoD must include: failing test now passes + minimal fix + regression coverage + verification gates green. Hotfix - DoD includes the Sev-1 fast path checklist: incident note, minimal fix with failing test, fast CI lane, production deploy, post-deploy smoke, and monitored stability window. ## 6) Branch and commit safety Use `ship-it-workflow.mdc` branching guidance: - `feat/<scope>-<short-title>` - `fix/<scope>-<issue#>` - `hotfix/<short-title>` Safety constraints from SDLC/charters: - Keep work phase-scoped and independently verifiable. - Do not work directly in the user’s dirty workspace when an applicable charter forbids it (if `.foundry/**/SDLC_CHARTER.md` or `.codex/**/SDLC_CHARTER.md` includes a “do not work directly” guardrail, comply). - Before switching phases or branches, update the active task-state `currentPhase` and `nextCommandSet` for the new state. ## 7) Task-state continuity updates (before phase close) If task-state state is present, maintain deterministic resumability: - Update the active task-state file when: - `currentPhase.status` changes to `verified` or `done` - `activeBranch` changes - `nextCommit` / `nextCommandSet` changes - verification gates complete and `doneCriteria` can be satisfied - Ensure the worktree matches the declared `currentPhase.branch` before continuing with the next phase. ## Canonical references (follow these) These docs are the source of detailed checklist text; this rule only orchestrates ordering and agent delegation: - `/.cursor/rules/03-workflow/sdlc-setup.mdc` - `/.cursor/rules/03-workflow/ship-it-workflow.mdc` - `/.cursor/rules/03-workflow/dev-workflow-and-git.mdc` - `/.cursor/rules/03-workflow/documentation-standards.mdc` - `/.cursor/rules/nx-sdlc/RULE.md` **Agent definitions** (specialist roles and behavioral contracts): - `/.cursor/agents/orchestrator.md` - `/.cursor/agents/systems-architect.md` - `/.cursor/agents/builder.md` - `/.cursor/agents/verifier.md` - `/.cursor/agents/docs-release-agent.md` **Skills** (executable procedures): - `/.cursor/skills/sdlc-phase-router/SKILL.md` - `/.cursor/skills/continuity-writer/SKILL.md` - `/.cursor/skills/nx-verification/SKILL.md` - `/.cursor/skills/handoff-generator/SKILL.md` **Flagship Foundry doctrine**: - `/flagship-foundry/flagship_systems_sdlc_handbook.docx.md` - `/.claude/CHARTER.md`
===FILE:.cursor/rules/03-workflow/dev-workflow-and-git.mdc===--- alwaysApply: true description: Development workflow, branching, and review standards --- # Development Workflow, Branching & Reviews Use Conventional Commits, short-lived branches, CODEOWNERS-based reviews, and objective quality gates. **Justification:** Consistent workflow and automated checks keep velocity high and reduce regressions. ## Conventional Commits - Types: feat, fix, chore, docs, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, revert - Scopes: use Nx domain tags (e.g., patients, dialer, intake) **Example:** Example: feat(patients): add consent verification to intake flow ## PR Hygiene & Reviews - Aim for ≤ 400 LOC per PR where feasible - Require passing gates: lint, typecheck, unit, e2e smoke, docs - CODEOWNERS assign domain reviewers automatically ```markdown # CODEOWNERS /apps/** @mm/frontend-leads /libs/** @mm/architecture /tools/** @mm/devex ``` ## Pre-commit & Pre-push Automate formatting, linting, and typechecking with Husky/lefthook. ```json { "husky": { "hooks": { "pre-commit": "pnpm lint && pnpm format", "pre-push": "pnpm typecheck && pnpm test:ci" } } } ``` ## Related Rules - ci-cd-and-releases
===FILE:.cursor/rules/03-workflow/documentation-standards.mdc===--- description: Documentation standards for code, APIs, and project maintenance globs: ["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx", "**/*.js", "**/*.jsx", "**/README.md", "**/docs/**"] alwaysApply: true --- # Documentation Standards ## JSDoc Requirements ### Public API Documentation All exported functions, classes, and interfaces must include comprehensive JSDoc comments: ```typescript /** * Creates a new user account with email verification * @param userData - User registration data * @param options - Additional registration options * @returns Promise resolving to created user with verification token * @throws {ValidationError} When user data is invalid * @throws {DuplicateUserError} When email already exists * @example * ```typescript * const user = await createUser({ * email: 'user@example.com', * name: 'John Doe' * }); * ``` */ export async function createUser( userData: UserData, options?: RegistrationOptions ): Promise<User> { // implementation } ``` ### Documentation Requirements Checklist - [ ] **@param** - All parameters with types and descriptions - [ ] **@returns** - Return value description and type - [ ] **@throws** - All possible error types and conditions - [ ] **@example** - At least one runnable usage example - [ ] **@since** - Version when feature was added (for major APIs) - [ ] **@deprecated** - Deprecation notice with migration path ## README Standards ### Project README Structure Every project must have a comprehensive README.md: ```markdown # Project Name Brief description of what this project does and its purpose. ## Installation ```bash pnpm install ``` ## Quick Start ```typescript import { mainFunction } from '@mm/project-name'; const result = await mainFunction(); ``` ## API Reference ### Core Functions #### `mainFunction(options: Options): Promise<Result>` Main entry point for the library. **Parameters:** - `options` - Configuration options **Returns:** Promise resolving to operation result **Example:** ```typescript const result = await mainFunction({ debug: true }); ``` ## Environment Variables | Variable | Description | Required | Default | |----------|-------------|----------|---------| | `API_KEY` | API authentication key | Yes | - | | `LOG_LEVEL` | Logging verbosity | No | `info` | ## Nx Targets | Target | Description | Command | |--------|-------------|---------| | `build` | Build the library | `nx build project-name` | | `test` | Run unit tests | `nx test project-name` | | `lint` | Lint the codebase | `nx lint project-name` | ## Development ### Prerequisites - Node.js 18+ - pnpm 8+ ### Setup ```bash pnpm install pnpm build ``` ### Testing ```bash pnpm test pnpm test:watch ``` ## Architecture [Include diagrams or flowcharts showing key components] ## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) for development guidelines. ## License MIT ``` ## ADR (Architecture Decision Records) ### When to Create ADRs Create an ADR for any non-trivial architectural decision: - Choosing between major technology options - Significant API design changes - Performance vs maintainability trade-offs - Security implementation decisions - Breaking changes to existing patterns ### ADR Structure ```markdown # ADR-001: Decision Title ## Status Accepted | Proposed | Rejected ## Context What problem are we solving? What constraints exist? ## Decision What did we decide and why? ## Consequences What becomes easier/harder? What are the trade-offs? ## Alternatives Considered What other options did we evaluate? - **Option A**: Pros/cons - **Option B**: Pros/cons ## Implementation How will this be implemented? Timeline? Migration plan? ``` ### ADR Organization ``` docs/ adr/ 001-use-typescript-strict-mode.md 002-adopt-nx-monorepo.md 003-implement-error-boundaries.md ``` ## API Documentation ### OpenAPI/Swagger Standards For HTTP APIs, maintain OpenAPI specifications: ```yaml openapi: 3.0.3 info: title: User Management API version: 1.0.0 description: User account and profile management paths: /users: post: summary: Create new user requestBody: required: true content: application/json: schema: $ref: '#/components/schemas/UserInput' responses: '201': description: User created successfully content: application/json: schema: $ref: '#/components/schemas/User' components: schemas: UserInput: type: object required: - email - name properties: email: type: string format: email name: type: string ``` ## Auto-Generated Documentation ### CI Documentation Generation Configure CI to automatically generate and publish documentation: ```yaml # .github/workflows/docs.yml name: Generate Docs on: push: branches: [main] pull_request: jobs: docs: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v3 - uses: actions/setup-node@v3 with: node-version: 18 cache: 'pnpm' - run: pnpm install - run: pnpm docs:generate - run: pnpm docs:publish ``` ### TypeDoc Configuration ```javascript // typedoc.config.js module.exports = { entryPoints: ['./src/index.ts'], out: './docs/api', exclude: ['**/*.spec.ts', '**/*.test.ts'], includeVersion: true, disableSources: false, excludePrivate: true, excludeProtected: true, hideGenerator: true, theme: 'default', readme: './README.md', name: 'My Library', tsconfig: './tsconfig.json' }; ``` ## Code Comments Standards ### When to Comment - **Complex business logic** - Explain why, not what - **Workarounds** - Document temporary solutions and TODOs - **Public APIs** - JSDoc as specified above - **Configuration choices** - Why specific values were chosen ### Comment Style ```typescript // ❌ Bad: states the obvious const total = price * quantity; // multiply price by quantity // ✅ Good: explains business logic const total = price * quantity; // Apply volume discount threshold check // ✅ Good: documents workaround // TODO: Remove when API supports bulk operations // Using individual requests due to rate limiting for (const item of items) { await api.update(item); } ``` ## Diagrams and Visual Documentation ### Mermaid Diagrams Use Mermaid for architecture and flow diagrams: ```mermaid graph TD A[User Request] --> B[API Gateway] B --> C[Authentication] C --> D[Business Logic] D --> E[Database] D --> F[External API] E --> G[Response] F --> G ``` ### Architecture Diagrams Include diagrams for: - System architecture overview - Data flow diagrams - Component interaction diagrams - Deployment diagrams ## Documentation Quality Checklist ### Code Documentation - [ ] All public APIs have JSDoc comments - [ ] Examples are runnable and tested - [ ] Error conditions are documented - [ ] Breaking changes are versioned and documented ### Project Documentation - [ ] README includes setup, usage, and API reference - [ ] Environment variables are documented - [ ] Nx targets are listed and described - [ ] Architecture diagrams exist for complex systems ### Process Documentation - [ ] ADRs exist for major decisions - [ ] Development workflow is documented - [ ] Deployment process is clear - [ ] Troubleshooting guides exist ### Maintenance - [ ] Documentation is reviewed in PRs - [ ] Outdated docs are updated with code changes - [ ] CI validates documentation generation - [ ] Documentation is versioned with releases ## Success Metrics - **Documentation Coverage**: > 90% of public APIs documented - **README Completeness**: All projects have comprehensive READMEs - **ADR Compliance**: Major decisions have corresponding ADRs - **Documentation Freshness**: < 30 days since last update - **Developer Satisfaction**: > 80% of developers can find needed information
===FILE:.cursor/rules/03-workflow/sdlc-setup.mdc===--- description: Apply to all files when setting up new projects, services, or major features to ensure complete SDLC coverage alwaysApply: false --- # SDLC Setup & Quality Gates - Freshworks App Monorepo Comprehensive checklist for managing the Software Development Life Cycle in a Freshworks CRM app environment. Use this when spinning up new apps, services, or major features. **Justification:** Structured SDLC prevents technical debt, ensures quality, and reduces production incidents in enterprise CRM integrations. ## SDLC Phases Overview 1. **Plan & Spec** → Define goals, users, scope, success criteria, risks 2. **Design** → Architecture, data models, APIs, UI flows, test strategy 3. **Implement** → Code + tests + configs (with continuous quality gates) 4. **Verify** → Automated + manual testing, QA 5. **Release** → Deploy, migrate, feature toggles 6. **Operate** → Monitor, alert, incident response 7. **Improve** → Learnings, backlog, iteration ## SDLC Checklist - Order of Operations Use this checklist for new apps/services or major features. Each phase builds on the previous. ## Task Progress Tracking & Verification Orchestration (Codex optional) Use this checklist for human-readable SDLC gates, but drive *phase progress* and *verification execution order* from a task-state file. ### Source of truth (Flagship Foundry + legacy Codex) - Foundry projects (**ADR-011**): - Machine-readable task state: `.foundry/projects/<project>/current-task.json` - Project charter / guardrails: `.foundry/projects/<project>/SDLC_CHARTER.md` (optional but preferred) - Legacy Codex-only paths (if present without `.foundry`): - `.codex/projects/<project>/current-task.json` and `SDLC_CHARTER.md` - Non-Codex projects (fallback): - Create and maintain a task-state file using the same schema fields at a recommended path like `.cursor/sdlc/task-state/<project>/current-task.json`. - Use `.codex/schemas/task-state.schema.json` as the reference shape for required fields. ### Task-state fields and how they map to SDLC progression - `sdlcPhase` selects the SDLC phase to target (`plan/design/implement/verify/document/release/operate`). - `currentPhase` drives phase-level tracking: - `currentPhase.id` identifies the current phase artifact/bundle. - `currentPhase.status` must move through `pending` → `in_progress` → (`verified` or `blocked`) → `done`. - `currentPhase.branch` is the worktree/branch that must be checked out when continuing work for that phase. - `nextCommandSet` is the verification execution plan for the *current* phase: - Prefer running those commands in order. - Only mark phase progress complete when the represented quality gates succeed. - `doneCriteria` defines the completion/exit conditions for the phase: - Use it as the “can we close this phase?” checklist in addition to the SDLC quality gates below. - `blockedBy` indicates known blockers: - If non-empty, set `currentPhase.status` to `blocked` and do not advance until blockers are resolved/cleared. - `artifacts` is where required phase outputs (handoff docs, diagrams, exports, runbook snippets) should be created/updated before phase close. ### Resume protocol (deterministic restart) Before continuing from an interruption, ensure the repo state matches the active task-state: - Verify `activeBranch` and `currentPhase.branch`. - Verify `nextCommit` and `nextCommandSet` match the intended phase. - Run the commands in `nextCommandSet` and only continue when the phase’s `doneCriteria` can be satisfied. ### 🚀 Phase 1: Project Initialization & Planning **Repository & Workspace Setup** - [ ] Create repository with main branch protection rules - [ ] Initialize pnpm workspace (monorepo structure) - [ ] Set up Nx workspace configuration - [ ] Add appropriate Nx tags for dependency constraints **Documentation & Governance** - [ ] Choose license (MIT for open-source components) - [ ] Create README.md with setup instructions - [ ] Add CONTRIBUTING.md guidelines - [ ] Configure CODEOWNERS for domain reviewers - [ ] Document success criteria and acceptance tests ### 🛡️ Phase 2: Quality Gates & Development Standards **Code Quality Tools** - [ ] Add Prettier formatter with consistent rules - [ ] Configure ESLint with strict TypeScript rules - [ ] Enable TypeScript strict mode (noImplicitAny, etc.) - [ ] Add Husky pre-commit hooks + lint-staged - [ ] Configure .editorconfig for consistent formatting **Testing Framework Setup** - [ ] Add Vitest for unit tests (preferred for new projects) - [ ] Configure Jest for existing packages (backward compatibility) - [ ] Set up test coverage thresholds (80% global, 70% per-file) - [ ] Add mutation testing (Stryker) for critical paths - [ ] Create smoke test for basic functionality ### 🔧 Phase 3: Infrastructure & Configuration **Environment Management** - [ ] Define environments: dev, staging, prod (+ PR previews) - [ ] Create .env.example with all required variables - [ ] Set up secret management (GitHub Secrets, SSM, Doppler) - [ ] Implement 12-factor config (env vars, no secrets in code) - [ ] Add runtime config validation (fail fast on boot) **CI/CD Pipeline** - [ ] Configure GitHub Actions with Nx affected commands - [ ] Set up pnpm store caching for faster builds - [ ] Implement PR pipeline: install → typecheck → lint → test → build - [ ] Add accessibility checks (a11y) for UI components - [ ] Configure SBOM generation and dependency scanning - [ ] Ensure fast feedback (<10 min for basic checks) ### 🧪 Phase 4: Testing Strategy Implementation **Unit Testing (White-box)** - [ ] Write unit tests for all new functions and classes - [ ] Use Vitest with TypeScript support - [ ] Mock external dependencies (APIs, databases) - [ ] Achieve coverage thresholds (80% global, 70% per-file) - [ ] Add mutation testing for critical business logic **Integration Testing** - [ ] Test module/service interactions - [ ] Add contract tests for API boundaries - [ ] Mock external services (Freshsales, ElevenLabs, Telnyx) - [ ] Test database operations with test containers - [ ] Verify authentication and authorization flows **End-to-End Testing** - [ ] Implement smoke tests (basic functionality verification) - [ ] Add sanity tests for critical user journeys - [ ] Create regression tests for existing features - [ ] Set up Playwright for UI component testing - [ ] Automate webhook service integration tests ### 🚀 Phase 5: Deployment & Release **Preview & Staging** - [ ] Set up ephemeral preview deployments per PR - [ ] Configure staging environment for main branch merges - [ ] Implement feature flags for gradual rollouts - [ ] Add database migration scripts (if needed) - [ ] Configure blue-green deployment strategy **Production Release** - [ ] Set up manual approval gates for production - [ ] Implement canary deployments for high-risk changes - [ ] Add automated rollback procedures - [ ] Configure health checks and monitoring - [ ] Set up alerting for production incidents ### 📊 Phase 6: Observability & Operations **Logging & Monitoring** - [ ] Implement structured JSON logging - [ ] Add OpenTelemetry traces and metrics - [ ] Configure health endpoints (/healthz, /ready) - [ ] Set up error tracking (Sentry) with context - [ ] Create dashboards for key SLIs/SLOs **Security & Compliance** - [ ] Enable dependency vulnerability scanning - [ ] Configure secret scanning in CI - [ ] Set up least-privilege IAM roles - [ ] Implement encryption at rest and in transit - [ ] Add HIPAA compliance mode for PHI modules **Operational Readiness** - [ ] Document runbook (local dev, deploy, rollback) - [ ] Set up on-call rotation and alerting - [ ] Create incident response procedures - [ ] Add post-deployment smoke tests - [ ] Configure backup and disaster recovery ### 📚 Phase 7: Documentation & Knowledge **Technical Documentation** - [ ] Create architecture diagrams (system, data flow) - [ ] Document API contracts and schemas - [ ] Write ADRs for architectural decisions - [ ] Add inline code documentation - [ ] Create troubleshooting guides **Operational Documentation** - [ ] Document deployment procedures - [ ] Create monitoring and alerting runbooks - [ ] Add security incident response guides - [ ] Document backup and recovery procedures - [ ] Create performance tuning guidelines ## Quality Gates by Phase ### Pre-commit (Automatic) - [ ] Code formatting (Prettier) - [ ] Linting (ESLint) - [ ] Type checking (TypeScript) - [ ] Unit tests pass ### Pre-merge (PR Review) - [ ] All pre-commit checks pass - [ ] Code review by domain experts - [ ] Integration tests pass - [ ] Accessibility checks pass (for UI) - [ ] Security scanning clean ### Pre-deploy (CI/CD) - [ ] Full test suite passes - [ ] Build artifacts generated - [ ] SBOM and vulnerability scan complete - [ ] Smoke tests pass in staging ### Post-deploy (Production) - [ ] Health checks pass - [ ] Monitoring alerts configured - [ ] Rollback plan documented - [ ] Incident response team notified ## Success Metrics - **Development Velocity**: PR merge time < 24 hours - **Code Quality**: 0 critical linting errors, 80%+ test coverage - **Reliability**: 99.9% uptime, < 5 min incident response - **Security**: 0 critical vulnerabilities in production - **User Experience**: All accessibility standards met
===FILE:.cursor/rules/03-workflow/ship-it-workflow.mdc===--- description: Battle-tested order of operations for shipping features and fixing bugs in modern Nx monorepos with strict TypeScript, CI/CD, and feature flags alwaysApply: false --- # Ship It! - Battle-Tested Order of Operations Complete workflow for shipping features and fixing bugs in modern Nx monorepos. Follow these steps every time for predictable, safe deployments. **Justification:** Consistent process prevents production incidents, ensures quality, and maintains velocity in enterprise CRM integrations. ## 🎯 Shared Principles ### Branching Strategy ```bash # Features feat/<scope>-<short-title> # Example: feat/intake-guard-dedupe # Bug fixes fix/<scope>-<issue#> # Example: fix/telephony-asserted-id-421 # Hotfixes (Sev-1) hotfix/<short-title> # Example: hotfix/critical-auth-bypass ``` ### Definition of Ready (DoR) ✅ **A task is ready when you can write:** - One-sentence goal - Clear acceptance criteria - Identified risks - Rollback strategy - Test plan outline ❌ **If you can't write these, it's not ready to start** ### Definition of Done (DoD) ✅ **A task is done when:** - All acceptance criteria pass - Tests added and passing - Documentation updated - Post-deploy smoke tests green - Monitoring alerts quiet - Ticket closed --- ## 🚀 FEATURE WORKFLOW - Order of Operations ### 1️⃣ Triage & Spec (30-60 min) ```markdown ## User Story Template As a [user type] I want to [action] So that [benefit] ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] AC-1: Specific measurable outcome - [ ] AC-2: Another measurable outcome - [ ] AC-3: Edge case handling ## Dependencies - APIs: [List external APIs] - Database: [Schema changes needed] - Libraries: [New packages required] - Feature Flag: `feature_<name>_enabled` ## Observability Plan - Logs: Key events to log - Metrics: Counters/timers to add - Dashboard: Panels to create ``` ### 2️⃣ Branch & Scaffold ```bash # Create feature branch git checkout -b feat/<scope>-<short-title> # Generate Nx module/lib if needed nx g @nx/js:lib features/<feature-name> --tags=scope:feature,type:feature # Add feature flag (default OFF) echo "FEATURE_<NAME>_ENABLED=false" >> .env.example ``` ### 3️⃣ Test Plan First ```typescript // Define test cases BEFORE coding // Unit Tests (Pure/Fast) describe('FeatureName Core Logic', () => { it('should handle happy path') it('should validate inputs') it('should handle edge cases') }); // Integration Tests (API ↔ DB) describe('FeatureName Integration', () => { it('should persist data correctly') it('should handle concurrent requests') it('should respect feature flag') }); // E2E Test (User Flow) describe('FeatureName E2E', () => { it('should complete user journey when flag enabled') it('should gracefully degrade when flag disabled') }); // Smoke Test (Critical Path) describe('FeatureName Smoke', () => { it('should not break existing flows') it('should respond to health check') }); ``` ### 4️⃣ Design the Change ```markdown ## ADR Template (if changing patterns) # ADR-XXX: [Decision Title] ## Status Proposed | Accepted | Deprecated ## Context What problem are we solving? ## Decision What are we doing? ## Consequences What becomes easier/harder? ``` ### 5️⃣ Implement Incrementally (Flag-First) ```typescript // Always check feature flag first if (process.env.FEATURE_<NAME>_ENABLED === 'true') { // New implementation return newFeatureLogic(); } else { // Existing behavior return existingLogic(); } // Tracer bullet approach - vertical slice // 1. Route → 2. Controller → 3. Service → 4. Repository → 5. Database ``` ### 6️⃣ Integration & E2E ```bash # Add integration tests with test containers docker-compose -f docker-compose.test.yml up -d nx test <project> --testPathPattern=integration # Add E2E test behind flag FEATURE_<NAME>_ENABLED=true nx e2e <project>-e2e ``` ### ⚠️ Testing Pitfalls to Avoid #### Constructor Signature Changes ```typescript // ❌ Don't test with hard-coded constructor params const service = new Service({ logger, db, cache }); // ✅ Use dependency injection with mocks const mockLogger = createMockLogger(); const mockDb = createMockDb(); const service = new Service(mockLogger, mockDb); ``` #### Private Method Testing ```typescript // ❌ Don't test private methods directly (service as any).privateMethod(); // ✅ Test public behavior instead await expect(service.publicMethod()).toThrow('Validation error'); ``` #### Node.js Built-in Module Imports ```typescript // ❌ ES module syntax for Node.js built-ins import fs from 'fs'; // Fails in Jest // ✅ Namespace imports for Node.js built-ins import * as fs from 'fs'; ``` #### Mock Typing Issues ```typescript // ❌ Incorrect mock return types mockPage.innerText.mockResolvedValue('text'); // Type error // ✅ Proper type assertions mockPage.innerText.mockResolvedValue('text' as any); ``` ### 7️⃣ Local Affected Checks (Nx) ```bash # Run all affected checks in parallel nx affected:lint --parallel nx affected:test --parallel nx affected:build --parallel # If infrastructure changes nx run <infra-project>:synth cdk diff ``` ### 8️⃣ Open PR Early (Draft) ```markdown ## PR Template **Title:** feat(scope): short intent **Summary:** What & why in 2-3 sentences **Acceptance Criteria:** - [ ] AC-1: Specific outcome - [ ] AC-2: Another outcome **Changes:** - Endpoints: `/api/v1/new-endpoint` - Schema: Added `field_name` to table - Environment: `FEATURE_X_ENABLED` - Feature Flag: `feature_x_enabled` **Test Plan:** - Unit: 15 new tests added - Integration: 5 API tests added - E2E: 1 user journey test - Smoke: Health check verified **Migration/Infra:** - [ ] Run migration script - [ ] Update CDK stack - Rollback: `git revert` + flag OFF **Observability:** - Metrics: `feature_x_usage_count` - Logs: Search for `feature_x` - Dashboard: Link to dashboard **Risks/Mitigations:** - Risk: Performance impact - Mitigation: Added caching layer **Screenshots/GIFs:** [If UI changes] ``` ### 9️⃣ CI Gates ```yaml # CI must pass these gates jobs: quality-gates: steps: - Typecheck # TypeScript strict mode - Lint # ESLint rules pass - Unit Tests # 80% coverage - Integration # API contracts valid - Build # Artifacts created - E2E Preview # Tests against preview URL ``` ### 🔟 Review & Iterate ```bash # Address review comments # Keep commits clean git commit -m "feat(intake): address review feedback" # Re-run affected checks nx affected:test --base=origin/main ``` ### 1️⃣1️⃣ Staging Deploy (Flag OFF) ```bash # Deploy with flag OFF FEATURE_<NAME>_ENABLED=false npm run deploy:staging # Run post-deploy smoke npm run test:smoke:staging # Enable for internal testing FEATURE_<NAME>_ENABLED=true npm run test:e2e:staging # Monitor logs/metrics tail -f logs/staging.log | grep "feature_x" ``` ### 1️⃣2️⃣ Production Rollout ```typescript // Progressive flag ramp const rolloutSchedule = { day1: { percentage: 1, cohort: 'internal' }, day2: { percentage: 10, cohort: 'beta_users' }, day3: { percentage: 50, cohort: 'all_users' }, day4: { percentage: 100, cohort: 'all_users' } }; // Monitor KPIs const monitoring = { errorRate: '< 0.1%', latencyP95: '< 500ms', businessMetric: 'conversion_rate' }; ``` ### 1️⃣3️⃣ Finish & Cleanup ```bash # Update documentation npm run docs:generate # Update CHANGELOG echo "### Added - Feature X: Description" >> CHANGELOG.md # Remove temporary code git grep "TODO(feature_x)" | xargs -I {} sed -i '' 's/TODO(feature_x)//' {} # Close ticket gh issue close <issue-number> --comment "Feature shipped successfully" ``` --- ## 🐛 BUG FIX WORKFLOW - Order of Operations ### 1️⃣ Triage ```markdown ## Bug Report Template **Symptom:** What's broken? **Scope/Impact:** How many users affected? **First Bad Release:** v1.2.3 **Suspected Area:** Authentication module **Severity:** P0 | P1 | P2 | P3 ## For Sev-1/Hotfix - Skip normal queue - Write incident note - Follow hotfix fast path ``` ### 2️⃣ Reproduce & Add Failing Test ```typescript // FIRST: Write a test that fails describe('Bug #421', () => { it('should preserve caller ID on transfer', () => { // This test MUST fail before the fix const result = transferCall({ assertedId: '+1234567890' }); expect(result.callerId).toBe('+1234567890'); // Currently fails }); }); ``` ### 3️⃣ Branch ```bash git checkout -b fix/<scope>-<issue#> # Example: fix/telephony-421 ``` ### 4️⃣ Root Cause & Minimal Fix ```typescript // Prefer smallest change that addresses root cause // BAD: Refactor entire module // GOOD: Fix the specific line causing the issue // Before (buggy) const callerId = call.id; // Wrong field // After (fixed) const callerId = call.assertedId || call.id; // Correct field with fallback ``` ### 5️⃣ Run Affected Targets ```bash nx affected:test --base=origin/main nx affected:build --base=origin/main # If infrastructure changed nx run <infra-project>:synth cdk diff ``` ### 6️⃣ PR (Can be marked "hotfix") ```markdown ## Bug Fix PR Template **Root Cause:** Caller ID field was using wrong property **Before:** System used `call.id` instead of `call.assertedId` **After:** System correctly uses `call.assertedId` with fallback **How to Verify:** Run test case in PR description **Risk:** Low - isolated change with fallback **Rollback:** `git revert` this commit ``` ### 7️⃣ CI + Staging ```bash # Deploy to staging npm run deploy:staging # Run focused sanity tests npm run test:sanity --area=telephony # Run global smoke tests npm run test:smoke:staging ``` ### 8️⃣ Production ```bash # Deploy (with flag if added for safety) BUGFIX_421_ENABLED=true npm run deploy:production # Verify metrics curl https://metrics.example.com/api/telephony/errors # Post incident resolution echo "Incident resolved: Bug #421 fixed and deployed" >> incidents.log ``` --- ## 🚨 HOTFIX FAST PATH (Sev-1) ### Immediate Response ```bash # 1. Create hotfix branch from prod tag git checkout -b hotfix/<short-title> production-v1.2.3 # 2. Reproduce → Failing test → Minimal fix npm run test:reproduce-bug # 3. Fast CI lane (skip non-critical) nx run-many -t lint,test,build --projects=affected # 4. Deploy directly to prod npm run deploy:production:hotfix # 5. Post-deploy smoke npm run test:smoke:production # 6. Monitor for 15-30 minutes watch -n 5 'curl https://api.example.com/health' # 7. Back-merge to main git checkout main git merge hotfix/<short-title> # 8. Create postmortem gh issue create --title "Postmortem: <incident>" \ --body "Root cause, timeline, action items" ``` --- ## 🎛️ ROLLOUT & SAFETY PATTERNS ### Feature Flags ```typescript // Ship dark, test safely, instant rollback const featureFlag = { name: 'feature_x_enabled', defaultValue: false, rollout: { internal: true, beta: false, production: false } }; ``` ### Migration Strategy ```typescript // 1. Deploy forward-compatible code function readData() { return newSchema || oldSchema; // Works with both } // 2. Run migration await runMigration(); // 3. Flip to new path function readData() { return newSchema; // Only new } // 4. Remove old code // Delete oldSchema references ``` ### Canary/Blue-Green ```yaml deployment: strategy: canary stages: - weight: 5% # 5% traffic duration: 1h - weight: 25% # If metrics good duration: 2h - weight: 100% # Full rollout ``` ### Observability ```typescript // Add instrumentation const timer = metrics.startTimer('feature_x_duration'); try { logger.info('feature_x_started', { userId, timestamp }); const result = await featureXLogic(); metrics.increment('feature_x_success'); return result; } catch (error) { metrics.increment('feature_x_error'); logger.error('feature_x_failed', { error, userId }); throw error; } finally { timer.end(); } ``` ### Kill Switch ```typescript // Emergency bypass if (process.env.KILL_FEATURE_X === 'true') { return legacyImplementation(); } ``` --- ## ✅ COMMIT HYGIENE (Conventional Commits) ```bash # Features feat(intake): de-duplicate leads on create feat(api): add webhook retry mechanism # Fixes fix(telephony): preserve asserted caller id on transfer fix(auth): handle expired tokens gracefully # Other types refactor(crm): extract lead normalizer test(api): add regression for empty policy_id docs(readme): update deployment instructions perf(query): optimize contact search chore(deps): update nx to v20 ``` --- ## 🛠️ MINIMAL COMMAND SET (Nx-Friendly) ```bash # Branch management git checkout -b feat/<scope>-<title> git checkout -b fix/<scope>-<issue#> # Code generation nx g @nx/js:lib <lib-name> nx g @nx/node:application <app-name> nx g @nx/react:component <component-name> # Development loop nx affected:lint --parallel nx affected:test --parallel nx affected:build --parallel # E2E testing nx run <app>-e2e:e2e nx run <app>-e2e:e2e --watch # Infrastructure (CDK) nx run <infra-project>:synth nx run <infra-project>:deploy --require-approval never nx run <infra-project>:destroy --force # Full pipeline simulation nx run-many -t lint,test,build,e2e --parallel # Deploy commands (handled by CI, but available locally) npm run deploy:preview # PR preview npm run deploy:staging # Staging environment npm run deploy:production # Production (requires auth) ``` --- ## 📋 TINY CHECKLISTS ### Feature DoR (Definition of Ready) ```markdown - ===FILE:.cursor/rules/04-testing/bridge-communication-testing.mdc===--- description: When working with Cursor-Flow communication always implement these testing standards alwaysApply: false --- # Bridge Communication Testing Standards Ensure robust testing of browser-to-platform communication bridges to prevent event handling failures. **Justification:** The "Open Editor" issue revealed that bridge functions can be silently overridden, causing events to be logged but never handled. This rule prevents such issues through comprehensive testing. ## 🎯 Single Responsibility This rule ONLY covers testing of bridge communication patterns between browser scripts and platform handlers. Not general testing (see comprehensive-testing-strategy) or UI testing (see playwright-automation-standards). ## 📋 Implementation Checklist ### Bridge Testing Requirements ```markdown - [ ] Verify bridge function exists before use - [ ] Test bridge function signature matches expectations - [ ] Ensure bridge is not overridden by subsequent scripts - [ ] Validate event routing to correct handlers - [ ] Test fallback mechanisms when bridge unavailable - [ ] Verify timing of bridge setup vs script injection - [ ] Monitor bridge events in development mode - [ ] Create automated tests for bridge communication ``` ## 🔍 Common Bridge Issues & Prevention ### Issue 1: Bridge Override **Problem:** Scripts override the platform's bridge with their own implementation ```javascript // ❌ BAD: Unconditional override window.__bridgeFunction = function(event) { console.log(event); // Just logs, never handles! }; // ✅ GOOD: Guarded implementation if (typeof window.__bridgeFunction !== 'function') { window.__bridgeFunction = function(event, payload) { // Fallback implementation }; } ``` ### Issue 2: Signature Mismatch **Problem:** Bridge function called with wrong number/type of arguments ```javascript // ❌ BAD: Inconsistent signatures // Platform expects: (event, payload) // Script calls: (combinedData) // ✅ GOOD: Consistent two-parameter signature bridge('eventName', { data: 'payload' }); ``` ### Issue 3: Timing Issues **Problem:** Bridge accessed before it's initialized ```javascript // ❌ BAD: Immediate use without checking window.__bridge('event', data); // May not exist yet! // ✅ GOOD: Defensive checking if (typeof window.__bridge === 'function') { window.__bridge('event', data); } else { console.warn('Bridge not ready, queueing event'); // Queue or retry logic } ``` ## 🧪 Required Bridge Tests ### 1. Existence Test ```javascript describe('Bridge Communication', () => { it('should expose bridge function to page context', async () => { await page.exposeFunction('__bridge', handler); const exists = await page.evaluate(() => { return typeof window.__bridge === 'function'; }); expect(exists).toBe(true); }); }); ``` ### 2. Non-Override Test ```javascript it('should not override existing bridge', async () => { // Setup bridge await page.exposeFunction('__bridge', originalHandler); // Inject script that tries to override await page.evaluate(() => { if (typeof window.__bridge !== 'function') { window.__bridge = () => console.log('override'); } }); // Verify original still works await page.evaluate(() => window.__bridge('test', {})); expect(originalHandler).toHaveBeenCalledWith('test', {}); }); ``` ### 3. Event Routing Test ```javascript it('should route events to correct handlers', async () => { const handlers = { openEditor: jest.fn(), saveFlow: jest.fn() }; await page.exposeFunction('__bridge', (event, payload) => { handlers[event]?.(payload); }); await page.evaluate(() => { window.__bridge('openEditor', { source: 'test' }); }); expect(handlers.openEditor).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ source: 'test' }); }); ``` ### 4. Timing Test ```javascript it('should handle bridge setup timing correctly', async () => { // Inject script first (before bridge) await page.addScriptTag({ content: scriptWithBridgeCheck }); // Then setup bridge await page.exposeFunction('__bridge', handler); // Verify script can now use bridge const result = await page.evaluate(() => { return window.__tryBridge?.('test'); }); expect(result).toBe('success'); }); ``` ## 🔧 Debug Tooling ### Bridge Monitor Create a development-only bridge monitor: ```javascript class BridgeMonitor { constructor() { this.events = []; this.errors = []; } wrap(originalBridge) { return (event, payload) => { const timestamp = Date.now(); console.log(`[Bridge] ${event} at ${new Date().toISOString()}`); try { const result = originalBridge(event, payload); this.events.push({ event, payload, timestamp, success: true }); return result; } catch (error) { this.errors.push({ event, payload, timestamp, error }); console.error('[Bridge] Error:', error); throw error; } }; } getStats() { return { totalEvents: this.events.length, errors: this.errors.length, averageTime: this.calculateAverage() }; } } ``` ### Runtime Assertions Add runtime checks in development: ```javascript if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development') { // Verify bridge setup await page.evaluate(() => { const checks = { exists: typeof window.__bridge === 'function', correctSignature: window.__bridge?.length === 2, notOverridden: window.__bridge?.toString().includes('exposeFunction') }; console.table(checks); if (!checks.exists) { console.error('❌ Bridge not found!'); } if (!checks.correctSignature) { console.error('❌ Bridge has wrong signature!'); } if (!checks.notOverridden) { console.warn('⚠️ Bridge may have been overridden'); } }); } ``` ## 📊 Testing Checklist ### Before Every Release ```markdown - [ ] Run bridge communication test suite - [ ] Verify no bridge override warnings in console - [ ] Check bridge event logs for dropped events - [ ] Test with scripts loaded in different orders - [ ] Verify fallback mechanisms work - [ ] Test in multiple browsers - [ ] Check for timing race conditions ``` ### For New Features ```markdown - [ ] Add bridge tests for new events - [ ] Document expected bridge behavior - [ ] Test error handling for bridge failures - [ ] Verify no conflicts with existing bridges - [ ] Add monitoring for new event types ``` ## 🚨 Anti-Patterns to Avoid ```javascript // ❌ Silent failures window.bridge = () => {}; // No-op override // ❌ Assuming bridge exists bridge('event'); // No existence check // ❌ Inconsistent signatures bridge(combinedObject); // vs bridge(event, payload) // ❌ No error handling window.bridge('event', data); // What if it throws? // ❌ No timing consideration // Script runs before bridge is ready ``` ## ✅ Best Practices ```javascript // ✅ Defensive bridge usage function safeBridge(event, payload) { if (typeof window.__bridge === 'function') { try { return window.__bridge(event, payload); } catch (error) { console.error('Bridge error:', error); // Fallback logic } } else { console.warn('Bridge not available'); // Queue or retry } } // ✅ Bridge setup verification async function setupBridge() { // 1. Expose function await page.exposeFunction('__bridge', handler); // 2. Verify it exists const exists = await page.evaluate(() => typeof window.__bridge === 'function' ); if (!exists) { throw new Error('Bridge setup failed'); } // 3. Log confirmation console.log('✅ Bridge ready'); } // ✅ Guarded script injection const overlayScript = ` // Don't override if already exists if (typeof window.__bridge !== 'function') { // Fallback implementation window.__bridge = async (event, payload) => { // HTTP fallback await fetch('/bridge', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ event, payload }) }); }; } `; ``` ## 📈 Success Metrics - **Zero Bridge Failures**: No dropped events due to bridge issues - **100% Event Delivery**: All events reach their handlers - **Override Prevention**: No scripts override platform bridges - **Timing Resilience**: No race conditions in bridge setup - **Clear Error Messages**: Failures clearly indicate bridge issues ## 🔗 Related Rules - [comprehensive-testing-strategy](./comprehensive-testing-strategy.mdc) - [playwright-automation-standards](./playwright/playwright-automation-standards.mdc) - [browser-injection-standards](../15-web-automation/browser-injection-standards.mdc) - [error-handling](../01-code-standards/error-handling.mdc)# Bridge Communication Testing Standards
===FILE:.cursor/rules/04-testing/comprehensive-testing-strategy.mdc===--- description: Comprehensive testing strategy combining unit, integration, and E2E testing with coverage requirements and best practices alwaysApply: false --- # Comprehensive Testing Strategy - 2025 Complete testing pyramid implementation with Vitest/Jest for unit tests, integration tests with mocked dependencies, and Playwright for E2E testing. **Justification:** Multi-layered testing prevents regressions, ensures reliability, validates business logic, and maintains confidence in production deployments. ## 🎯 Single Responsibility This rule defines testing standards, patterns, and coverage requirements. It does NOT cover CI/CD integration (see ci-pipeline) or deployment validation (see deployment-stages). ## 📋 Master Testing Checklist ### Project Setup ```markdown - [ ] Choose test framework (Vitest factories - [ ] Configure mocking strategies - [ ] Set up E2E test infrastructure - [ ] Configure mutation testing (Stryker) - [ ] Set up visual regression testing - [ ] Configure performance testing ``` ## 🏗️ Test Structure & Organization ### Directory Structure ``` src/ __tests__/ # Unit tests (alongside source) utils.spec.ts helpers.spec.ts __it__/ # Integration tests api.integration.spec.ts thresholds: { lines: 80, functions: 80, branches: 75, statements: 80, perFile: true, }, }, testTimeout: 10000, hookTimeout: 10000, mockReset: true, restoreMocks: true, }, resolve: { alias: { '@': 70% critical-paths: # Higher for critical code lines: 95% functions: 95% branches: 90% statements: 95% ``` ### Coverage Reporting ```bash # Generate coverage report pnpm test:coverage # Generate
