===FILE:.foundry/skills/adr-writer/SKILL.md===# ADR Writer Create Architecture Decision Records that capture the reasoning behind structural decisions. ## ADR Template ```markdown # ADR-[NNN]: [Short Decision Title] ## Status [proposed | accepted | deprecated | superseded by ADR-NNN] ## Date [ISO 8601 date] ## Context [What is the issue or situation that motivates this decision? Include relevant constraints, requirements, and forces at play. Reference specific files, schemas, or prior ADRs that inform this context.] ## Options Considered ### Option A: [Name] **Description**: [How this approach works] **Pros**: - [advantage 1] - [advantage 2] **Cons**: - [disadvantage 1] - [disadvantage 2] ### Option B: [Name] **Description**: [How this approach works] **Pros**: - [advantage 1] - [advantage 2] **Cons**: - [disadvantage 1] - [disadvantage 2] ## Decision [What is the change we're proposing or the decision we've made? Why did we choose this option over the others? Reference specific tradeoffs.] ## Consequences ### Positive - [What becomes easier or better] ### Negative - [What becomes harder or worse] ### Risks - [What could go wrong and how we mitigate it] ## References - [File paths, schema references, prior ADRs, external resources] ``` ## Naming Convention - Store ADRs in the project's `docs/adr/` directory - Name files: `adr-NNN-short-kebab-title.md` (e.g., `adr-001-use-event-driven-messaging.md`) - Number sequentially within the project ## Quality Checklist - [ ] Context explains WHY, not just WHAT - [ ] At least two options are considered - [ ] Pros and cons are specific, not generic - [ ] Decision rationale references the tradeoffs - [ ] Consequences include both positive and negative - [ ] All file references use actual paths that exist - [ ] Status is set correctly (usually `proposed` for new ADRs)
===FILE:.foundry/skills/c4-diagram-generator/SKILL.md===# C4 Diagram Generator Generate C4 architecture diagrams using Mermaid syntax. Reference diagrams are in the project's `docs/diagrams/` directory. ## C4 Level 1 — System Context Shows the system and its relationships to users and external systems. ```mermaid C4Context title System Context: [System Name] Person(userAlias, "User Role", "Description of user") System(systemAlias, "System Name", "What it does") System_Ext(extAlias, "External System", "What it does") Rel(userAlias, systemAlias, "Uses", "HTTPS") Rel(systemAlias, extAlias, "Calls", "REST/JSON") UpdateLayoutConfig($c4ShapeInRow="3", $c4BoundaryInRow="1") ``` **Required annotations:** - Every `Person` entry = a real human stakeholder - Every `System_Ext` = an external dependency (3rd party, platform API) - `Rel` labels must include protocol where known --- ## C4 Level 2 — Container Diagram Shows the major runtime units inside the system boundary. ```mermaid C4Container title Container: [System Name] Person(userAlias, "User Role", "") System_Boundary(sysBoundary, "System Name") { Container(app, "App Name", "Technology", "What it does") Container(worker, "Background Worker", "Service Worker", "What it does") ContainerDb(store, "Storage", "chrome.storage / IndexedDB", "Persisted state") } System_Ext(extAlias, "External API", "") Rel(userAlias, app, "Uses", "UI interaction") Rel(app, worker, "Sends messages", "chrome.runtime") Rel(worker, store, "Reads/writes", "") Rel(worker, extAlias, "Calls", "HTTPS/REST") ``` **Required annotations:** - Technology stack in each container - Communication protocols on every `Rel` - Storage type and what data category (public/internal/sensitive/regulated) --- ## C4 Level 3 — Component Diagram Shows modules within a single container. ```mermaid C4Component title Components: [Container Name] Container_Boundary(containerBoundary, "Container Name") { Component(comp1, "Component 1", "Module", "Responsibility") Component(comp2, "Component 2", "Module", "Responsibility") Component(comp3, "Component 3", "Module", "Responsibility") } Rel(comp1, comp2, "Calls", "") Rel(comp2, comp3, "Emits events to", "") ``` --- ## C4 Level 4 — Dynamic / Sequence Diagram Shows execution flow for a specific scenario. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Human participant Orchestrator participant Builder participant Verifier Human->>Orchestrator: Describes intent Orchestrator->>Builder: Work order (bounded scope) Builder->>Builder: Implements changes Builder->>Orchestrator: Reports completion Orchestrator->>Verifier: Validate independently Verifier->>Orchestrator: PASS / FAIL with evidence Orchestrator->>Human: Phase complete / blockers ``` --- ## Trust Boundary Annotations Add trust boundary overlays to container and context diagrams: ```mermaid C4Container title Container with Trust Boundaries Boundary(b1, "Browser Sandbox (Extension Origin)") { Container(popup, "Popup UI", "React/MV3", "") Container(sidepanel, "Side Panel", "React/MV3", "") } Boundary(b2, "Service Worker Context") { Container(sw, "Service Worker", "MV3", "") } Boundary(b3, "External Network") { System_Ext(api, "Platform API", "") } Rel(popup, sw, "Messages", "chrome.runtime — validated") Rel(sw, api, "Fetches", "HTTPS — auth required") ``` **Trust boundary rules:** - Every cross-boundary `Rel` must label auth/validation mechanism - Boundaries must align with Chrome extension privilege scopes where applicable --- ## Diagram Storage Save diagrams to: `docs/diagrams/[system]-[level]-[date].mmd` --- ## Output Section for Intent Packet When producing diagrams as part of `define-intent`, format output as: ```markdown ## Architecture Diagrams ### System Context (C4 L1) \`\`\`mermaid [diagram here] \`\`\` **Saved**: `docs/diagrams/[system]-context-[date].mmd` ### Container Diagram (C4 L2) \`\`\`mermaid [diagram here] \`\`\` **Saved**: `docs/diagrams/[system]-containers-[date].mmd` ```
===FILE:.foundry/skills/continuity-writer/SKILL.md===# Continuity Writer Update `.foundry/projects/<project>/current-task.json` (**ADR-011**; legacy fallback: `.codex/projects/<project>/current-task.json`) to maintain deterministic resumability. ## When to Update - Phase transition (entering or completing a phase) - Branch switch (new feature branch, merge to base) - Verification completion (test results change state) - Blocker discovered or resolved - Work interrupted (generate handoff before stopping) ## Update Protocol ### Step 1: Read Current State ```bash cat .foundry/projects/<project>/current-task.json ``` ### Step 2: Determine Changes Compare current state against what just happened: - Did the phase status change? (`pending` → `in_progress` → `verified` → `done`) - Did the active branch change? - Did verification commands change? - Were new artifacts produced? - Were blockers added or resolved? - Were done criteria satisfied? ### Step 3: Apply Updates Update only the fields that changed. Preserve all other fields exactly. **Fields to update:** | Field | When to Update | |---|---| | `currentPhase.status` | Phase status changed | | `currentPhase.updatedAt` | Any phase update (use ISO 8601) | | `currentPhase.notes` | Add notes about what happened | | `activeBranch` | Branch switched | | `nextCommit.branch` | Next commit target changed | | `nextCommit.message` | Next expected commit message | | `nextCommandSet` | Verification commands changed | | `blockedBy` | Blockers added or resolved | | `artifacts` | New artifacts produced | | `doneCriteria` | Criteria added, modified, or satisfied | | `lifecycleStage` | 11-phase enum value (when using Flagship schema) | ### Step 4: Validate the Continuity Invariant > An AI system must be able to determine from committed artifacts alone: current phase, active branch, next verification commands, blocked conditions, and done criteria. If any of these cannot be determined from the updated state, the update is incomplete. ## Flagship Schema Fields (for enhanced continuity) When using the Flagship `continuity-state.schema.json`, also update: - `lifecycleStage`: The 11-phase enum value - `phaseSequence`: Integer sequence number - `graphRevision`: Version of the graph state - `nextWorkOrders`: Array of pending work order references - `verificationPlan`: Array of verification commands - `artifactAuthorities`: Map of artifact type to authority/owner - `evidenceBundles`: Array of evidence bundle paths - `impactedSystems`: Array of affected system IDs ## Commit Convention When committing continuity updates: ``` chore(codex): update <project> task state — <phase> <status> ```
===FILE:.foundry/skills/define-intent/reference/feature-intake-runbook.md===# Feature Intake Reference Source: flagship-foundry-work/runbooks/feature-intake.md ## Purpose Turn intended capability into typed work orders without skipping contracts, risks, or acceptance criteria. ## Steps 1. **Restate outcome** — One sentence: what changes for the user or system when this ships? 2. **Enumerate impacted systems and contracts** — Which systems, components, schemas, and APIs are touched? What contracts change? 3. **Attach principle cards and guardrail packs** — Which principles apply? Which guardrail packs constrain the work? 4. **Define acceptance criteria and rollback** — What must be true for this to be considered done? How do we undo it? 5. **Create ecosystem and system planning work orders** — High-level decomposition with explicit agent roles and bounded scope 6. **Decompose into repo and verifier work orders** — File-scoped implementation tasks plus independent verification tasks 7. **Publish handoff envelope** — Continuity state, evidence references, open questions ## Gate: Definition of Ready Before proceeding to plan/implement, confirm: - [ ] Outcome stated in one sentence - [ ] Impacted systems and contracts enumerated - [ ] Principle cards and guardrail packs identified - [ ] Acceptance criteria defined and testable - [ ] Rollback plan documented - [ ] Test outline present
===FILE:.foundry/skills/define-intent/SKILL.md===# Define Intent — Interactive Pipeline Transform a vague idea into a fully-defined intent packet ready for the plan and implement phases. ## When to Invoke - User has a new feature idea or capability request - User wants to define scope for a major change - User says "I want to build X" or "what if we added Y" - Resuming discovery work from interrupted session ## Output: Intent Packet At the end of this pipeline, produce a single markdown document containing all sections below. Save to `docs/intent/intent-[slug]-[date].md`. --- ## Stage 1: Discover — Problem Statement Ask the user to answer (or draft answers yourself from context): 1. **Problem**: What problem or gap exists today? Who experiences it? 2. **User/Stakeholder**: Who is this for? (end user, developer, operations, compliance) 3. **Outcome**: What does success look like in one sentence? 4. **Constraints**: What must NOT change? What boundaries must be respected? 5. **Risks**: What could go wrong? What is the blast radius if this fails? **Output section**: ```markdown ## Problem Statement - **Problem**: ... - **Stakeholder**: ... - **Success Outcome**: ... - **Constraints**: ... - **Known Risks**: ... ``` --- ## Stage 2: Define — Scope and Acceptance Criteria Based on the problem statement, define: 1. **In scope**: What will be built or changed? 2. **Out of scope / Non-goals**: What will NOT be done in this slice? 3. **Glossary**: 5-15 key terms that must be used consistently 4. **Acceptance criteria**: 3-10 testable statements in format "Given X, when Y, then Z" 5. **Rollback plan**: How to undo this if it causes issues **Output section**: ```markdown ## Scope - **In Scope**: ... - **Non-Goals**: ... ## Glossary | Term | Definition | |------|-----------| | ... | ... | ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] Given [context], when [action], then [outcome] - [ ] ... ## Rollback Plan ... ``` --- ## Stage 3: Visualize — C4 Diagrams Use the `c4-diagram-generator` skill to produce: 1. **System Context Diagram** (C4 Level 1): What is the system, who uses it, what external systems does it interact with? 2. **Container Diagram** (C4 Level 2): What are the major runtime units (apps, services, databases, extensions)? For each diagram, annotate: - Trust boundaries (what crosses a security boundary?) - Data flow direction - External dependencies Reference existing diagrams in `docs/diagrams/`. **Output section**: ```markdown ## System Context Diagram \`\`\`mermaid C4Context title System Context: [System Name] Person(user, "User", "Description") System(system, "System Name", "Description") ... \`\`\` ## Container Diagram \`\`\`mermaid C4Container title Container Diagram: [System Name] ... \`\`\` ``` --- ## Stage 4: Architect — Principles and Guardrails Apply applicable principles and guardrail packs from the Flagship Foundry catalogs. ### Principles to Check Reference `flagship-foundry-work/ontology/principle-catalog.json`. For each principle, determine if it applies: - `principle:complexity-budgets` — Does this change increase data model complexity? - `principle:contract-first` — Are we defining interfaces before implementation? - `principle:observed-vs-declared-truth` — Are we distinguishing runtime observations from declared state? **Output section**: ```markdown ## Applicable Principles | Principle | Applies | How | |-----------|---------|-----| | complexity-budgets | yes/no | [explanation] | | contract-first | yes/no | [explanation] | | observed-vs-declared-truth | yes/no | [explanation] | ``` ### Guardrail Packs to Attach Reference `flagship-foundry-work/guardrails/`. Select applicable packs: - `guardrail:typescript-core` — always for TypeScript changes - `guardrail:chrome-extension-mv3` — for Chrome extension changes - `guardrail:web-frontend` — for UI/React changes - `guardrail:aws-serverless` — for cloud/serverless changes **Output section**: ```markdown ## Guardrail Packs - [ ] guardrail:typescript-core — [required checks from pack] - [ ] guardrail:chrome-extension-mv3 — [required checks from pack] ``` --- ## Stage 5: Handoff to Plan Phase Once all stages are complete, produce the final summary: ```markdown ## Intent Packet Summary - **Phase**: ready for `plan` - **Primary Agent**: @orchestrator - **Next Action**: invoke `scope-chunker` to decompose into work orders - **Key Decisions Pending**: [list any open architectural questions] - **Definition of Ready Met**: yes / no (if no, list what's missing) ``` Invoke `scope-chunker` with the complete intent packet as input.
===FILE:.foundry/skills/evidence-collector/SKILL.md===# Evidence Collector Gather and structure verification evidence for phase gates and release decisions. ## Evidence Bundle Structure ```markdown # Evidence Bundle: [phase-id] ## Metadata - Phase: [lifecycle stage] - Project: [project name] - Branch: [active branch] - Collected: [ISO 8601 timestamp] - Collector: evidence-collector ## Test Evidence | Suite | Pass | Fail | Skip | Coverage | Path | |-------|------|------|------|----------|------| | [suite name] | [n] | [n] | [n] | [%] | [path to results] | ## Build Evidence | Target | Status | Size | Output Path | |--------|--------|------|-------------| | [target] | PASS/FAIL | [KB] | [path] | ## Code Quality Evidence | Check | Status | Details | |-------|--------|---------| | TypeCheck | PASS/FAIL | [error count] | | Lint | PASS/FAIL | [warning count] | | Security | PASS/FAIL | [finding count] | ## Artifact Inventory | Artifact Type | Path | Status | |---------------|------|--------| | [type] | [path] | exists/missing | ## Acceptance Criteria Evidence | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence | |-----------|---------|----------| | [criterion text] | PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN | [reference to evidence above] | ## Gaps - [evidence that should exist but doesn't] ``` ## Collection Protocol 1. Run verification commands from `nextCommandSet` in continuity state 2. Capture test results: look for Jest/Vitest output, coverage reports 3. Capture build results: sizes, output paths, exit codes 4. Scan for type errors: TypeScript diagnostics 5. Check artifact existence: verify all declared artifacts exist at their paths 6. Map evidence to acceptance criteria from `doneCriteria` 7. Identify gaps: evidence expected but not found ## Evidence Locations Common places to find evidence: - `coverage/` — Test coverage reports - `dist/` — Build outputs - `test-results/` — Test result files - `.nx/cache/` — Nx computation cache (contains prior run results) - Project `docs/` — Documentation artifacts
===FILE:.foundry/skills/handoff-generator/SKILL.md===# Handoff Generator Generate standardized handoff documents that enable any agent — or a new session after context collapse — to resume work with full context. ## When to Generate - Phase completion (work is done, next phase starts) - Work interruption (session ending, context limit approaching) - Agent delegation (handing work from one agent to another) - Plan completion (plan approved, implementation about to begin) ## Generation Protocol ### Step 1: Read Current State - Read `.foundry/projects/<project>/current-task.json` (legacy: `.codex/projects/<project>/current-task.json`) - Read recent git log: `git log --oneline -10` - Read any open work orders or pending tasks ### Step 2: Collect Evidence References For each claim or decision made during the work: - What was the claim? - What evidence supports it? - Where is the evidence located (file path)? ### Step 3: Identify Supporting Files List every file that a resuming agent would need to read to have full context: - Continuity state file - Charter and rules files - Source files that were modified - Test files that validate the changes - Schema files that constrain the work ### Step 4: Fill Template Use the template at `.foundry/skills/handoff-generator/templates/PLAN_HANDOFF_TEMPLATE.md` ### Step 5: Save Save the handoff document to the project's `docs/` directory: ``` docs/handoffs/handoff-[phase-id]-[date].md ``` ## Quality Checklist - [ ] Summary is 1-3 sentences, not a wall of text - [ ] Every evidence reference has a real file path - [ ] Continuity state snapshot matches actual `current-task.json` - [ ] Supporting files list includes only files that actually exist - [ ] Open questions are actionable, not vague - [ ] Rollback notes describe a concrete reversal path - [ ] Next steps are specific and ordered
===FILE:.foundry/skills/handoff-generator/templates/PLAN_HANDOFF_TEMPLATE.md===# Plan Handoff: [Plan Title] ## Generated - **Date**: [ISO 8601 timestamp] - **Agent**: [agent that generated this handoff] - **Lifecycle Stage**: [current stage from 11-phase lifecycle] - **Phase ID**: [phase ID from continuity state] ## Summary [1-3 sentences: what was attempted, what changed, what is the current state] ## Evidence References | Claim | Evidence | Path | |-------|----------|------| | [acceptance criterion or decision] | [test result, build output, code review] | [file path] | | [acceptance criterion or decision] | [test result, build output, code review] | [file path] | ## Continuity State Snapshot - **Active Branch**: [git branch name] - **Current Phase**: [phase id] / [status: pending|in_progress|blocked|verified|done] - **Next Commit**: [branch] — [message] - **Next Command Set**: ```bash [verification command 1] [verification command 2] ``` - **Blocked By**: [blockers or "none"] - **Done Criteria**: - [ ] [criterion 1] - [ ] [criterion 2] ## Supporting Files for Context Recovery Load these files to reconstruct full context: - [ ] [path] — [why this file matters for resumption] - [ ] [path] — [why this file matters for resumption] - [ ] [path] — [why this file matters for resumption] ## Open Questions and Blockers - [question or blocker with enough context to act on it] ## Rollback Notes [How to undo the work done in this phase if needed. Include specific commands or branch references.] ## Next Steps 1. [specific next action] 2. [specific next action] 3. [specific next action]
===FILE:.foundry/skills/model-router/SKILL.md===# Model Router Route work to the correct model tier based on task class. Provider configuration lives in `flagship-foundry-work/configs/`. ## Task Class to Model Tier Routing | Task Class | Model Tier | Use Local? | Rationale | |-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------| | `strategic_reasoning` | frontier_reasoner | NO | High ambiguity, architectural decisions — needs best model | | `constraint_interpretation` | frontier_reasoner | NO | Nuanced interpretation of rules and requirements | | `verification` | balanced_reasoner | conditional | Needs good reasoning but not the most expensive | | `diagnostics` | balanced_reasoner | conditional | Root cause analysis requires good reasoning | | `learning` | balanced_reasoner | conditional | Pattern extraction from evidence | | `deterministic_transformation` | low_cost_executor | YES | Bounded code generation with clear spec — local models excel | | `structured_generation` | low_cost_executor | YES | Schema/config/template generation — predictable structure | ## Provider Registry ### Frontier Reasoner (Cloud — Required for strategic work) | Provider | Model IDs | Notes | |----------|-----------|-------| | Anthropic (Claude Code) | `claude-opus-4-6`, `claude-sonnet-4-6` | Default for orchestrator, systems-architect | | OpenAI (Codex) | `o3`, `gpt-4o` | Available via Codex provider swap | ### Balanced Reasoner (Remote — Verification and diagnostics) | Provider | Model IDs | Notes | |----------|-----------|-------| | Anthropic | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | Default for verifier, docs-release-agent | | OpenAI compatible remote | Any hosted instruct model | Via `provider:openai-compatible-remote` | ### Low Cost Executor (Local — Bounded implementation) | Provider | Model IDs | Notes | |----------|-----------|-------| | Ollama local | `llama3.2`, `qwen2.5-coder`, `codellama` | See local setup below | | Ollama remote | Any OpenLlama-compatible model | External network host | | vLLM remote | Any vLLM hosted model | See provider config reference files | --- ## Local LLM Setup — Ollama on External Network ### 1. Verify Ollama endpoint is reachable ```bash curl http://<REMOTE_HOST>:11434/v1/models # Should return a list of available models ``` ### 2. Configure Claude Code to use local models In Claude Code, configure custom API endpoints via environment variables. For Ollama (OpenAI-compatible): ```bash # Set the base URL for the local Ollama endpoint export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://<REMOTE_HOST>:11434/v1 ``` Claude Code also supports custom providers via `.mcp.json`. Add the Ollama provider as an MCP tool server that wraps the local endpoint. ### 3. Configure Cursor to use local models In Cursor Settings → Models → Add Custom Model: - **Model Name**: `ollama/<model-name>` (e.g., `ollama/qwen2.5-coder:7b`) - **Base URL**: `http://<REMOTE_HOST>:11434/v1` - **API Key**: `ollama` (placeholder — Ollama doesn't require auth by default) Or via `.cursor/mcp.json` pointing at the Ollama MCP server. ### 4. Configure Codex to use local models Codex supports provider swap. In `~/.codex/config.toml`: ```toml [provider] name = "openai-compatible" base_url = "http://<REMOTE_HOST>:11434/v1" api_key = "ollama" model = "qwen2.5-coder:7b" ``` Or at runtime: `codex --provider ollama --model qwen2.5-coder` ### 5. Recommended Models by Task | Task | Recommended Local Model | |------|------------------------| | Code generation (TS/JS) | `qwen2.5-coder:7b` or `deepseek-coder-v2` | | Config/schema generation | `llama3.2:3b` (fast, structured output) | | Documentation generation | `llama3.1:8b` | | General small tasks | `llama3.2:1b` (fastest) | ### 6. Routing Rule for Agents When a work order has `taskClass: deterministic_transformation` or `taskClass: structured_generation` AND the work is clearly bounded with explicit file scope and contracts: - Prefer local model tier - Use `provider:ollama-local` or `provider:openai-compatible-remote` - If local model fails or produces invalid output, escalate to `balanced_reasoner` When a work order has `taskClass: strategic_reasoning` or `taskClass: constraint_interpretation`: - **Always use frontier_reasoner** (Claude Opus / GPT-4o) - Local models are not suitable for ambiguous architectural decisions --- ## Provider Config Reference Files - `flagship-foundry-work/configs/provider-manifests/` — all registered providers - `flagship-foundry-work/configs/model-routing/default.json` — task class routing rules - `flagship-foundry-work/configs/provider-manifests/local-ollama.json` — Ollama local config - `flagship-foundry-work/configs/provider-manifests/vllm-remote.json` — vLLM remote config
===FILE:.foundry/skills/nx-verification/SKILL.md===# Nx Verification Run Nx verification pipelines and produce structured results. ## Standard Verification Pipeline ### 1. TypeScript Type Checking ```bash npx nx typecheck <project> ``` Expected: Exit code 0, no type errors. ### 2. Unit Tests ```bash npx nx test <project> ``` Expected: All tests pass, coverage meets threshold. ### 3. Build ```bash npx nx build <project> --configuration=production ``` Expected: Exit code 0, no build errors, output in `dist/`. ### 4. E2E Tests (when available) ```bash npx nx e2e <project>-e2e ``` Expected: All E2E scenarios pass. ## Affected Pipeline When changes span multiple projects, use affected: ```bash npx nx affected -t typecheck test build ``` ## Chrome Extension Specific For Chrome extension projects, add: ```bash npx nx validate-dist <project> ``` Validates the built extension manifest, file sizes, and CSP compliance. ## Result Format Produce a verification report: ```markdown ## Verification Results: <project> - **TypeCheck**: PASS/FAIL [details] - **Tests**: PASS/FAIL [X passed, Y failed, Z skipped] - **Build**: PASS/FAIL [output size: X KB] - **E2E**: PASS/FAIL/SKIPPED [details] - **Overall**: PASS/FAIL - **Timestamp**: [ISO 8601] - **Branch**: [current branch] - **Commands Run**: [list of commands executed] ``` ## Error Handling - If a command fails, capture the full error output - Do not retry automatically — report the failure - If a project target doesn't exist (e.g., no `e2e` target), report as SKIPPED, not FAIL - If `node_modules` is missing, run `npm install` first, then retry
===FILE:.foundry/skills/scope-chunker/reference/work-order-quick-ref.md===# Work Order Quick Reference Source: flagship-foundry-work/schemas/agent-work-order.schema.json ## Required Fields | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | workOrderId | string | Unique identifier | | lifecycleStage | enum | discover/define/visualize/architect/plan/implement/verify/release/operate/diagnose/improve | | phaseId | string | kebab-case slug | | systemId | string | Which system this targets | | taskClass | enum | strategic_reasoning/constraint_interpretation/deterministic_transformation/structured_generation/verification/diagnostics/learning | | agentRole | enum | systems_architect/builder/verifier/security_reviewer/performance_reviewer/etc. | | agentPersona | enum | curious_architect/conservative_builder/skeptical_verifier/paranoid_security/performance_hunter/sync_editor/incident_commander | | modelTier | enum | frontier_reasoner/balanced_reasoner/low_cost_executor/deterministic_rule_engine | | sourceArtifacts | string[] | Input files/docs | | allowedTools | string[] | Tools the agent may use | | constraints | string[] | Rules and limits | | expectedOutputs | string[] | What the agent produces | | acceptanceCriteria | string[] | How to verify success | | verificationPlan | string[] | Commands to run | | approvalRequirements | string[] | What needs human sign-off | | status | enum | pending/ready/in_progress/blocked/awaiting_approval/verified/failed/done | ## Model Tier Routing | Tier | Providers | Use For | |------|-----------|---------| | frontier_reasoner | Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini cloud | strategic_reasoning, constraint_interpretation | | balanced_reasoner | compatible-remote, OpenAI | verification, diagnostics, learning | | low_cost_executor | Ollama local, compatible-remote | deterministic_transformation, structured_generation | | deterministic_rule_engine | local function | schema validation, policy checks |
===FILE:.foundry/skills/scope-chunker/SKILL.md===# Scope Chunker — Intent to Work Order Tree Decompose a defined intent packet into executable, bounded work orders with explicit agent assignments, file scope, and verification plans. ## Prerequisites - Intent packet from `define-intent` must be complete (DoR met) - Acceptance criteria defined and testable - System context and container diagrams exist - Applicable principles and guardrail packs identified ## Decomposition Protocol ### Step 1: Extract Glossary and Domain Map From the intent packet, extract: - Key terms and their definitions (already in glossary) - System and component identifiers - Contract and schema names - Data flow boundaries (what moves where) ### Step 2: Enumerate Impacted Nodes Using the system context and container diagrams, list every system, component, and contract that will change. For each node: - What changes? (new, modified, deleted) - What contracts does it expose or consume? - Which guardrail packs apply? ```markdown ## Impacted Node Inventory | Node ID | Node Type | Change Type | Contracts | Guardrail Packs | |---------|-----------|-------------|-----------|-----------------| | ... | system/component/contract | new/modify/delete | ... | ... | ``` ### Step 3: Map to Task Classes and Model Tiers Using `flagship-foundry-work/configs/model-routing/default.json`, assign each work unit a task class: | Task Type | Task Class | Model Tier | |-----------|-----------|------------| | Architecture decisions, risk analysis | `strategic_reasoning` | frontier_reasoner | | Constraint interpretation, scope clarification | `constraint_interpretation` | frontier_reasoner | | Code generation within bounded scope | `deterministic_transformation` | low_cost_executor | | Schema/contract/config generation | `structured_generation` | low_cost_executor | | Independent test validation | `verification` | balanced_reasoner | | Root cause analysis | `diagnostics` | frontier_reasoner | | Fix-memory and learning extraction | `learning` | balanced_reasoner | ### Step 4: Generate Work Order Tree For each chunk, produce a work order following `flagship-foundry-work/schemas/agent-work-order.schema.json`: ```markdown ## Work Order: [work-order-id] - **Lifecycle Stage**: [implement / verify / etc.] - **Phase ID**: [kebab-case slug] - **Task Class**: [from step 3] - **Agent Role**: builder / verifier / systems-architect / etc. - **Model Tier**: [from step 3] - **File Scope**: [explicit list of files to create/modify] - **Source Artifacts**: [intent packet, ADRs, schemas] - **Constraints**: [guardrail pack rules that apply] - **Acceptance Criteria**: - [ ] [criterion from intent packet] - **Verification Plan**: - `pnpm exec nx run <project>:typecheck` - `pnpm exec nx run <project>:test` - **Rollback Notes**: [how to undo] - **Approval Required**: yes/no [for high-risk actions] ``` ### Step 5: Attach Principle Cards For each applicable principle from `flagship-foundry-work/ontology/principle-catalog.json`, attach to affected work orders: **`principle:complexity-budgets`** — Apply to any work order touching data models or schemas: - Anti-patterns to avoid: unbounded lists, deeply nested structures, implicit relationships - Visual hints: flag data model diagrams with complexity score **`principle:contract-first`** — Apply to any work order creating or modifying APIs/interfaces: - Required: define interface/schema before implementation - Anti-pattern: defining contracts after implementation **`principle:observed-vs-declared-truth`** — Apply to any work order touching state or telemetry: - Required: distinguish runtime observations from declared state - Anti-pattern: treating cached/derived data as authoritative ### Step 6: Produce Chunked Task Summary ```markdown # Scope Chunk Summary - **Total Work Orders**: [n] - **Estimated Phases**: [list phases in order] - **Critical Path**: [sequence of dependent work orders] - **Parallelizable**: [work orders that can run simultaneously] - **Approval Gates**: [work orders requiring human approval] ## Work Order Sequence 1. [WO-001]: [title] → @[agent] ([task class]) [depends on: none] 2. [WO-002]: [title] → @[agent] ([task class]) [depends on: WO-001] ... ## First Work Order (Ready to Execute) [Paste the first work order in full] ``` ### Step 7: Update Continuity State Use `continuity-writer` to update `current-task.json`: - `lifecycleStage` → `plan` - `currentPhase.status` → `done` (plan phase complete) - `nextWorkOrders` → array of generated work order IDs - `artifacts` → add intent packet path and work order tree path
===FILE:.foundry/skills/sdlc-phase-router/reference/phase-gate-matrix.md===# Phase Gate Matrix — Flagship Foundry 11-Phase Lifecycle | Phase | Entry Criteria (DoR) | Primary Agent | Required Outputs | Exit Criteria (DoD) | |-------|---------------------|---------------|-----------------|---------------------| | **discover** | Problem statement exists | context-curator | Stakeholder map, constraint list, risk register | Problem is bounded, stakeholders identified, risks cataloged | | **define** | Discovery complete | systems-architect | Acceptance criteria, non-goals, scope boundary, glossary | Acceptance criteria testable, scope approved by human | | **visualize** | Scope defined | systems-architect | C4 system context diagram, container diagram | Diagrams reviewed, trust boundaries marked | | **architect** | Visualization complete | systems-architect | ADRs, contracts, schemas, decomposition plan | Architecture approved, contracts machine-readable | | **plan** | Architecture approved | orchestrator | Task tree, implementation slices, rollout path | Tasks bounded, each slice independently verifiable | | **implement** | Plan approved, DoR met per slice | builder | Code, config, tests, build passing | All acceptance criteria met, tests passing, scope respected | | **verify** | Implementation claims complete | verifier | Verification report, evidence bundle | PASS verdict or actionable FAIL with evidence | | **release** | Verification PASS | docs-release-agent | Release notes, handoff doc, deployment guide | Artifacts packaged, rollback rehearsed, release gate green | | **operate** | Released to production | performance-reviewer | Baseline metrics, monitoring confirmation | Telemetry flowing, alerts configured, runbooks current | | **diagnose** | Incident or anomaly detected | verifier + security-reviewer | Root cause analysis, evidence timeline | Root cause identified, remediation plan proposed | | **improve** | Diagnosis complete or sprint end | docs-release-agent | Learning record, continuity patch, standard updates | Learnings recorded, standards updated, continuity current |
===FILE:.foundry/skills/sdlc-phase-router/SKILL.md===# SDLC Phase Router Route work to the correct lifecycle stage by reading continuity state and matching user intent to the 11-phase lifecycle. ## Routing Protocol ### Step 1: Read Continuity State ```bash cat .foundry/projects/<project>/current-task.json ``` If missing, try legacy `cat .codex/projects/<project>/current-task.json`. Extract `sdlcPhase` (legacy 7-phase) or `lifecycleStage` (Flagship 11-phase). ### Step 2: Map Intent to Phase | User Intent Pattern | Target Phase | Primary Agent | |---|---|---| | "I have an idea", "new feature", "what if we..." | discover | @context-curator → @systems-architect | | "define scope", "acceptance criteria", "requirements" | define | @systems-architect | | "show me the architecture", "diagram", "visualize" | visualize | @systems-architect | | "design the system", "ADR", "contracts", "schema" | architect | @systems-architect | | "break it down", "task list", "implementation plan" | plan | @orchestrator (self) | | "build it", "implement", "code this" | implement | @builder | | "test it", "verify", "does it work", "review" | verify | @verifier | | "ship it", "release", "deploy" | release | @docs-release-agent | | "monitor", "how is it running", "production" | operate | @performance-reviewer | | "it's broken", "bug", "incident", "why did this fail" | diagnose | @verifier + @security-reviewer | | "what did we learn", "improve", "retrospective" | improve | @docs-release-agent | ### Step 3: Check Definition of Ready (DoR) Before entering the target phase, verify: - [ ] Goal is stated - [ ] Scope is bounded - [ ] Acceptance criteria defined - [ ] Risks identified - [ ] Rollback idea documented - [ ] Test outline present If DoR is not met, the orchestrator must fill gaps before delegation. ### Step 4: Generate Work Order Summary Produce a work order with: - `lifecycleStage`: the target phase - `phaseId`: a kebab-case identifier (e.g., `feature-auth-login-implement`) - `agentRole`: which agent to delegate to - `fileScope`: files the agent may touch - `acceptanceCriteria`: how to know it's done - `verificationPlan`: commands to run after completion ### Step 5: Delegate Hand the work order to the appropriate agent and monitor for completion. ## Legacy Phase Mapping When reading Codex `sdlcPhase` (7 values), map to Flagship lifecycle: | Codex Phase | Flagship Stage(s) | |---|---| | plan | discover + define + plan | | design | visualize + architect | | implement | implement | | verify | verify | | document | improve | | release | release | | operate | operate + diagnose |

===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/apps/cursor-companion/README.md===# Flagship Foundry Cursor Companion A Cursor and VS Code companion surface for Flagship Foundry. ## Capabilities - Start the local Foundry control plane - Import the current workspace into the ecosystem graph - Create plans from the current workspace - Toggle auto approval and auto start behavior - Approve plans manually - Start, pause, resume, and stop simulated runs ## Install during development 1. Open the `apps/cursor-companion/` folder as an extension project in a VS Code compatible environment. 2. Run the extension host for development. 3. Open the Foundry repository in Cursor. 4. Run `Flagship Foundry: Open Orchestration Overlay`. ## Settings - `flagshipFoundry.controlPlaneUrl` - `flagshipFoundry.autoApproveDraftPlans` - `flagshipFoundry.autoStartApprovedPlans`

===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/apps/graph-viewer/src/hooks/useGlossary.ts===import { useEffect, useMemo, useRef, useState } from 'react' import type { Glossary, GlossaryCategory, GlossaryTerm } from '../types.ts' const API_BASE = import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE ?? 'http://localhost:4010' // Raw term shape as received from the API — category is absent since it lives // on the parent category object. interface RawGlossaryTerm { term: string definition: string relatedTerms?: string[] applicablePhases?: string[] } interface RawGlossaryCategory { id: string name: string description?: string terms: RawGlossaryTerm[] } interface RawGlossary { version: string source: string categories: RawGlossaryCategory[] } // Enrich the raw payload by injecting the category id into each term. function enrichGlossary(raw: RawGlossary): Glossary { const categories: GlossaryCategory[] = raw.categories.map((cat) => ({ id: cat.id, name: cat.name, description: cat.description, terms: cat.terms.map((t) => ({ ...t, category: cat.id, })), })) return { version: raw.version, source: raw.source, categories } } // Module-level cache so the large JSON is only fetched once per page load. let cachedGlossary: Glossary | null = null let pendingFetch: Promise<Glossary> | null = null function fetchGlossary(): Promise<Glossary> { if (cachedGlossary !== null) { return Promise.resolve(cachedGlossary) } if (pendingFetch !== null) { return pendingFetch } pendingFetch = fetch(`${API_BASE}/ontology/glossary`) .then((res) => { if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`) return res.json() as Promise<RawGlossary> }) .then((raw) => { const data = enrichGlossary(raw) cachedGlossary = data pendingFetch = null return data }) .catch((err: unknown) => { pendingFetch = null throw err }) return pendingFetch } export interface UseGlossaryResult { categories: GlossaryCategory[] allTerms: GlossaryTerm[] lookupTerm: (term: string) => GlossaryTerm | undefined searchTerms: (query: string) => GlossaryTerm[] getTermsForPhase: (phaseId: string) => GlossaryTerm[] getTermsForCategory: (categoryId: string) => GlossaryTerm[] loading: boolean error: string | null } export function useGlossary(): UseGlossaryResult { const [glossary, setGlossary] = useState<Glossary | null>(cachedGlossary) const [loading, setLoading] = useState<boolean>(cachedGlossary === null) const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null) // Prevent state updates after unmount. const mountedRef = useRef(true) useEffect(() => { mountedRef.current = true return () => { mountedRef.current = false } }, []) useEffect(() => { if (cachedGlossary !== null) { setGlossary(cachedGlossary) setLoading(false) return } setLoading(true) setError(null) fetchGlossary() .then((data) => { if (!mountedRef.current) return setGlossary(data) }) .catch((err: unknown) => { if (!mountedRef.current) return const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) setError(`Failed to load glossary: ${msg}`) }) .finally(() => { if (!mountedRef.current) return setLoading(false) }) }, []) const categories = useMemo<GlossaryCategory[]>( () => glossary?.categories ?? [], [glossary], ) const allTerms = useMemo<GlossaryTerm[]>(() => { if (!glossary) return [] return glossary.categories.flatMap((cat) => cat.terms) }, [glossary]) // Build a lowercase-keyed lookup map for O(1) term resolution. const termMap = useMemo<Map<string, GlossaryTerm>>(() => { const map = new Map<string, GlossaryTerm>() for (const t of allTerms) { map.set(t.term.toLowerCase(), t) } return map }, [allTerms]) const lookupTerm = useMemo( () => (term: string): GlossaryTerm | undefined => termMap.get(term.toLowerCase()), [termMap], ) const searchTerms = useMemo( () => (query: string): GlossaryTerm[] => { if (!query.trim()) return allTerms const lower = query.toLowerCase() return allTerms.filter((t) => t.term.toLowerCase().includes(lower)) }, [allTerms], ) const getTermsForPhase = useMemo( () => (phaseId: string): GlossaryTerm[] => allTerms.filter((t) => t.applicablePhases?.includes(phaseId) ?? false), [allTerms], ) const getTermsForCategory = useMemo( () => (categoryId: string): GlossaryTerm[] => { const cat = categories.find((c) => c.id === categoryId) return cat ? cat.terms : [] }, [categories], ) return { categories, allTerms, lookupTerm, searchTerms, getTermsForPhase, getTermsForCategory, loading, error, } }

===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/apps/graph-viewer/src/layout.ts===import type { Node } from '@xyflow/react' import type { FoundryNode } from './types.ts' const NODE_WIDTH = 220 const NODE_HEIGHT = 90 const H_GAP = 40 const V_GAP = 80 // Ordered tiers for hierarchical layout — types not listed fall into the last tier const TYPE_TIER: Record<string, number> = { ecosystem: 0, repo: 1, system: 2, project: 3, framework: 4, platform: 4, 'rule-pack': 5, environment: 5, diagram: 5, } function getTier(type: string): number { return TYPE_TIER[type] ?? 6 } export function buildHierarchicalLayout(foundryNodes: FoundryNode[]): Node[] { // Group nodes by tier const tiers = new Map<number, FoundryNode[]>() for (const node of foundryNodes) { const tier = getTier(node.type) const existing = tiers.get(tier) if (existing) { existing.push(node) } else { tiers.set(tier, [node]) } } const sortedTiers = Array.from(tiers.keys()).sort((a, b) => a - b) const result: Node[] = [] let currentY = 0 for (const tier of sortedTiers) { const nodesInTier = tiers.get(tier) ?? [] const totalWidth = nodesInTier.length * NODE_WIDTH + (nodesInTier.length - 1) * H_GAP const startX = -(totalWidth / 2) for (let i = 0; i < nodesInTier.length; i++) { const foundryNode = nodesInTier[i] result.push({ id: foundryNode.id, type: mapToReactFlowType(foundryNode.type), position: { x: startX + i * (NODE_WIDTH + H_GAP), y: currentY, }, data: { foundryNode, }, style: { width: NODE_WIDTH, minHeight: NODE_HEIGHT, }, }) } currentY += NODE_HEIGHT + V_GAP } return result } export function mapToReactFlowType(nodeType: string): string { switch (nodeType) { case 'ecosystem': return 'ecosystemNode' case 'system': return 'systemNode' case 'project': return 'projectNode' default: return 'defaultNode' } }

===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/adr/adr-001-artifact-authority-and-research-home.md===# ADR-001: Establish Artifact Authority and Research Home ## Status accepted ## Date 2026-03-23 ## Context The initiative spans two planes with different roles: - `flagship-foundry-work/` is the canonical runnable application root. - The parent workspace contains rules, skills, plans, and research artifacts that are valuable inputs but not consistently authoritative. `WO-FF-001` requires an explicit authority model before source-of-truth mapping and sync-direction policy can be executed safely. ## Options Considered ### Option A: Keep root-level research as a co-equal canonical source **Description**: Treat root research and `flagship-foundry-work/docs/` as peers. **Pros**: Minimal migration effort. **Cons**: Ongoing ambiguity and drift. ### Option B: Move all research immediately under `flagship-foundry-work/docs/` **Description**: Force immediate migration before implementation begins. **Pros**: Single clear home quickly. **Cons**: High blast radius and broken references. ### Option C: Dual-plane with curated promotion into canonical docs **Description**: Keep `flagship-foundry-work/` authoritative. Root-level research remains reference-only until curated and promoted into canonical docs. **Pros**: Clear authority, low migration risk, supports phased transition. **Cons**: Temporary dual locations remain. ## Decision Choose **Option C**. - Canonical behavior-defining documentation lives under `flagship-foundry-work/docs/`. - Root-level research artifacts are supporting references unless explicitly promoted. - Sync direction is canonical -> projections only. ## Consequences ### Positive - Unblocks `WO-FF-001` with explicit authority boundaries. - Reduces accidental writes to non-canonical areas. - Preserves historical material without immediate destructive moves. ### Negative - Temporary dual-document locations persist. - Promotion workflow must be enforced. ### Risks - Teams may continue using root artifacts as authority unless documentation is prominent. - Promotion backlog could delay consolidation. ## References - `/Users/evanmccall/Projects/SDLC - Visual - Workflow - SoftwareEngineering-NewAge/.cursor/plans/foundry-gap-analysis-intent_d20ed327.plan.md` - `/Users/evanmccall/Projects/SDLC - Visual - Workflow - SoftwareEngineering-NewAge/README.md` - `/Users/evanmccall/Projects/SDLC - Visual - Workflow - SoftwareEngineering-NewAge/flagship-foundry-work/README.md` - `/Users/evanmccall/Projects/SDLC - Visual - Workflow - SoftwareEngineering-NewAge/flagship-foundry-work/docs/REPOSITORY_LAYOUT.md`
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/adr/adr-002-continuity-schema-authority-and-bootstrap.md===# ADR-002: Define Continuity Schema Authority and Bootstrap Path ## Status accepted ## Date 2026-03-23 ## Context The workflow depends on machine-readable continuity state for deterministic resume and lifecycle routing. Current signals: - `flagship-foundry-work/schemas/continuity-state.schema.json` exists. - Operational continuity commonly uses `.codex/projects/<project>/current-task.json`. `WO-FF-002` needs one contract authority and one runtime instance authority. ## Options Considered ### Option A: Keep continuity state only inside `flagship-foundry-work/state/` **Description**: Use Foundry state as both schema and runtime authority. **Pros**: Single app-root boundary. **Cons**: Conflicts with existing resume workflows. ### Option B: Let each tool own separate continuity contracts **Description**: Keep `.codex/.cursor/.claude` independent. **Pros**: Low immediate change. **Cons**: Guaranteed drift and non-deterministic behavior. ### Option C: Separate contract authority from runtime instance authority **Description**: Foundry owns schema; active runtime instance lives at `.codex/projects/<project>/current-task.json`. **Pros**: Contract-first with practical compatibility. **Cons**: Requires migration and clear documentation. ## Decision Choose **Option C**. - Contract authority: `flagship-foundry-work/schemas/continuity-state.schema.json`. - Runtime instance authority: `.foundry/projects/<project>/current-task.json` (**ADR-011**; historically `.codex/projects/...` before 2026-03-23). - Any mirrors are derived, not authoritative. ## Consequences ### Positive - Unblocks `WO-FF-002`. - Preserves deterministic resume expectations. - Supports parity projection without duplicated authority. ### Negative - Requires schema migration and compatibility checks. - Adds conceptual split (contract owner vs instance owner). ### Risks - Legacy tooling may assume old phase semantics. - Missing bootstrap files can cause routing failures. ## Amendment (2026-03-23): runtime instance path The **runtime instance authority** path **`.codex/projects/<project>/current-task.json`** described in **Option C** is superseded for Flagship Foundry by **ADR-011**: continuity instances are stored at **`.foundry/projects/<project>/current-task.json`** (agent-neutral root). The **contract authority** is unchanged. ## References - `/Users/evanmccall/Projects/SDLC - Visual - Workflow - SoftwareEngineering-NewAge/.cursor/plans/foundry-gap-analysis-intent_d20ed327.plan.md` - `/Users/evanmccall/Projects/SDLC - Visual - Workflow - SoftwareEngineering-NewAge/flagship-foundry-work/schemas/continuity-state.schema.json` - `docs/adr/adr-011-foundry-directory-layout-and-continuity-instance.md`
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/adr/adr-003-artifact-classification-drift-and-archive-retention.md===# ADR-003: Classify Artifacts, Drift Rules, and Archive Retention ## Status accepted ## Date 2026-03-23 ## Context The repo includes active code, duplicated artifacts, generated outputs, packaged research, and iterative copies. `WO-FF-003` requires explicit classification and retention rules before drift automation or cleanup can run. ## Options Considered ### Option A: Retain all copies indefinitely; informational drift only **Description**: Keep all duplicates and archives without lifecycle rules. **Pros**: No immediate cleanup risk. **Cons**: Persistent ambiguity and search noise. ### Option B: Aggressive duplicate deletion after canonical selection **Description**: Remove duplicates immediately. **Pros**: Fast simplification. **Cons**: High rollback risk. ### Option C: Three classes with explicit drift and retention rules **Description**: Canonical, generated, archive with class-specific handling. **Pros**: Safe automation, reversible migration, objective drift checks. **Cons**: Requires inventory and policy discipline. ## Decision Choose **Option C**. Artifact classes: - **Canonical**: authoritative human-maintained sources. - **Generated**: reproducible outputs; manual edits are non-authoritative. - **Archive**: historical snapshots and iterative copies retained for rollback/audit. Retention policy: - Keep archive snapshots for at least 30 days and one successful release cycle after replacement, whichever is longer. - No destructive cleanup until parity checks are green and approval is recorded. ## Consequences ### Positive - Unblocks safe drift policy implementation. - Preserves rollback while enabling cleanup later. - Clarifies handling of packaged research and iterative copies. ### Negative - Some duplicates remain in short term. - Inventory maintenance becomes ongoing work. ### Risks - Misclassification can hide real drift. - Archive volume can grow if cleanup discipline slips. ## References - `/Users/evanmccall/Projects/SDLC - Visual - Workflow - SoftwareEngineering-NewAge/.cursor/plans/foundry-gap-analysis-intent_d20ed327.plan.md` - `/Users/evanmccall/Projects/SDLC - Visual - Workflow - SoftwareEngineering-NewAge/flagship-foundry-work/docs/REPOSITORY_LAYOUT.md`
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/adr/adr-004-parity-projection-merge-policy.md===# ADR-004: Set Parity Projection Merge and Regeneration Policy ## Status accepted ## Date 2026-03-23 ## Context This initiative requires convergence across `.cursor`, `.codex`, and `.claude` without breaking user-owned local setups. `WO-FF-004` needs explicit ownership and conflict policy for generated doctrine projections. ## Options Considered ### Option A: Blind overwrite from generated outputs **Description**: Always regenerate and replace target files. **Pros**: Maximum parity consistency. **Cons**: High risk to user-owned configs. ### Option B: Advisory diffs only, no writes **Description**: Detect drift but require full manual edits. **Pros**: Lowest overwrite risk. **Cons**: High toil and persistent divergence. ### Option C: Detect, diff, merge, and approval for conflicts **Description**: Auto-apply only machine-owned changes; require approval for user-owned conflicts. **Pros**: Balanced safety and automation. **Cons**: Requires ownership metadata and conflict flow. ## Decision Choose **Option C**. Projection policy: 1. Detect existing artifacts. 2. Generate proposed outputs from canonical source. 3. Diff target vs generated. 4. Auto-apply only to machine-owned or empty targets. 5. Require manual approval for user-owned conflicts. 6. Never blind-overwrite local user configuration. ## Consequences ### Positive - Unblocks parity pipeline with bounded blast radius. - Preserves trust in local developer setups. - Enables scalable parity with explicit conflict handling. ### Negative - More implementation complexity than pure regenerate/overwrite. - Conflict queue may require manual triage. ### Risks - Ownership tagging errors can still cause accidental modifications. - Weak reporting can slow approvals. ## References - `/Users/evanmccall/Projects/SDLC - Visual - Workflow - SoftwareEngineering-NewAge/.cursor/plans/foundry-gap-analysis-intent_d20ed327.plan.md` - `/Users/evanmccall/Projects/SDLC - Visual - Workflow - SoftwareEngineering-NewAge/flagship-foundry-work/environments/README.md`
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/adr/adr-005-knowledge-pack-completeness-and-freshness-sla.md===# ADR-005: Define Knowledge-Pack Completeness and Freshness SLA ## Status accepted ## Date 2026-03-23 ## Context `WO-FF-005` is the knowledge-coverage work order in milestone `M2`, following the authority decisions in ADR-001 and the drift rules in ADR-003. The repository already has: - a pack contract at `flagship-foundry-work/schemas/knowledge-pack.schema.json` - knowledge-state manifests under `flagship-foundry-work/state/knowledge/` - a coverage report at `flagship-foundry-work/state/knowledge/foundry-foundational-docs/coverage-report.md` - source lineage and versions at `flagship-foundry-work/state/knowledge/foundry-foundational-docs/manifest.json` - SME profile outputs that depend on pack quality under `flagship-foundry-work/state/ecosystems/web-automation-workspace/profiles/` What is missing is a decision for when a pack is considered complete enough and fresh enough to unblock later work. Document counts alone do not tell the team whether a pack has the required lineage, downstream links, or refresh cadence. `M2` needs an explicit SLA so `WO-FF-005` can exit with objective criteria and so `M3` and `M4` do not consume stale pack inputs. ## Options Considered ### Option A: Best-effort pack growth with no formal SLA **Description**: Keep adding documents and coverage reports, but leave completeness and refresh timing to operator judgment. **Pros**: Lowest process overhead. **Cons**: No objective exit criteria, high drift risk, and later milestones cannot reliably know whether pack inputs are current. ### Option B: One global repository-wide SLA for every pack **Description**: Apply one uniform completeness rule and one uniform refresh window to all packs. **Pros**: Simple to explain and automate. **Cons**: Treats high-churn and low-churn packs the same, over-constrains archival/reference packs, and under-specifies milestone-critical packs. ### Option C: Tiered SLA by pack criticality and downstream linkage **Description**: Define completeness using canonical contract plus lineage and linkage, and define freshness windows by milestone relevance. **Pros**: Aligns to `M2` through `M4`, supports objective verification, and focuses operational effort on packs that actually gate work orders. **Cons**: Requires pack classification and waiver handling. ## Decision Choose **Option C**. Completeness policy: - A knowledge pack is complete only when its canonical contract is defined by `flagship-foundry-work/schemas/knowledge-pack.schema.json`. - The pack must have source lineage recorded in a knowledge manifest such as `flagship-foundry-work/state/knowledge/foundry-foundational-docs/manifest.json`. - The pack must appear in a generated coverage artifact such as `flagship-foundry-work/state/knowledge/foundry-foundational-docs/coverage-report.md`. - If the pack is used to drive personas, runbooks, or guardrails for active work, the corresponding downstream artifacts must resolve from canonical Foundry assets rather than ad hoc notes. Freshness policy: - Packs directly supporting the active milestone are **critical** and must be refreshed within 14 days of source-version change or before milestone exit, whichever comes first. - Packs required for the next planned milestone are **important** and must be refreshed within 30 days. - Reference-only packs may exceed these windows only if they are not referenced by active work orders or gate logic. Milestone alignment: - `M2` exit for `WO-FF-005` requires all packs that directly support knowledge coverage, environment parity, verification, or observability work to meet the completeness rules above. - `M3` and `M4` may consume only packs that are complete and not past SLA, unless an explicit waiver is recorded in the active plan or approval artifacts. ## Consequences ### Positive - Gives `WO-FF-005` an objective definition of done. - Makes later milestone inputs auditable through manifests and coverage reports. - Reduces the risk that stale documentation silently feeds planning, verification, or operations. ### Negative - Introduces pack classification and waiver-management work. - Some packs that appear large by document count may still fail completeness because their linkage is weak. ### Risks - Overly strict freshness windows could slow milestone closure if source refresh automation is incomplete. - Weak downstream linkage checks could still allow apparently complete packs that do not materially help planning. - Teams may optimize for document counts unless completeness checks emphasize lineage and linkage over volume. ## Acceptance Notes - `WO-FF-005` implements tier-aligned completeness and freshness checks in `packages/core/src/gap-analysis.mjs`. - Knowledge-base outputs now stamp SLA authority and freshness policy from ADR-005 under ADR-001 authority constraints. - Canonical downstream linkage for active packs is enforced through SME profile `knowledgePackIds` references. ## References - `/Users/evanmccall/Projects/SDLC - Visual - Workflow - SoftwareEngineering-NewAge/.cursor/plans/foundry-gap-analysis-intent_d20ed327.plan.md` - ===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/adr/adr-006-control-plane-auth-and-trust-boundary.md===# ADR-006: Adopt Control-Plane Auth and Trust-Boundary Model ## Status accepted ## Date 2026-03-23 ## Context The control plane is central to planning, runs, continuity, and evidence. Security hardening requires a clear auth model and trust-boundary policy before `WO-FF-006`. ## Options Considered ### Option A: Local-only unauthenticated mode **Description**: Trust loopback and host boundaries only. **Pros**: Minimal complexity and friction. **Cons**: Unsafe beyond pure local use. ### Option B: Scoped bearer-token baseline with explicit local-dev exception **Description**: Require tokens for non-loopback access; allow bounded local loopback mode. **Pros**: Strong baseline without heavy federation complexity. **Cons**: Requires token lifecycle and secret-handling discipline. ### Option C: Federated identity from day one **Description**: Full OIDC or similar immediately. **Pros**: Strong long-term enterprise posture. **Cons**: Premature complexity for current maturity. ## Decision Choose **Option B**. Security policy: - Non-loopback access requires scoped bearer tokens. - Loopback no-auth mode is allowed only as explicit development mode. - Remove wildcard CORS; enforce explicit allowlist. - Add request validation, payload size limits, timeouts, and rate limits. ## Consequences ### Positive - Raises security baseline before production-core execution. - Preserves practical local development. - Defers federation until a real multi-user hosting requirement exists. ### Negative - Token issuance/rotation introduces operational overhead. - Existing clients may need configuration changes. ### Risks - Overuse of local no-auth mode can erode posture. - Token leakage risk if logging/redaction is weak. ## References - `/Users/evanmccall/Projects/SDLC - Visual - Workflow - SoftwareEngineering-NewAge/.cursor/plans/foundry-gap-analysis-intent_d20ed327.plan.md` - `/Users/evanmccall/Projects/SDLC - Visual - Workflow - SoftwareEngineering-NewAge/flagship-foundry-work/apps/control-plane/src/server.mjs` - `/Users/evanmccall/Projects/SDLC - Visual - Workflow - SoftwareEngineering-NewAge/flagship-foundry-work/configs/approval-policies/default.json`
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/adr/adr-007-evidence-bundle-and-telemetry-contract.md===# ADR-007: Define Evidence Bundle and Telemetry Contract ## Status proposed ## Date 2026-03-23 ## Context `WO-FF-007` sits in `M3` after the control-plane trust decision in ADR-006 and alongside the operational reliability and observability work described in the gap-analysis intent. Foundry already has: - an evidence-bundle schema at `flagship-foundry-work/schemas/evidence-bundle.schema.json` - bundle assembly logic at `flagship-foundry-work/packages/core/src/evidence-bundle.mjs` - run state at `flagship-foundry-work/packages/core/src/runs.mjs` - richer run timeline semantics at `flagship-foundry-work/schemas/run-timeline.schema.json` - observability guardrails at `flagship-foundry-work/guardrails/telemetry-and-observability.json` - telemetry-oriented runbook and SME outputs under `flagship-foundry-work/runbooks/` and `flagship-foundry-work/state/ecosystems/web-automation-workspace/profiles/` The current evidence bundle is verifier-friendly but minimal. It captures task status, verification results, and evidence artifacts, but it does not yet define how telemetry signals correlate to the same run, task, plan, and adapter. `M3` needs one contract so an independent verifier can answer three questions deterministically: what ran, what passed, and what runtime signals changed. ## Options Considered ### Option A: Keep evidence bundles minimal and leave telemetry separate **Description**: Preserve the current evidence bundle shape and rely on ad hoc logs or manual telemetry lookup. **Pros**: Minimal schema change. **Cons**: Weak diagnosability, poor verifier ergonomics, and no deterministic correlation for incidents. ### Option B: Embed all telemetry payloads directly into the evidence bundle **Description**: Make the bundle a single artifact that contains both verification and raw telemetry data. **Pros**: One file per run, easy offline review. **Cons**: Large payloads, noisy reviewer experience, and poor separation between summary evidence and raw signal streams. ### Option C: Use one correlated contract with summary evidence plus telemetry references **Description**: Keep evidence bundles concise and verifier-oriented while requiring telemetry records to share stable correlation keys and referenceable artifacts. **Pros**: Balances readability, diagnosability, and storage discipline. **Cons**: Requires stronger correlation rules and artifact-generation discipline. ## Decision Choose **Option C**. Contract policy: - `flagship-foundry-work/schemas/evidence-bundle.schema.json` remains the canonical verifier-facing summary contract. - Detailed execution and verification timing remains anchored in the run and run-timeline artifacts. - Telemetry data is linked to the evidence bundle by reference rather than embedded wholesale. Correlation requirements: - Every evidence summary and telemetry artifact must carry `runId`. - Task-scoped records must also carry `taskId`. - Run-correlated artifacts must carry `planId`, `ecosystemId`, and `adapterId` when available. - Timestamps must be preserved in machine-readable form for before/after comparison and incident reconstruction. Verifier requirements: - The bundle must summarize verification outcomes and point to the produced evidence artifacts. - Incident-derived or telemetry-driven work must include before/after telemetry references. - When a fix-memory record is produced, the evidence model must point to it so learning artifacts remain tied to the originating run. Milestone alignment: - `WO-FF-007` exits only when an independent verifier can reconstruct the execution path from run state, evidence bundle, and telemetry references without relying on chat history or operator memory. - `M4` release decisions may only consume evidence that conforms to this correlation model. ## Consequences ### Positive - Gives the verifier a deterministic contract for operational and release sign-off. - Preserves concise review artifacts while keeping deep telemetry available. - Supports incident analysis, fix-memory generation, and release evidence reuse. ### Negative - Adds correlation-field discipline across execution, verification, and telemetry producers. - Requires schema and implementation changes in more than one artifact family. ### Risks - Partial adoption could create mixed bundles where some tasks are fully correlated and others are not. - If telemetry references are not retained long enough, evidence bundles may degrade over time. - Over-collecting telemetry could produce noise unless the contract distinguishes required summaries from optional detail. ## References - `/Users/evanmccall/Projects/SDLC - Visual - Workflow - SoftwareEngineering-NewAge/.cursor/plans/foundry-gap-analysis-intent_d20ed327.plan.md` - ===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/adr/adr-008-runtime-adapter-isolation-and-rollback-boundary.md===# ADR-008: Define Runtime Adapter Isolation and Rollback Boundary ## Status accepted ## Date 2026-03-23 ## Context `WO-FF-008` is the real-execution hardening work order in `M3`. It follows the security baseline in ADR-006 and depends on evidence discipline so real runs can be rolled back safely. The repository already shows an execution direction: - `flagship-foundry-work/packages/core/src/run-executor.mjs` creates per-run work directories under `state/run-workspaces/` - `flagship-foundry-work/packages/core/src/runs.mjs` supports `start`, `pause`, `resume`, `stop`, `complete`, and `fail` - `flagship-foundry-work/packages/runtime-adapters/src/registry.mjs` defines adapter identities - `flagship-foundry-work/README.md` documents `adapter:local-shell` for execute mode and `GET /runs/:id/evidence-bundle` - `flagship-foundry-work/configs/approval-policies/default.json` preserves manual approval by default What is still missing is an explicit architectural rule for adapter isolation and rollback. Without it, a real adapter could bypass the intended safety boundary, mutate canonical assets directly, or leave the team without a clean rollback point when an execution fails. ## Options Considered ### Option A: Allow adapters to execute directly against the workspace root **Description**: Let each adapter decide its own working directory and rollback behavior. **Pros**: Lowest friction for adapter authors. **Cons**: High blast radius, inconsistent rollback semantics, and weak auditability. ### Option B: Require full container or VM sandboxing for every adapter from day one **Description**: Only allow execution in heavyweight isolated sandboxes. **Pros**: Strong isolation posture. **Cons**: High implementation cost, slow path to first production-safe adapter, and likely over-engineered for current maturity. ### Option C: Use a bounded adapter contract with per-run isolation and explicit rollback boundary **Description**: Every execute-mode adapter runs inside a run-scoped boundary and must preserve state, evidence, and approvals needed for rollback. **Pros**: Strong enough for `M3`, consistent with current implementation direction, and practical for incremental adapter expansion. **Cons**: Requires clear policy enforcement and future adapter conformance work. ## Decision Choose **Option C**. Isolation policy: - Execute-mode adapters must operate through a registered adapter identity and run contract. - The default execution boundary is a run-scoped working directory such as `flagship-foundry-work/state/run-workspaces/<run-id>/`. - Evidence output must be written to state artifacts, not hidden in transient process output only. - Adapters must not treat canonical docs, schemas, or source trees as writable by default. Rollback policy: - The rollback boundary is the run instance, its task states, and its isolated workspace. - `pause` and `stop` remain first-class rollback controls for halting execution without destroying evidence. - Failed or stopped runs preserve approvals, task status, and evidence artifacts for diagnosis. - Any adapter capability that writes outside the isolated run boundary requires explicit approval and separate policy treatment before promotion to default use. Promotion policy: - `adapter:dry-run` remains the default baseline for broad planning flows. - `adapter:local-shell` is the first production-safe real adapter path only if it satisfies isolation, evidence, and rollback requirements. - Future adapters may be added only if they honor the same contract and do not weaken the rollback boundary. ## Consequences ### Positive - Gives `WO-FF-008` a concrete safety boundary that matches the repository’s current execution design. - Preserves evidence for diagnosis instead of trading rollback for cleanup. - Makes adapter behavior more consistent across local and future runtimes. ### Negative - Adapter authors must implement to a stricter contract. - Some useful direct-host capabilities will remain gated behind approval and policy work. ### Risks - If the isolated working directory is treated as sufficient without stronger policy checks, adapters may still reach outside the boundary through spawned commands. - Weak evidence capture could make stopped runs hard to diagnose even if isolation is correct. - Future non-shell adapters may need additional isolation mechanisms beyond the current run-workspace model. ## DoD Indicators - [x] Run records include run-scoped isolation contract and rollback boundary metadata. - [x] Executor persists per-task evidence in run workspace and records verification artifacts. - [x] `pause` and `stop` transitions preserve rollback timeline/evidence context. - [x] Default policy and guardrails prohibit default writes outside run-scoped workspace. - [x] Tests cover isolation metadata and rollback semantics. ## References - `/Users/evanmccall/Projects/SDLC - ===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/adr/adr-009-ci-gate-baseline-and-release-evidence-threshold.md===# ADR-009: Set CI Gate Baseline and Release Evidence Threshold ## Status accepted ## Date 2026-03-23 ## Context `WO-FF-009` is the `M4` industrialization work order for CI and release gating. It depends on the evidence and runtime hardening completed in `M2` and `M3`. Today the repository has: - a minimum milestone verification note in `flagship-foundry-work/docs/adr/NEXT_AGENT_EXECUTION_STEPS.md` that points to `cd flagship-foundry-work && npm test` - executable sample scripts in `flagship-foundry-work/package.json` - API endpoints and run evidence concepts documented in `flagship-foundry-work/README.md` - evidence and run schemas under `flagship-foundry-work/schemas/` What it does not yet have is a repository-owned CI baseline and a release threshold that says exactly how much automated evidence is enough to declare a change releasable. Without that decision, later milestones risk falling back to manual judgment or inconsistent gate depth. ## Options Considered ### Option A: Manual sign-off with advisory automation **Description**: Keep tests and scripts available, but let operators decide what to run and whether release evidence is sufficient. **Pros**: Minimal setup effort. **Cons**: Inconsistent release quality, poor auditability, and weak protection against regressions. ### Option B: Full enterprise-grade gate stack from day one **Description**: Require a comprehensive pipeline immediately, including every desired quality, security, and release artifact. **Pros**: Strong long-term posture. **Cons**: High initial cost and likely blocks `M4` on tooling that does not yet exist in the repository. ### Option C: Staged CI baseline with explicit blocking release evidence **Description**: Define a blocking minimum gate set now, expand it as tooling lands, and require evidence-backed sign-off for release readiness. **Pros**: Practical for current maturity, aligns with milestone sequencing, and prevents "green by anecdote." **Cons**: Requires careful distinction between current blocking gates and planned future gates. ## Decision Choose **Option C**. CI baseline policy: - `WO-FF-009` must introduce repository-owned automated gates rather than relying on operator memory. - The blocking baseline must include the currently supported automated test surface, beginning with `npm test`. - The blocking baseline must also include at least one targeted workflow that exercises the changed surface using existing repository commands or APIs, rather than unit tests alone. - Gate results must be preserved as evidence artifacts that can be attached to milestone and release sign-off. Release evidence threshold: - A release candidate is not release-ready unless it has current automated gate results plus a corresponding evidence bundle or equivalent run-linked evidence for the changed scope. - `M4` decisions must consume `M2` and `M3` evidence, not just the current pipeline run, because runtime hardening and telemetry contracts are prerequisite quality signals. - If required categories such as dependency or SBOM evidence are not yet automated, they must remain explicit blockers or approved waivers. They must not be treated as silent future work. Operational rule: - CI status is necessary but not sufficient; release readiness requires both passing automation and evidence that the independent verifier can inspect. - The threshold for production-style release is evidence-backed completion, not only successful command exit codes. ## Consequences ### Positive - Gives `WO-FF-009` a realistic but enforceable starting point. - Keeps the team from confusing "some tests ran" with "release evidence exists." - Allows the CI system to mature incrementally without losing architectural discipline. ### Negative - Teams must define and maintain targeted workflow checks in addition to the generic test command. - Some releases may be delayed until evidence retention and upload are automated cleanly. ### Risks - If the baseline remains too shallow for too long, the repository may have formal CI without meaningful protection. - If waivers are easy to grant, evidence thresholds may erode in practice. - If evidence artifacts are produced but not retained, release audits may become non-reproducible. ## References - `/Users/evanmccall/Projects/SDLC -
