===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/IDE_ENVIRONMENT_SPEC.md===# IDE Environment Spec ## Product role The IDE environment is a **shell around the control plane**, not the source of truth. The source of truth remains: - schemas, - graph state, - work orders, - continuity, - evidence, - learning artifacts. ## Required surfaces ### 1. Graph canvas - system map - component map - sequence and event views - ownership and trust-boundary overlays - complexity/principles overlays - production telemetry overlays ### 2. Orchestration board - active change requests - work-order tree - approval queue - blocked items - verification evidence - handoff readiness ### 3. Code/workspace surface - repository explorer - diff review - file-level work-order scope highlighting - contract view for impacted APIs/events/schemas ### 4. Runtime/operations surface - incident cockpit - alerts and SLOs - remediation proposals - rollback status - learning capture queue ### 5. Provider and adapter surface - connected terminal agents - model routing policies - local/remote backend health - adapter capabilities and failure notes ## Suggested architecture ### Phase 1 - terminal agent + browser dashboard - optional VS Code companion extension ### Phase 2 - Theia-based product shell - embedded graph canvas - embedded orchestration board - terminal adapter bridge panel - work-order inspector and evidence viewer ## Non-negotiable IDE constraints - the IDE may render and manipulate control-plane state, but not invent private hidden state; - every action must resolve to typed artifacts; - manual human edits are valid first-class operations and should be captured as evolution events; - the system must keep working without the IDE present.
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/IDE_STRATEGY.md===# IDE Strategy ## Problem The ecosystem needs an eventual integrated environment, but the control plane must not depend on that environment to be correct. ## Options considered ### Option A: VS Code / Cursor-style extension first **Strengths** - fastest adoption path - huge existing extension ecosystem - strong remote development story - familiar to most developers - ideal as a thin companion surface over a separate control plane **Weaknesses** - product surface is constrained by the host editor - deeper orchestration UX becomes awkward over time - marketplace and telemetry constraints are influenced by the host ecosystem - long-term product identity is dependent on another vendor’s editor shape ### Option B: Eclipse Theia-based custom IDE/tooling shell **Strengths** - vendor-neutral foundation - browser and Electron targets - deeper customization than a plain extension - strong fit for a graph canvas + orchestration + dashboard product - compatible with many VS Code extensions via Open VSX **Weaknesses** - slower to ship than an extension - requires product-level frontend/platform engineering - extension compatibility is strong but not identical in every case ### Option C: Grassroots editor/IDE from scratch **Strengths** - maximum product control - no inherited assumptions - can optimize everything around orchestration and visualization **Weaknesses** - highest cost and longest time to value - must rebuild editor, terminal, language tooling, debugging, extensions, remote dev, accessibility, and theming foundations - very poor validation path for an ambitious product this early ## Determination ### Phase 1 recommendation Use a **terminal-first control plane** plus **thin editor companions** where helpful. The system should work even if the only surface is a terminal agent and a browser dashboard. ### Phase 2 recommendation Build the dedicated product shell on **Eclipse Theia**, not by forking VS Code and not by building a grassroots editor from scratch. ### Why this determination is correct The product is not just “an editor with AI.” It is a **human/AI orchestration environment with graph visualization, evidence review, process control, and runtime operations**. That argues for full product control eventually, but not at the cost of delaying validation. ## Final recommendation - **Now:** terminal-first + VS Code-compatible companion where necessary - **Target product shell:** Theia-based custom environment - **Avoid initially:** building a net-new editor core from zero
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/IMPORT_AND_SCAFFOLD_PIPELINE.md===# Import and Scaffold Pipeline ## Goal Turn an existing ecosystem into a graph-native, approval-aware, knowledge-backed SDLC workspace without forcing a new implementation stack first. ## Supported entry paths - direct filesystem import for a live repository or workspace; - export-bundle import for text exports of code, configs, rules, and documentation; - future adapter path for connector or remote repository ingestion. ## Import stages 1. **Topology detection** - identify Nx monorepo, polyrepo, or undefined legacy structure; - detect systems, projects, frameworks, platforms, and deployment surfaces. 2. **Continuity and artifact ingestion** - ingest current task states, diagrams, rule packs, handoff markers, and phase-ledger signals; - detect agent-environment artifacts such as `.cursor`, `.claude`, `.codex`, `.foundry`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `.mcp.json`. 3. **Graph construction** - create nodes for ecosystem, repo, system, project, framework, platform, rule pack, diagram, task state, and environment; - create edges for containment, dependency, governance, platform targeting, visualization, environment configuration, and shared patterns. 4. **Knowledge publication** - generate SME profiles for detected frameworks, platforms, environment parity, and knowledge ingestion; - generate visualization exports; - publish an import report for human review. 5. **Planning enablement** - create plans from requests, telemetry, or inspection findings; - default to manual approval unless policy explicitly enables auto approval; - insert adversarial review rounds before implementation for risky work. ## Polyrepo and undefined ecosystem extrapolation When a workspace is not neatly organized, Foundry groups package roots, infers system boundaries from manifests and directories, marks uncertain edges as provisional, and publishes a review list rather than pretending certainty.
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/intent/intent-foundry-dot-foundry-ecosystem-init-2026-03-23.md===# Intent Packet: `.foundry` project root, ecosystem onboarding, Docker, and Cursor extension **Date:** 2026-03-23 **Slug:** `intent-foundry-dot-foundry-ecosystem-init-2026-03-23` --- ## Problem Statement - **Problem**: Continuity and project state today are rooted under **`.codex/projects/`**, which reads as **Codex-specific** even though the same JSON contract is meant to drive **any** agent (Cursor, Claude Code, generic CI). Operators want a **neutral, Foundry-branded** location—**`.foundry/`**—so project tracking is not tied to one vendor. Separately, there is no **single, authoritative step-by-step** for “initialize Foundry against a real ecosystem” including agents, skills, and pipeline gates. Finally, teams need a decision on **Docker** for supporting services and clarity on whether a **local Cursor/VS Code extension** can **bootstrap or refresh** a repo with agents, skills, and pipeline requirements for the Foundry development pipeline. - **Stakeholder**: Developers and platform owners adopting Flagship Foundry; AI agent operators; release/CI owners. - **Success Outcome**: Foundry-owned project state lives under **`.foundry/`** (with a clear migration path from `.codex`), documented **ecosystem initialization** steps exist, **Docker** posture is decided with rationale, and a **local extension** path is defined to auto-init/re-init pipeline artifacts where feasible. - **Constraints**: - Must respect **ADR-002** (contract authority in schema vs runtime instance path); changing the instance path requires **schema + code + tests** alignment (`continuity-state.schema.json` currently **patterns** `runtimeInstanceAuthority` to `.codex/projects/.../current-task.json`). - Must not break existing imports that scan **`.codex/`** for workspace content until an explicit migration/import strategy exists (`import-pipeline.mjs` treats `.codex/` as high-signal paths). - **Canonical product docs** remain under `flagship-foundry-work/docs/` per **ADR-001**. - **Known Risks**: - **Migration blast radius**: repos with `.codex/projects/**` and rules referencing that path need coordinated updates (or symlink/shim period). - **Schema tightening**: relaxing or changing `runtimeInstanceAuthority` pattern affects validation and any tooling that assumes `.codex`. - **Extension scope creep**: auto-init can overwrite user files; must align with **ADR-004** (no blind overwrite) and explicit approval/dry-run where needed. --- ## Scope - **In Scope**: 1. **Design + implement** moving (or aliasing) **runtime continuity instance** from `.codex/projects/<id>/` to **`.foundry/projects/<id>/`** (or agreed layout under `.foundry/`), including updates to: - `schemas/continuity-state.schema.json` (`authority.runtimeInstanceAuthority` pattern), - `packages/core/src/continuity.mjs` (`projectDir`, `authorityFor`, paths), - `tests/continuity.test.mjs` and any other consumers, - ADR-002 narrative and `.cursor` rules that reference `.codex/projects/**/current-task.json`, - Optional: **migration note** (copy/symlink from `.codex` → `.foundry` for existing projects). 2. **Author** a **step-by-step walkthrough** (operator doc) for initializing Foundry on a **filesystem-backed ecosystem**: import → knowledge → gap → plan → continuity → optional control plane + companion; include **agents/skills/pipeline** as “wire these artifacts from `knowledge/`, `.cursor/skills/`, runbooks, and CI gates” rather than inventing a new agent runtime. 3. **Document** a **Docker** recommendation: which components *may* be containerized (control plane, optional graph-viewer, optional MCP server), when it helps (CI, team parity), and when **plain Node on host** is enough. 4. **Assess** building a **local VS Code–compatible extension** (Cursor-compatible) to **initialize or re-initialize** Foundry scaffolding: invoke CLI (`init-project`, `import`, `scaffold-env`), prompt for config, optional API health check—aligned with existing `apps/cursor-companion/`. - **Non-Goals** (this slice): - Replacing Codex/OpenAI/Cursor products or shipping a hosted multi-tenant service. - Full “one click” parity projection apply without approvals (violates **ADR-004**). - Mandatory Docker for all developers if local Node is sufficient. --- ## Glossary | Term | Definition | |------|------------| | **Ecosystem** | A bounded workspace imported into Foundry (`ecosystemId`), with manifest + graph under `state/ecosystems/<id>/`. | | **Continuity instance** | Runtime JSON (`current-task.json`) plus optional charter, holding phase, `nextCommandSet`, `doneCriteria`. | | **Contract authority** | JSON Schema under `flagship-foundry-work/schemas/` that defines valid continuity shape (**ADR-002**). | | **`.foundry`** | Target neutral directory for Foundry-owned project metadata (replacing or alongside `.codex` for continuity). | | **Import source** | `filesystem` or `export-bundle` per `ecosystem-import-request.schema.json`. | | **Control plane** | HTTP API in `apps/control-plane/` (Node). | | **Local extension** | VS Code extension API–compatible extension run in Cursor/VS Code (dev or packaged). | --- ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] Given a repo adopting Foundry, when continuity is initialized, then **runtime instance path** resolves under **`.foundry/projects/<projectName>/current-task.json`** (or documented equivalent) and validates against updated schema. - [ ] Given existing projects using `.codex`, when migration is needed, then documentation describes **at least one** supported path (fresh init, copy, or symlink) without silent data loss. - [ ] Given a new engineer, when they follow the new walkthrough, then they can perform **import → knowledge → gap → plan** (and optional API) with explicit commands and expected `state/` outputs. - [ ] Given a platform review, when Docker is evaluated, then the doc states **which services are optional in containers**, **security notes** (tokens, bind mounts), and **default recommendation** (e.g., dev: no Docker required; CI: optional Docker for reproducibility). - [ ] Given the extension assessment, when documented, then it lists **feasible VS Code extension capabilities** (tasks, terminal, file templates), **integration points** (`node .../main.mjs`, `npm run api`), and **non-goals** (cannot auto-install proprietary Cursor CLI internals). --- ## Rollback Plan - Revert continuity path changes behind a **feature flag or env** (`FLAGSHIP_CONTINUITY_ROOT=.codex|.foundry`) if issues arise; restore schema pattern to `.codex` if needed. - Keep **backup** of `current-task.json` before migration scripts run. - Extension: ship as **optional** local package; disable via workspace setting. --- ## System Context Diagram High-level actors and systems (Mermaid). ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph operators [Operators] Dev[Developer] Agent[AI Agents] end subgraph foundry [Flagship Foundry] CLI[Orchestrator CLI] CP[Control Plane API] State[(state/)] FoundryMeta[".foundry/projects/"] end subgraph external [External] Repo[Target git repo] Cursor[Cursor / VS Code] end Dev --> CLI Dev --> CP Agent --> CLI Agent --> CP CLI --> State CP --> State CLI --> FoundryMeta Cursor -->|optional extension| CP Cursor -->|optional| CLI Repo -->|filesystem import| CLI ``` **Trust boundaries**: Control plane auth (**ADR-006**) for non-loopback; secrets stay in env/KMS, not in `.foundry` committed files. --- ## Container Diagram Major runtime units. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph host [Developer machine or CI runner] Node[Node.js runtime] CLI[apps/orchestrator-cli] CP[apps/control-plane] Ext[cursor-companion extension] Node --> CLI Node --> CP Node --> Ext end subgraph optional_docker [Optional containers] DCP[control-plane image] DGV[graph-viewer static server optional] end CP -.->|optional pack| DCP ``` **Data flow**: Import/read repo → write `state/ecosystems/`; continuity writes **`.foundry/projects/`** (target); extension calls CLI/API over localhost. --- ## Applicable Principles | Principle | Applies | How | |-----------|---------|-----| | artifact-authority | yes | Schema + `state/` remain authoritative; `.foundry` instance must validate against `continuity-state.schema.json`. | | continuity-is-mandatory | yes | Moving roots must preserve resumable `nextCommandSet` / `doneCriteria`. | | blast-radius-before-build | yes | Ecosystem init walkthrough should order **import → knowledge → gap → plan** before execute-mode runs. | | approval-at-plan-boundary | yes | Extension must not auto-approve real plans without policy match. | | independent-verification | yes | Init/migration changes need tests + verifier pass (`npm test`, `ci:targeted`). | | fix-memory-compounds | partial | Document learnings in guardrails/knowledge when init failures repeat. | --- ## Guardrail Packs - [ ] **Node platform / reliability** — timeouts, no blocking CPU on request threads for control plane in Docker. - [ ] **Security baseline** — no secrets in `.foundry` committed files; bearer tokens for non-loopback API. - [ ] **Browser injection / extension standards** — if extension injects scripts, follow workspace rules for sanitization (usually N/A for CLI-spawning extension). --- ## Docker analysis (architectural recommendation) | Component | Container? | Notes | |---------|------------|--------| | **Orchestrator CLI** | **No** (default) | Runs on host against repo; needs direct filesystem access to `workspaceRoot`. | | **Control plane** | **Optional** | Node HTTP server; Docker useful for **CI smoke** or **team-identical** dev URLs; local dev often `npm run api` on host. Bind mounts for `flagship-foundry-work` if containerized; set **ADR-006** env for tokens. | | **Graph viewer** | **Optional** | If used, static or small Node service—container optional. | | **Foundry MCP server** | **Optional** | Same as control plane—package per `apps/foundry-mcp-server`; Docker only if you need isolated deps. | **Recommendation**: **Do not require Docker** for day-one Foundry adoption. Introduce **optional** `Dockerfile` / compose for **control plane + pinned Node** when teams need reproducible environments or CI integration tests. For **local-shell execute** runs (**ADR-008**), containerizing the *executor* is a **separate** decision (sandbox differs from macOS `sandbox-exec`). --- ## Local Cursor / VS Code extension (feasibility) **Yes, you can build a local extension** (the repo already has `apps/cursor-companion/` as a starting point). Feasible capabilities: - Commands: **“Initialize Foundry project”**, **“Re-import ecosystem”**, **“Start control plane”** (spawn terminal or `child_process`). - Configuration: `flagshipFoundry.repoRoot`, `flagshipFoundry.importConfigPath`, `flagshipFoundry.controlPlaneUrl`. - Run **CLI** with explicit args: `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs import <config>`, `init-project`, `scaffold-env`, etc. - Optional: HTTP `GET /health` before dependent actions. **Limitations**: “**CursorCLI**” as a product-specific CLI is not something this repo defines—extensions use the **VS Code extension API** + **terminal subprocess**. Cannot rely on undocumented Cursor internals. **Re-init** of skills/agents should mean **copying or merging templates** from `knowledge/`, `.cursor/skills/`, `environments/` with user confirmation (**ADR-004**). --- ## Step-by-step: Initialize Foundry into an ecosystem (walkthrough summary) *Full operator doc should be extracted to `docs/guides/` in implement phase; this is the intent-level sequence.* 1. **Prereqs**: Node 20+, `cd flagship-foundry-work`, `npm install`. 2. **Create import config** with `source.type: "filesystem"` and `workspaceRoot` = absolute path to target repo. 3. **Import**: `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs import <config.json>` → verify `state/ecosystems/<ecosystemId>/`. 4. **Knowledge** (optional but recommended): prepare manifest under `examples/knowledge-sources/` pattern; `knowledge <manifest.json>`. 5. **Gap**: `gap` with request JSON referencing `ecosystemId` and `knowledgeBaseId` as needed. 6. **Plan**: `plan` with change request JSON; review approval policy. 7. **Continuity**: `init-project <name> <objective>` — **after `.foundry` migration**, this writes under **`.foundry/projects/<name>/`** (today: still `.codex` until implementation). 8. **Control plane** (optional): `npm run api` with env per README; use REST or Cursor companion. 9. **Agents / skills / pipeline**: wire **existing** repo assets—`.cursor/rules`, `.cursor/skills`, `knowledge/` packs, `runbooks/`, and CI per `docs/ci-release-gates.md`—rather than a single “agent installer” unless built as extension templates with approval. --- ## Intent Packet Summary - **Phase**: ready for `plan` - **Primary Agent**: `@orchestrator` - **Next Action**: invoke **`/scope-chunker`** to decompose into work orders (schema + continuity + docs + optional extension spike + optional Docker compose) - **Key Decisions Pending**: - Exact **`.foundry` layout** (`projects/` only vs additional `cache/` or `templates/`). - **Migration strategy** for existing `.codex` users (symlink vs one-time copy vs dual-read period). - Whether **import pipeline** should treat **`.foundry/`** as a first-class scan path like `.codex/` for workspace metadata. - **Definition of Ready Met**: **partially** — problem, scope, AC, rollback, and architecture notes are clear; **pending** stakeholder sign-off on breaking schema pattern change and migration policy. --- ## Follow-on artifacts - **ADR-011** (proposed): `docs/adr/adr-011-foundry-directory-layout-and-continuity-instance.md` — canonical `.foundry/projects/<slug>/` layout. - **Scope chunk:** `docs/intent/scope-chunk-foundry-dot-foundry-2026-03-23.md` — work orders WO-FF-011-01 … WO-FF-011-05. ## References - `flagship-foundry-work/schemas/continuity-state.schema.json` — `runtimeInstanceAuthority` pattern - `flagship-foundry-work/packages/core/src/continuity.mjs` — `.codex` path construction - `flagship-foundry-work/docs/adr/adr-002-continuity-schema-authority-and-bootstrap.md` - `flagship-foundry-work/apps/cursor-companion/README.md` - `flagship-foundry-work/docs/ci-release-gates.md`
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/intent/intent-foundry-dot-foundry-ssot-charters-personas-skills-2026-03-23.md===# Intent Packet: `.foundry` as SSOT for Charters, Task Tracking, Personas, and Skills **Date:** 2026-03-23 **Pipeline:** `/define-intent` **Related:** ADR-011 (`.foundry` layout and continuity instance) --- ## Problem Statement - **Problem:** Foundry-related continuity (charters, `current-task.json`), operator personas (“personalities”), and executable skills are split across `.cursor/`, `.claude/`, `.codex/`, and `flagship-foundry-work/` (e.g. `personas/`, `knowledge/`). That fragmentation makes it unclear which copy is authoritative, complicates the Flagship Foundry application when it needs stable paths to read/write state, and forces each CLI environment to duplicate or drift from the same definitions. - **Stakeholder:** Developers and operators running multi-agent SDLC workflows; maintainers of the Flagship Foundry control plane and import/bootstrap pipelines; CLI/agent integrators (Cursor, Codex, Claude Code, future tools). - **Success Outcome:** A single, repo-root **`.foundry/`** tree is the canonical home for Foundry charter, per-project task tracking, persona definitions, and Foundry-owned skills; every environment agent **inherits** those definitions and may only **extend** with thin, documented adapter layers for tool-specific behavior. - **Constraints:** Must align with ADR-002/ADR-011 split (schema authority in `flagship-foundry-work/schemas/`, runtime instance under `.foundry/projects/<slug>/`); avoid silent split-brain with legacy `.codex/projects/**` during migration; no secrets in `.foundry/`; respect existing Nx/workspace boundaries for application code vs metadata. - **Known Risks:** Migration drift if some automation still reads old paths; merge conflicts if multiple agents write continuity concurrently; over-nesting `.foundry/` before consumers exist (per ontology discipline); breaking external docs or scripts that hardcode `.cursor` paths. --- ## Scope - **In Scope:** - Define normative **directory layout** under `.foundry/` for: project charters, `current-task.json` (and schema pointers), **personas** (personalities), and **skills** (executable procedures) used by Foundry and consumed by the Flagship app. - Define an **inheritance model**: base definitions in `.foundry/`; per-environment **optional** overlays (e.g. `.cursor/skills/` → re-export or wrap) documented as non-authoritative extensions. - Specify **discovery contract** for the Flagship Foundry application (which paths to index, validation against schemas). - **Rollback and migration** story: symlink, copy, or dual-read period; update rules/docs that reference legacy locations. - **Non-Goals:** - Moving the entire monorepo’s generic Cursor rules (unrelated to Foundry) into `.foundry/`. - Replacing every third-party CLI’s global config; only repo-local agent behavior tied to Foundry. - Re-implementing the control plane UI in this intent slice (layout and contracts only unless already scoped elsewhere). --- ## Glossary | Term | Definition | |------|------------| | **SSOT** | Single source of truth: one canonical path and format; other locations are mirrors, overlays, or deprecated. | | **`.foundry/`** | Repo-root namespace for Foundry-owned metadata and configuration instances (per ADR-011). | | **Continuity instance** | Machine-readable task state (e.g. `current-task.json`) bound to a project slug. | | **Charter** | Human-facing project SDLC constraints (`SDLC_CHARTER.md`) paired with continuity. | | **Persona** | Structured agent personality/profile (role, tone, constraints) used to steer specialist behavior. | | **Skill** | Executable procedure (e.g. markdown skill with steps) invoked by agents. | | **Environment agent** | A CLI or IDE-integrated agent (Cursor, Codex, Claude Code) that loads repo-local definitions. | | **Adapter / overlay** | Thin layer in a tool-specific folder that imports or wraps `.foundry` definitions without copying content. | | **Flagship Foundry application** | The workspace’s Foundry tooling (e.g. control plane, import pipeline) that reads artifacts under agreed paths. | | **Authority (contract)** | JSON Schema and ontology location under `flagship-foundry-work/schemas/` (and related), per ADR-002. | --- ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] Given a repository with `.foundry/projects/<slug>/` populated, when the Flagship Foundry app or documented CLI resolves project state, then **charter and `current-task.json` paths** are read from `.foundry/projects/<slug>/` without requiring `.codex/` for Foundry authority. - [ ] Given persona and skill definitions committed under `.foundry/` (exact subpaths documented in a short README or ADR addendum), when an environment agent is configured per the handoff doc, then it **loads base personality and procedures from `.foundry/`** before applying any local extension. - [ ] Given two environments (e.g. Cursor and Claude Code), when both are used on the same repo, then **behavioral drift from duplicated persona/skill text** is eliminated for Foundry-scoped content (one canonical text in `.foundry/`). - [ ] Given a breaking path change, when operators follow the rollback section, then the repo can **revert to prior path resolution** (e.g. dual-read flag or symlink) without data loss. - [ ] Given the import/bootstrap pipeline runs, when it classifies workspace files, then `.foundry/**` is **discoverable and labeled** as Foundry metadata (not conflated with unrelated app source). --- ## Rollback Plan - Keep **legacy read paths** for one transition window (dual-read: try `.foundry` first, fall back to `.codex/projects/**` for continuity only), with explicit deprecation warnings in logs or import reports. - Prefer **copy + verify** over destructive moves; use symlinks only where the team accepts cross-OS constraints. - Revert application and rule changes via git; continuity JSON remains valid against the same schema—only **path strings** in `authority` or docs change. - If persona/skill consolidation causes tooling breakage, restore thin **stub files** in legacy locations that only point to `.foundry/` paths (forwarding stubs), then remove in a follow-up slice. --- ## System Context Diagram Trust boundaries: human operators and local CLIs run inside the **dev workstation**; the **Git repo** holds `.foundry/` and app code; external registry or cloud is out of scope unless already integrated. ```mermaid C4Context title System Context: Foundry SSOT and Environment Agents Person(developer, "Developer / Operator", "Runs agents and Foundry tooling") Person(maintainer, "Maintainer", "Owns schemas, layouts, and migrations") System_Boundary(repo, "Git repository") { System(foundry, ".foundry/ (SSOT)", "Charters, continuity, personas, skills") System(flagship, "Flagship Foundry application", "Control plane, import pipeline, state") } System_Ext(cli, "CLI agents (Cursor / Codex / Claude)", "Load repo-local definitions") Rel(developer, cli, "Invokes", "IDE / terminal") Rel(developer, flagship, "Configures / runs", "local HTTP / CLI") Rel(cli, foundry, "Reads canonical", "file://") Rel(flagship, foundry, "Reads / writes", "file://") Rel(maintainer, foundry, "Commits layout & content", "git") Rel(maintainer, flagship, "Ships consumers", "code") UpdateLayoutConfig($c4ShapeInRow="3", $c4BoundaryInRow="1") ``` --- ## Container Diagram ```mermaid C4Container title Container: Foundry SSOT in Repo Person(dev, "Developer", "") System_Boundary(repo, "Repository") { Container(foundryTree, ".foundry/", "FS / git", "Charters, projects/*, personas, skills") Container(app, "flagship-foundry-work apps", "Node", "Control plane, pipelines") Container(schemas, "schemas + ontology", "JSON Schema", "Contracts (authority separate from instance)") } Container_Boundary(agents, "Environment agents") { Container(cursorAdapters, "Cursor adapters", ".cursor/", "Rules/skills that wrap .foundry") Container(otherAdapters, "Other CLI adapters", ".claude/ / .codex/", "Optional thin overlays") } Rel(dev, app, "Uses", "CLI / UI") Rel(dev, cursorAdapters, "Uses", "IDE") Rel(app, foundryTree, "Reads/writes project state", "POSIX paths") Rel(app, schemas, "Validates", "AJV / internal") Rel(cursorAdapters, foundryTree, "Inherits base", "read-only preferred") Rel(otherAdapters, foundryTree, "Inherits base", "read-only preferred") Rel(foundryTree, schemas, "Conforms to", "instance → contract refs") ``` **Data flow notes:** Writes to `current-task.json` should go through the same validation as today; persona/skill files are typically human-reviewed git content (public/internal; no secrets). --- ## Applicable Principles Reference: `flagship-foundry-work/ontology/principle-catalog.json`. | Principle | Applies | How | |-----------|---------|-----| | **artifact-authority** | yes | Canonical personas, skills, and continuity live as committed artifacts under `.foundry/`, not ad-hoc chat. | | **blast-radius-before-build** | yes | Migration touches rules, pipelines, and multiple agent folders; enumerate affected paths before implementation. | | **approval-at-plan-boundary** | yes | Layout and migration plans should follow existing plan/approval flows in Foundry. | | **independent-verification** | yes | Verifier still validates against acceptance criteria; SSOT does not merge builder/verifier roles. | | **continuity-is-mandatory** | yes | Task tracking remains resumable; paths update in continuity and derived mirrors as needed. | | **fix-memory-compounds** | partial | Optional: record migration pitfalls as guardrails or fix-memory entries after cutover. | *Thematic alignment (from ontology discipline): **contract-first** — schemas and README specify layout before bulk file moves; **observed-vs-declared-truth** — runtime state in `current-task.json` remains declared continuity; import reports reflect observed disk state.* --- ## Guardrail Packs Reference: `flagship-foundry-work/guardrails/` - [ ] **guardrail:workspace-governance** — Artifacts outrank chat; blast radius and handoff explicit; continuity updates on phase transitions. - [ ] **guardrail:terminal-agent-adapters** — Adapter layers stay thin; no duplication of Foundry-canonical text outside `.foundry/` without a forwarding stub. - [ ] **guardrail:nx-monorepo** — Application code changes stay in correct projects; `.foundry/` remains metadata-friendly for Nx boundaries. - [ ] **guardrail:typescript-core** — If validation or loaders are TypeScript, keep strict typing at boundaries. *(Add **guardrail:chrome-extension-mv3** / **guardrail:web-frontend** only if skills or personas embed extension/UI-specific rules in this slice.)* --- ## Intent Packet Summary - **Phase:** ready for `plan` - **Primary Agent:** @orchestrator - **Next Action:** Invoke `/scope-chunker` with this packet to decompose into work orders (schema/path updates, `.foundry` README, adapter stubs, dual-read migration, Flagship discovery, test updates). - **Key Decisions Pending:** - Exact subpaths under `.foundry/` for `personas/` and `skills/` (flat vs `projects/<slug>/`-scoped personas). - Whether environment overlays remain as symlinks, `import` re-exports, or generated stubs from a manifest. - Dual-read duration and telemetry for deprecated `.codex` Foundry paths. - **Definition of Ready Met:** **Partially** — problem, scope, diagrams, principles, and rollback are defined; **pending** final agreement on subdirectory layout and stub mechanism for non-Foundry Cursor rules (explicitly out of scope for moving, but interaction must be clear). --- ## run targeted tests - **Rollback Notes:** Restore stubs pointing to `.foundry/` - **Approval Required:** yes (high blast radius) --- ## Work Order: wo-004-agent-adapters - **Lifecycle Stage:** implement - **Phase ID:** `foundry-ssot-adapters` - **Task Class:** `deterministic_transformation` - **Agent Role:** builder - **Model Tier:** low_cost_executor - **File Scope:** `.cursor/rules/**` (only lines referencing Foundry paths); `.cursor/agents/*` if needed; `.claude/` mirror if repo uses it - **Constraints:** terminal-agent-adapters - **Acceptance Criteria:** - [ ] Cursor/Claude agents document inheritance from `.foundry/` - **Verification Plan:** Manual smoke: agent loads without missing file errors - **Rollback Notes:** Restore previous rule text - **Approval Required:** no --- ## Work Order: wo-005-flagship-discovery - **Lifecycle Stage:** implement - **Phase ID:** `foundry-ssot-control-plane` - **Task Class:** `deterministic_transformation` - **Agent Role:** builder - **Model Tier:** low_cost_executor - **File Scope:** `flagship-foundry-work/apps/control-plane/src/server.mjs` (or relevant modules); import pipeline if indexing `.foundry` - **Constraints:** workspace-governance - **Acceptance Criteria:** - [ ] Control plane discovers `.foundry` project state and new persona/skill roots if in scope - **Verification Plan:** Unit/integration tests for path resolution - **Rollback Notes:** Feature flag or config flag to old paths - **Approval Required:** no --- ## Work Order: wo-006-verify - **Lifecycle Stage:** verify - **Phase ID:** `foundry-ssot-verify` - **Task Class:** `verification` - **Agent Role:** verifier - **Model Tier:** balanced_reasoner - **File Scope:** Evidence bundle only (tests + grep + import report) - **Acceptance Criteria:** All intent acceptance criteria checked - **Verification Plan:** Run full `nextCommandSet` from `current-task.json` when available; else Nx affected as per orchestrator rule - **Rollback Notes:** N/A - **Approval Required:** no --- ## Scope Chunk Summary - **Total Work Orders:** 6 - **Estimated Phases:** layout decision (wo-001) → schema + continuity (wo-002) → content migration (wo-003) → adapters (wo-004) → control plane (wo-005) → verify (wo-006) - **Critical Path:** wo-001 → wo-002 → wo-003 → wo-006 (wo-004/005 can parallelize after wo-001) --- ## Principle Card Attachments - **artifact-authority:** wo-0003, wo-004 (no duplicated canonical prose) - **blast-radius-before-build:** wo-001 (inventory before moves) - **continuity-is-mandatory:** wo-002 (phase transitions update state) --- ## Open Questions (blockers for wo-003) 1. **Subpaths:** e.g. `.foundry/personas/*.json` vs `.foundry/projects/<slug>/personas/*.json` 2. **Skills format:** single tree `.foundry/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` vs manifest-generated stubs 3. **Dual-read window:** duration and logging for `.codex` fallback
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/INTERACTIVE_DRILLDOWN_AND_DEBATE.md===# Interactive Drilldown and Debate ## Drilldown model Foundry should let a human start from an ecosystem view and narrow into: - system; - project; - module or component; - rule pack; - task state; - environment contract; - focused blast-radius slice. The current minimum slice implements the first technical step: a focus-view generator that builds a Mermaid drilldown from a query and the current ecosystem graph. ## Debate model For risky or architecture-shaping work, the plan should not jump from inspect to code. The current review policy model supports: - proposal; - adversarial challenge rounds; - reconciliation memos; - implementation only after the debate has stabilized the blast radius. ## Why this exists This is the bridge between static diagrams and trustworthy implementation. The goal is not only to visualize impact, but to force hidden dependencies, rollout issues, and sibling drift to surface before code is written.
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/KNOWLEDGE_BASE_ARCHITECTURE.md===# Knowledge Base Architecture ## Design goals - version documentation sources instead of treating them as transient prompt context; - preserve source lineage for every document chunk; - align retrieval to packs, frameworks, platforms, personas, and runbooks; - support future framework-specific skill generation from the same source base. ## Primary artifacts - `knowledge/catalogs/domain-packs.json` - `knowledge/catalogs/framework-registry.json` - `knowledge/catalogs/source-presets.json` - `knowledge/templates/agent-blueprints/` - `knowledge/templates/skill-blueprints/` - `state/knowledge/<knowledgeBaseId>/manifest.json` - `state/knowledge/<knowledgeBaseId>/documents/index.json` - `state/knowledge/<knowledgeBaseId>/coverage-report.md` ## Retrieval posture Retrieval should happen in layers: 1. identify the ecosystem and impacted pack set; 2. narrow by framework or platform; 3. narrow by persona or runbook phase; 4. retrieve only the documents needed for the current planning or execution step. This keeps context small and makes low-cost microtask agents viable.
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/LARGE_CODEBASE_STRATEGY.md===# Large Codebase Strategy ## Problem The ultimate product must operate over codebases too large to fit inside a context window. ## Core response The system should reason over a **graph + registry + evidence model**, not over raw file dumps. ## Required layers ### 1. Repository registration Know which repositories, modules, runtimes, owners, and contracts exist. ### 2. Structural index Track symbols, files, APIs, events, data stores, deployments, and dependencies. ### 3. Contract registry Keep schemas, APIs, events, and interface boundaries first-class. ### 4. Work-order narrowing Each task sees only: - the relevant graph neighborhood, - the relevant contracts, - the relevant runbook, - the relevant guardrail pack, - the relevant file slice. ### 5. Evidence and continuity Completed work updates: - graph edges and properties, - evidence bundles, - continuity state, - fix memory, - evolution events. ## Versioning strategy ### Public history Keep a clean, reviewable Git history for externally visible engineering work. ### Internal evolution ledger Also track a more granular event stream for: - work-order execution - evidence outcomes - graph mutations - handoffs - learning captures Git remains the default source for code history, but the evolution ledger can be backed by another store later. The key is that the orchestration model is not Git-only even if Git is the first backend.
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/LOCAL_MODEL_GUIDE.md===# Local and Remote Model Guide ## Goal Use low-cost models for bounded microtasks and preserve expensive models for ambiguity-heavy reasoning. ## Supported host patterns ### 1. Local laptop host - best for personal development - lowest latency - ideal for deterministic executors and low-cost code transforms ### 2. Remote workstation or Windows machine on the LAN/VPN - useful when a stronger GPU is available elsewhere - good for team-shared executor backends - requires explicit host, auth, and routing policy ### 3. Dedicated inference server - best for high-throughput execution or larger local models - useful for future team and marketplace scenarios ## Backend recommendations ### Ollama Use Ollama when you want quick local setup and a broad integration ecosystem. Treat it as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint where possible. ### vLLM Use vLLM when you want a more explicit server deployment model, higher throughput, or larger hosted models with OpenAI-compatible APIs. ## Example provider patterns ### Local Ollama - base URL: `http://localhost:11434/v1` - auth key can be a placeholder for OpenAI-compatible clients ### Remote Ollama on a Windows machine - install Ollama on Windows - set `OLLAMA_HOST` so the service binds to the network interface you intend to expose - protect access with network controls, reverse proxy, or VPN/tailnet - if browser-based tools need access, allow the correct origins with `OLLAMA_ORIGINS` ### Remote vLLM - start `vllm serve <model>` on the remote host - expose the OpenAI-compatible endpoint on a controlled network path - register the host as `provider:openai-compatible-remote` ## Routing guidance - use local/remote low-cost backends for deterministic transformation, formatting, sync, and repetitive generation; - use stronger cloud or high-capability backends for architectural reasoning, failure diagnosis, and policy-heavy verification; - keep provider choice out of runbooks and encode it in routing policy. ## Operational safety - never expose local model hosts to the open internet without an authenticated gateway; - prefer VPN/tailnet or internal network routing; - treat every remote host as production infrastructure once it becomes a shared executor.
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/LOW_LEVEL_MODEL_TRAINING_GUIDE.md===# Low-Level Model Training Guide ## Objective Train a smaller executor-oriented model or adapter so recurring implementation and remediation patterns become cheaper and faster. ## What to train on Do not train first on raw chat logs. Train on structured artifacts: - fix-memory records - work orders and their outcomes - evidence bundles - guardrail packs - accepted diffs and rejected diffs - incident-to-remediation chains ## Recommended data units ### 1. Work-order examples Input: - task class - constraints - file/component scope - relevant contracts Output: - bounded implementation or analysis artifact ### 2. Fix-memory examples Input: - problem summary - environment - symptoms - root cause Output: - validated remediation pattern and prevention rules ### 3. Guardrail-aware transformations Input: - language/platform/cloud guardrails - narrow objective Output: - compliant microtask result ## Training sequence ### Phase A: corpus curation - normalize fix-memory and work-order outcomes into JSONL - exclude low-confidence or unresolved incidents - label by task class, language, platform, and risk ### Phase B: SFT / adapter training - start with parameter-efficient adaptation rather than full fine-tuning - prioritize LoRA/QLoRA style adaptation for small-to-mid models - keep training artifacts versioned and reproducible ### Phase C: evaluation Evaluate on: - exactness to schema - guardrail adherence - regression reproduction and repair quality - token efficiency - false-positive and hallucination rate ### Phase D: distillation and promotion Once the dataset is healthy: - distill larger orchestration outputs into smaller executor models - separate orchestration reasoning from microtask execution - promote only after offline evaluation and shadow-mode validation ## Practical rule The first fine-tuned low-level model should target **one narrow executor lane** such as: - TypeScript refactor microtasks, - regression test generation, - bug-fix pattern matching, - documentation synchronization. Do not try to train the “whole ecosystem model” first.
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/MINIMUM_EXECUTABLE_SLICE.md===# Minimum Executable Slice The minimum slice now proves nine things end to end: 1. import an existing ecosystem from a filesystem workspace or export bundle; 2. build a graph of systems, projects, frameworks, platforms, rules, diagrams, task states, and agent environments; 3. ingest foundational documentation into a versioned knowledge base; 4. analyze knowledge gaps against required domain packs; 5. generate Mermaid visualizations, focus views, and SME profiles; 6. create a plan with manual or auto approval policy; 7. insert debate and reconciliation tasks for risky plans; 8. create and control a run with start, pause, resume, and stop; 9. surface the same flow through a Cursor-compatible companion extension. ## Core commands ```bash npm run bootstrap:full-sample npm run api npm test ``` ## Sample assets - `examples/current-workspace/input/` holds the imported workspace export bundle used for the demo. - `examples/knowledge-sources/input/` holds the seed documentation sources and manifest. - `state/ecosystems/web-automation-workspace/` holds the generated graph, report, visualizations, focus views, and SME profiles. - `state/knowledge/foundry-foundational-docs/` holds the ingested knowledge base and coverage report.
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/PRINCIPLES_ALIGNMENT.md===# Principles Alignment ## Why this matters Domain experts often understand the governing principles of their field better than the exact implementation details of a new stack. The ecosystem should turn those principles into reusable visual and machine-readable artifacts. ## Principle cards A principle card is a structured statement such as: - acceptable complexity budgets, - search/indexing tradeoffs, - consistency models, - safety invariants, - accessibility heuristics, - latency budgets, - privacy or compliance rules. ## How principle cards are used - attached to systems, components, and work orders through the graph - rendered as overlays in diagrams - referenced by personas during questioning and implementation - linked to fix-memory records when principle violations cause bugs ## Example A data-design principle card may state that interactive search paths should not rely on repeated O(n) scans over large collections. Once that principle is attached to a component, future planning and bug analysis should ask whether the current design violates it.
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/PROJECT_HANDOFF.md===# Project Handoff ## What exists now This repository now contains a runnable minimum slice for Foundry as an import-first orchestration system: - a control-plane API under `apps/control-plane/`; - a planner and bootstrap CLI under `apps/orchestrator-cli/`; - a Cursor-compatible companion extension under `apps/cursor-companion/`; - a workspace import pipeline for filesystem and export-bundle ingestion; - a graph of systems, projects, frameworks, platforms, diagrams, task states, and agent environments; - a seed knowledge-base ingestion pipeline with versioned source manifests; - a knowledge-gap analysis pass that maps ecosystems against required domain packs; - a focus-view generator for drill-down blast-radius visualization; - approval-aware and debate-aware plan generation; - simulated run control with start, pause, resume, and stop. ## Where to resume 1. `README.md` 2. `docs/FOUNDRY_KNOWLEDGE_PIPELINE.md` 3. `docs/INTERACTIVE_DRILLDOWN_AND_DEBATE.md` 4. `docs/ENVIRONMENT_PARITY_AND_MIGRATION.md` 5. `state/ecosystems/web-automation-workspace/manifest.json` 6. `state/ecosystems/web-automation-workspace/graph.json` 7. `state/knowledge/foundry-foundational-docs/manifest.json` 8. `state/ecosystems/web-automation-workspace/analysis/gap-report.json` 9. latest files in `state/plans/` and `state/runs/` ## Primary next tranche Implement one real terminal adapter end to end so an approved work order can leave simulation mode, execute in a controlled worktree, emit evidence, update continuity, and write fix-memory artifacts automatically. ## Important doctrine - manual approval is the default plan boundary; - auto approval is a deliberate policy toggle, not an assumption; - blast radius must be wider than changed files when shared patterns are in play; - environment-specific prompts are projections of shared doctrine, not separate truth; - no task is complete without evidence, continuity, and handoff.
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/REPOSITORY_LAYOUT.md===# Repository layout and canonical source ## Canonical application root **`flagship-foundry-work/`** is the canonical root for runnable Flagship Foundry code: control plane, CLI, Cursor companion, MCP server, model gateway, packages, schemas, ontology, and generated `state/`. Open this folder as the VS Code/Cursor workspace when developing or running Foundry. Scripts such as `npm run api` and `npm test` assume the current working directory is `flagship-foundry-work/`. ## Parent workspace (SDLC meta-repo) The enclosing repository (`SDLC - Visual - Workflow - SoftwareEngineering-NewAge`) may contain: - Cursor rules, skills, and SDLC orchestration docs - **`.foundry/projects/<project>/`** — Flagship Foundry **continuity** (`current-task.json`, `SDLC_CHARTER.md`) per **ADR-011** (agent-neutral; not Codex-specific) - Research markdown, plans, and handoff notes at the repo root - A copy of or symlink to `flagship-foundry-work` - Legacy **`.codex/projects/`** may still exist for other tools; Foundry runtime uses **`.foundry/projects/`** for continuity **Doc sync policy:** Product behavior and APIs are defined by code and `flagship-foundry-work/docs/`. Root-level research files are supporting material; when they conflict with `flagship-foundry-work`, **prefer the implementation under `flagship-foundry-work/`** and update research docs when intentionally changing behavior. ## State and artifacts Generated artifacts live under `flagship-foundry-work/state/` (ecosystems, plans, runs, knowledge). Do not commit secrets; treat `state/` as machine-local unless your team policy says otherwise. For canonical-vs-generated-vs-archive classification and sync direction, see [source-of-truth-matrix.md](source-of-truth-matrix.md). ## CI and release evidence Automated gate baseline and release sign-off expectations (ADR-009) are in [ci-release-gates.md](ci-release-gates.md). The repo-root workflow `.github/workflows/flagship-foundry-ci.yml` runs when `flagship-foundry-work/` changes. Operational rollout, rollback, and incident records (ADR-010) are described in [rollout-rollback-incident-model.md](rollout-rollback-incident-model.md); they must link to canonical `state/` artifacts and continuity.
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/ROADMAP.md===# Roadmap ## Phase 0 — Foundation - repository skeleton - core schemas - runbooks - personas - guardrail packs - graph seed - CLI + API slice ## Phase 1 — Real repository onboarding - system registration - repo indexing - graph enrichment - continuity writer ## Phase 2 — Execution bridge - terminal adapter integration - git/worktree envelopes - evidence bundle generation - verifier service ## Phase 3 — Operate and improve - telemetry and incident ingestion - remediation planning - fix-memory automation - evolution ledger ## Phase 4 — Visualization product - graph canvas - orchestration board - production data flow dashboard - animated learning environment experiments ## Phase 5 — IDE shell - terminal-first companion surfaces - Theia-based custom IDE shell - approval and review UX ## Phase 6 — Marketplace and training - persona/guardrail/adapter marketplace - curated training corpus - low-level model promotion workflow
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/rollout-rollback-incident-model.md===# Rollout, rollback, and incident documentation model (ADR-010) This document implements [adr-010-rollout-rollback-and-incident-documentation-model.md](adr/adr-010-rollout-rollback-and-incident-documentation-model.md). It defines **how operator-facing records** relate to **canonical state** under `flagship-foundry-work/state/` and **continuity** under `.codex/projects/<project>/`. ## Principles 1. **State is truth** — Plans, approvals, runs, timelines, and evidence bundles in `state/` are authoritative for what happened. Operational docs **link** to them; they do not replace them. 2. **Runbooks shape process** — Process flow follows [runbook](../schemas/runbook.schema.json) contracts. Primary anchors: - [feature-delivery.runbook.json](../runbooks/feature-delivery.runbook.json) — release-style delivery - [telemetry-driven-improvement.runbook.json](../runbooks/telemetry-driven-improvement.runbook.json) — signal-driven change - [task-handoff.runbook.json](../runbooks/task-handoff.runbook.json) — agent continuity 3. **Continuity closes the loop** — After rollout, rollback, or incident closeout, update `.codex/projects/<project>/current-task.json` (`nextCommandSet`, `doneCriteria`, phase notes) so the next operator or agent can resume deterministically. ## Record types | Record | Purpose | Governing runbook(s) | | --- | --- | --- | | **Rollout** | Planned promotion of a change with verified gates | Feature delivery | | **Rollback** | Controlled reversal or stop at a boundary with retained diagnosis evidence | Feature delivery + M3 isolation/rollback semantics | | **Incident** | Response to an unplanned signal; ties verifier evidence to fix-memory / guardrail proposals | Telemetry-driven improvement + task handoff | ## Minimum linkage — rollout Every rollout record **must** identify: | Field | Description | Example location pattern | | --- | --- | --- | | Plan | Approved work scope | `state/plans/plan-<ecosystem>-<slug>-<id>.json` | | Approval | Decision artifact | `state/approvals/approval-*.json` (as produced by the control plane) | | Run(s) | Execution instances | `state/runs/run-*.json` | | Evidence | Correlated bundle or API ref | `GET /runs/:id/evidence-bundle` or exported bundle JSON | Optional but recommended: CI run URL per [ci-release-gates.md](ci-release-gates.md). ## Minimum linkage — rollback Every rollback record **must** identify: | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | Trigger | Human, verifier failure, policy gate, or telemetry signal | | Boundary | What is rolled back (e.g., plan scope, deployment slice, adapter config) | | Stopping point | Run/task id where execution halted (`pause` / `stop` per M3 semantics) | | Retained evidence | Paths or bundle ids for timeline + task evidence under `state/run-workspaces/<run-id>/` | ## Minimum linkage — incident Every incident record **must** identify: | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | Triggering signal | Alert, test failure, user report, verifier block | | Impacted system | Ecosystem / project / control-plane surface | | Verifier evidence | Test logs, evidence bundle, CI artifact name | | Learning outputs | Proposed fix-memory entry or guardrail update (see `guardrails/`, knowledge packs) | M3 adapter and telemetry evidence (ADR-007/008) are **inputs** to incident and rollback narrative, not optional appendices. ## Go / no-go checklist (M4 closure) A release-style go/no-go **must** confirm: - [ ] Current automated gates per [ci-release-gates.md](ci-release-gates.md) (ADR-009). - [ ] M2/M3 quality signals still valid for the change scope (classification, parity policy, auth boundary, telemetry correlation, adapter isolation)—cite prior verifier notes or bundles. - [ ] Rollout record links plan + approval + run + evidence. - [ ] Continuity updated with `nextCommandSet` and open risks. ## Example stub (copy into an incident ticket or internal doc) ```json { "recordType": "incident", "id": "inc-2026-03-23-example", "triggeringSignal": "Verifier blocked: npm test failure in gap-analysis", "impactedSystem": "flagship-foundry-work packages/core gap analysis", "verifierEvidence": "local: cd flagship-foundry-work && npm test (log path: …)", "runRef": "state/runs/run-….json", "evidenceBundleRef": "/runs/{id}/evidence-bundle", "proposedLearning": "guardrails/telemetry-and-observability.json review", "continuityUpdate": ".codex/projects/flagship-foundry/current-task.json" } ``` ## Related - [ci-release-gates.md](ci-release-gates.md) — blocking CI and evidence threshold - [source-of-truth-matrix.md](source-of-truth-matrix.md) — artifact classes - [NEXT_AGENT_EXECUTION_STEPS.md](adr/NEXT_AGENT_EXECUTION_STEPS.md) — agent verification playbook
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/source-of-truth-matrix.md===# Source of Truth Matrix This matrix defines artifact classes, canonical homes, and sync direction under ADR-001 and ADR-003. | Artifact area | Artifact class | Canonical home | Sync direction | ADR references | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Product behavior and runnable contracts (APIs, schemas, executable code) | canonical | `flagship-foundry-work/` and `flagship-foundry-work/docs/` | canonical -> projections only | ADR-001, ADR-003 | | Generated runtime/project state (`state/` plans, runs, graph, knowledge manifests) | generated | `flagship-foundry-work/state/` | canonical inputs -> generated outputs (no reverse authority) | ADR-003 | | Root-level SDLC research/plans outside `flagship-foundry-work/` | archive | Parent workspace root research locations | canonical -> archive snapshots/promotions only | ADR-001, ADR-003 | | Deprecated/iterative copies retained for rollback or audit | archive | Team-defined archive locations with retention policy | canonical -> archive only; no archive -> canonical promotion without curation | ADR-003 | | CI workflow definitions and gate scripts (blocking automation contract) | canonical | `.github/workflows/flagship-foundry-ci.yml` (parent repo root) + `flagship-foundry-work/package.json` scripts | canonical -> CI truth; no silent waiver of documented gates | ADR-001, ADR-009 | | CI run artifacts (logs, uploaded `ci-gate-evidence.txt`) | generated | GitHub Actions / CI provider | CI inputs -> retained outputs for audit; not behavior authority | ADR-009 | | Operational rollout / rollback / incident records (tickets, postmortems) | archive or generated | Team tracker + `docs/rollout-rollback-incident-model.md` pattern | Must link to canonical `state/` + continuity; never override product state | ADR-001, ADR-010 | ## Notes - Canonical sources are the only authority for behavior-changing decisions. - Generated artifacts are reproducible outputs and are not manually authoritative. - Archive artifacts are historical references retained per ADR-003 retention rules.
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/TERMINAL_AGENT_SUPPORT.md===# Terminal Agent Support ## Principle Terminal environments are adapters around the same core contracts: - change request - work order - graph patch - evidence bundle - continuity state - fix memory ## Expected adapter responsibilities Each terminal adapter should know how to: - read a work order - narrow file and artifact scope - launch the target environment - capture outputs as typed artifacts - update continuity and evidence on completion ## Target environments ### Codex Strong fit for parallel tasking, worktrees, MCP integration, and a single account across app/editor/terminal surfaces. ### Claude Code Strong fit for local tool use and MCP-based tool extension. Useful as a high-signal interactive supervisor or focused executor. ### Gemini CLI Useful as an open-source terminal agent with built-in tools and MCP support. Treat it as an adapter with some evolving MCP semantics. ### OpenClaw Useful as a gateway-centric orchestrator and plugin/skill platform when you want long-lived sessions, remote nodes, or a broader assistant environment. ### Local OpenAI-compatible hosts Use for inexpensive executors and repeatable microtasks. ## Adapter design rule Never encode business logic in the adapter. Keep the adapter thin and keep the orchestration intelligence in the control plane.
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/docs/VERSIONING_AND_EVOLUTION.md===# Versioning and Evolution ## Goal Support both a clean public-facing history and a richer internal execution history. ## Public-facing history Use Git for: - source code - documentation - contracts - diagrams - user-visible changes This history should stay reviewable and phase-scoped. ## Internal evolution history Track a more granular evolution ledger for: - work-order start and completion - graph patch application - evidence bundle creation - handoff publication - fix-memory creation - provider/adapter decisions ## Why both are needed Git is excellent for code review and release history, but it is not a complete representation of orchestration behavior. The evolution ledger makes it possible to understand how the system itself changed task by task even when those changes should not all appear as separate public commits. ## Interchangeability rule Git is the first backend, not the only possible backend. The architecture should allow other versioning or event-storage backends later without changing the work-order model.
