**Recursive Search**: Finds all `.md` files in the specified folder and subfolders - **Duplicate Prevention**: Automatically deletes existing master files to prevent duplication - **Organized Output**: Creates `master-{folder-name}-documentation.md` in the target folder - **Structured Content**: Each file becomes a numbered section with file path reference - **Error Handling**: Continues processing even if individual files have errors ### Example ```bash # Generate master documentation for Chrome Extension API docs node generate-master-documentation.cjs chrome-ext-api # This creates: chrome-ext-api/master-chrome-ext-api-documentation.md ``` ### Output Structure The generated master file includes: - Header with generation timestamp and file count - Numbered sections for each `.md` file - File path references for each section - Original content from each file - Section separators between files ### Testing The script has been tested on the `chrome-ext-api` folder containing 70 `.md` files (1 root + 69 in subfolder), successfully generating a 30,000+ line master documentation file. ==== FILE: docx-generation-export/README.md ==== # DOCX Generation Modules Standalone extraction of the DOCX generation modules and supporting components from the patient-record-generation app. Generates Microsoft Word (.docx) documents from encounter JSON records with configurable styles, headers, and page layout. ## Contents - **src/docx/** – Core DOCX generation - `docx-generator.ts` – Main generator (Document, sections, numbering, header) - `docx-styles.ts` – Style config (title, headings, body, field label/value, header table, page margins) - `docx-header.ts` – Header table (patient info, DOB, MRN, column widths, borders) - `index.ts` – Public API - **src/types/encounter-types.ts** – TypeScript types (EncounterRecord, Block, DocxStyleConfig, EncounterHeader, etc.) - **src/cli/generate-docx.ts** – CLI for single file, patient folder, or batch ## Install ```bash cd docx-generation-export npm install # or: pnpm install ``` ## Usage ### Programmatic ```ts import { generateDocx, createDocxGenerator, DEFAULT_DOCX_STYLE_CONFIG } from './src/docx/index.js'; import type { EncounterRecord } from './src/types/encounter-types.js'; const encounter: EncounterRecord = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('encounter.json', 'utf-8')); const buffer = await generateDocx(encounter, { includeHeader: true }); fs.writeFileSync('output.docx', buffer); ``` ### CLI ```bash # Single file npx tsx src/cli/generate-docx.ts --input=path/to/encounter.json # Custom output npx tsx src/cli/generate-docx.ts --input=encounter.json --output=out.docx # All JSONs in a patient folder (expects patient folder to have encounters/ subdir) npx tsx src/cli/generate-docx.ts --patient=patient-12345 # All patient folders (default base: output/Bravado-Unified-Patient-Folders) npx tsx src/cli/generate-docx.ts --all # Help npx tsx src/cli/generate-docx.ts --help ``` ## Encounter JSON shape Input JSON must be an `IDEEncounterRecord` or `MMEEncounterRecord`: `schemaVersion`, `encounter`, `patient`, `provider`, `clinical`, `header` (with `table.rows`), and `blocks` (title, heading, paragraph, bullets). See `src/types/encounter-types.ts` for full definitions. ## Dependencies - **docx** (^8.6.0) – Word document generation - **tsx** (dev) – Run TypeScript CLI - **typescript** (dev) – Build ## License Same as the source workspace. ==== FILE: libs/cursor-flow/README.md ==== # Cursor Flow - Web Automation Made Easy A comprehensive web automation system for creating, editing, and managing automated workflows with AI assistance. ## 🚀 Features - **🎯 Visual Flow Editor**: Create and edit automation flows with a user-friendly interface - **🤖 AI-Powered**: Generate flows automatically using AI models - **📦 Staging & Promotion**: Test flows in staging before promoting to production - **🔧 Step Management**: Add, edit, move, and delete individual steps - **🎨 Element Picker**: Visually select elements on web pages - **📊 Observability**: Comprehensive logging and action tracking - **🔄 Bridge Communication**: Seamless integration with backend platforms ## 📋 Architecture The cursor-flow system consists of several key components: ### Core Components 1. **FlowEditorUI** (`src/ui/FlowEditorUI.ts`) - Main UI component for flow editing - Handles modal display and user interactions - Manages flow state and step editing 2. **FlowEditor** (`src/ui/flow/FlowEditor.ts`) - Core business logic for flow management - Implements the `FlowEditorApi` interface - Handles flow validation and step operations 3. **CursorCLIIntegration** (`src/cursorCLI.ts`) - Interface for AI model integration - Handles flow generation and optimization 4. **StagingWorkflowManager** (`src/stagingWorkflow.ts`) - Manages flow deployment lifecycle - Handles staging, testing, and promotion ### Interface Definition The `FlowEditorApi` interface defines the contract for flow editing operations: ```typescript interface FlowEditorApi { getSteps(): FlowStepDef[] setSteps(steps: FlowStepDef[]): void append(step: FlowStepDef): void loadFlow(flow: Flow): void getFlow(): Flow addStep(step: FlowStep): void moveStep(fromIndex: number, toIndex: number): void validateFlow(): void updateStepLocator(stepIndex: number, locator: any): void saveFlow(): void canRunFlow(): boolean updateContent(content: string): void } ``` ## 🎯 Usage ### Basic Flow Creation 1. **Open Editor**: Click the "Open Editor" button in the main menu 2. **Create Flow**: Click "Create New Flow" to start a new automation 3. **Add Steps**: Use the step editor to add individual actions 4. **Configure Elements**: Use the element picker to select page elements 5. **Save & Test**: Save your flow and test it in the staging environment 6. **Promote**: Move successful flows to production ### Step Types The system supports various step types: - **click**: Click on an element - **type**: Type text into an input field - **select**: Select an option from a dropdown - **goto**: Navigate to a URL - **waitFor**: Wait for an element or condition - **assertVisible**: Assert that an element is visible - **assertText**: Assert that text is present - **iterate**: Repeat steps for multiple elements ### Element Locators Elements can be located using various strategies: - **CSS Selectors**: `.button`, `#element-id` - **Text Content**: Elements containing specific text - **ARIA Roles**: `button`, `textbox`, etc. - **Labels**: Form elements with specific labels - **Placeholders**: Input fields with placeholder text - **Test IDs**: Elements with `data-testid` attributes ## 🔧 Bridge Events The system uses bridge events for communication between the overlay and platform: ### Outgoing Events (from overlay to platform) - `openEditor`: Open the flow editor modal - `saveSteps`: Save flow steps to storage - `runDraft`: Execute the current draft flow - `promoteDraft`: Promote draft to production - `testFlow`: Test flow in staging environment - `generateFlow`: Generate flow using AI ### Incoming Events (from platform to overlay) - `cursorflow:testResults`: Test execution results - `cursorflow:aiSuggestions`: AI-generated step suggestions ## 🧪 Testing ### Running Tests ```bash # Run all tests npm test # Run specific test files npm test FlowEditorUI.spec.ts # Run tests with coverage npm test -- --coverage ``` ### Test Structure - **Unit Tests**: Test individual components in isolation - **Integration Tests**: Test component interactions - **E2E Tests**: Test complete user workflows ## 📊 Observability The system provides comprehensive observability features: ### Action Tracking Every action is tracked with timing information: ``` 🔄 Action started: openEditor at 2025-09-24T00:18:26.727Z ✅ Action completed: openEditor in 150ms ``` ### Bridge Communication Logging All bridge events are logged for debugging: ``` [CursorFlow] 🔓 User clicked Open Editor button [CursorFlow] Bridge function found, calling... 🎯 Handling bridge event: openEditor 🎯 Opening Cursor Flow Editor via bridge event ``` ### Error Handling Errors are caught and logged with context: ``` ❌ Action failed: generateFlow after 3000ms Error: AI service unavailable ``` ## 🚀 Development ### Setting Up Development Environment 1. **Install Dependencies** ```bash npm install ``` 2. **Start Development Server** ```bash npm run dev ``` 3. **Run Tests** ```bash npm test ``` ### Building for Production ```bash npm run build ``` ### Code Quality - **TypeScript**: Strict type checking enabled - **ESLint**: Comprehensive linting rules - **Prettier**: Consistent code formatting - **Husky**: Pre-commit hooks for quality checks ## 📚 API Reference ### FlowStepDef Interface ```typescript interface FlowStepDef { type: FlowStepType locator?: FlowStepLocator value?: string description?: string url?: string state?: string text?: string each?: FlowStepDef[] } ``` ### FlowStepLocator Interface ```typescript interface FlowStepLocator { by: 'css' | 'text' | 'role' | 'label' | 'placeholder' | 'testId' selector?: string text?: string role?: string id?: string } ``` ## 🔒 Security - **CSP Compliance**: All scripts are CSP-compatible - **Input Sanitization**: All user inputs are validated - **XSS Prevention**: Content properly escaped - **Shadow DOM**: UI isolated from page content ## 🤝 Contributing 1. **Fork the repository** 2. **Create a feature branch**: `git checkout -b feature/amazing-feature` 3. **Make your changes** 4. **Add tests**: Ensure comprehensive test coverage 5. **Run the test suite**: `npm test` 6. **Submit a pull request** ## 📄 License This project is licensed under the MIT License - see the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details. ## 🆘 Support For support and questions: 1. **Check the documentation** above 2. **Review the test files** for usage examples 3. **Check the issue tracker** for known issues 4. **Create a new issue** if you find a bug --- **Made with ❤️ for web automation enthusiasts** ==== FILE: libs/Google-Chrome-Extension-Library/README.md ==== # Chrome Extension Library A composable, modular Chrome Extension library for MV3 with pluggable authentication providers and a fluid design system. ## Overview This library provides a foundation for building Chrome Extensions with: - **Modular architecture** - Pick and choose only the modules you need - **Pluggable authentication** - Support for Google, Microsoft, Social, SSO, and Email/password - **MV3 compliant** - Service worker, promises, and modern Chrome APIs - **Fluid design system** - Responsive typography and spacing using `clamp()` and viewport units - **Side panel support** - Optional MV3 side panel UI (Chrome 114+) - **Type-safe** - Full TypeScript support with strict typing - **Observable** - Structured logging, correlation IDs, and metrics ## Library Structure ``` libs/Google-Chrome-Extension-Library/ ├── core/ │ ├── runtime/ # MV3 scaffolding, manifest builder, message bus │ ├── storage/ # chrome.storage wrappers with namespacing │ └── telemetry/ # Structured logging, correlation IDs, metrics ├── ui/ │ └── design-tokens/ # Fluid typography/spacing tokens └── auth/ ├── base/ # AuthProvider interface and registry ├── google/ # Google Identity API provider ├── microsoft/ # Azure AD provider ├── social/ # OAuth2 social providers ├── sso/ # OIDC/SAML providers └── email/ # Email/password provider ``` ## Quick Start ### Installation Import the modules you need: ```typescript import { buildManifest, bootstrapBackground } from '@chrome-ext/core-runtime'; import { ChromeStorage } from '@chrome-ext/core-storage'; import { logger } from '@chrome-ext/core-telemetry'; import { googleProvider } from '@chrome-ext/auth-google'; import { microsoftProvider } from '@chrome-ext/auth-microsoft'; import { registerProviders } from '@chrome-ext/auth-base'; ``` ### Basic Usage #### 1. Build Manifest ```typescript import { buildManifest } from '@chrome-ext/core-runtime'; const manifest = buildManifest({ name: 'My Extension', version: '1.0.0', permissions: ['storage', 'identity'], sidePanel: { defaultPath: 'sidepanel.html', }, oauth2: { clientId: 'your-google-client-id', scopes: ['openid', 'profile', 'email'], }, }); ``` #### 2. Setup Background Service Worker ```typescript import { bootstrapBackground, setupSidePanel } from '@chrome-ext/core-runtime'; bootstrapBackground({ onInstalled: async (details) => { console.log('Extension installed:', details.reason); await setupSidePanel({ openPanelOnActionClick: true, defaultPath: 'sidepanel.html', }); }, }); ``` #### 3. Setup Authentication ```typescript import { registerProviders } from '@chrome-ext/auth-base'; import { googleProvider } from '@chrome-ext/auth-google'; import { microsoftProvider } from '@chrome-ext/auth-microsoft'; const providers = registerProviders( googleProvider({ clientId: 'your-google-client-id', scopes: ['openid', 'profile', 'email'], }), microsoftProvider({ clientId: 'your-microsoft-client-id', scopes: ['openid', 'profile', 'email', 'User.Read'], }), ); // Use providers const googleAuth = providers.find(p => p.id === 'google'); if (googleAuth) { const result = await googleAuth.signIn(); console.log('Signed in:', result.user); } ``` #### 4. Use Storage ```typescript import { ChromeStorage } from '@chrome-ext/core-storage'; const storage = new ChromeStorage('local', 'my-namespace'); await storage.set('key', { value: 'data' }); const value = await storage.get('key'); ``` #### 5. Use Logging ```typescript import { logger } from '@chrome-ext/core-telemetry'; logger.info('User signed in', { userId: '123' }); logger.error('Sign-in failed', error, { provider: 'google' }); ``` ## Design Tokens Import the CSS file to use fluid design tokens: ```html <link rel="stylesheet" href="path/to/tokens.css"> ``` Tokens include: - **Fluid typography** using `clamp()` (H1, H2, H3, body, subtext, caption) - **Fluid spacing** (8-pt system with clamped values) - **Safe-area support** for mobile devices - **Container query units** for resizable panes - **Touch targets** (minimum 44×44px) ## Authentication Providers ### Google Uses MV3 Identity API (`chrome.identity.getAuthToken`): ```typescript import { googleProvider } from '@chrome-ext/auth-google'; const provider = googleProvider({ clientId: 'your-client-id', scopes: ['openid', 'profile', 'email'], }); const result = await provider().signIn(); ``` **Required manifest:** ```json { "oauth2": { "client_id": "your-client-id", "scopes": ["openid", "profile", "email"] }, "permissions": ["identity"] } ``` ### Microsoft Uses `chrome.identity.launchWebAuthFlow` with PKCE: ```typescript import { microsoftProvider } from '@chrome-ext/auth-microsoft'; const provider = microsoftProvider({ clientId: 'your-client-id', tenant: 'common', // or your tenant ID scopes: ['openid', 'profile', 'email', 'User.Read'], }); const result = await provider().signIn(); ``` ## Module Boundaries Libraries follow Nx module boundaries: - `core/*` - Runtime utilities (can be used by all) - `ui/*` - UI components and tokens (can be used by features) - `auth/*` - Authentication providers (can be used by features) ## Testing Each library includes test configuration: ```bash nx test chrome-ext-core-runtime nx test chrome-ext-auth-google ``` ## Contributing When adding new providers or modules: 1. Follow the existing structure 2. Implement the `AuthProvider` interface for auth providers 3. Export through `src/index.ts` 4. Add proper TypeScript types 5. Include tests ## Documentation - [Provider Selection Guide](./docs/PROVIDER_GUIDE.md) - Choose and configure auth providers - [Manifest Configuration](./docs/MANIFEST_CONFIG.md) - Complete manifest setup guide - [Troubleshooting](./docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) - Common issues and solutions - [API Reference](./docs/API_REFERENCE.md) - Complete API documentation - [Operations Runbook](./docs/RUNBOOK.md) - Deployment and operations procedures ## Testing Run tests for all libraries: ```bash # Unit tests nx test chrome-ext-core-runtime nx test chrome-ext-auth-google # All tests nx run-many -t test --all ``` ## License MIT ==== FILE: libs/web-documentation/README.md ==== # Web Documentation Scraper A TypeScript library for scraping documentation websites and converting them to clean Markdown format. ## Features - **HTTP Scraping**: Robust web page fetching with retry logic and timeouts - **HTML to Markdown**: Intelligent conversion preserving structure and formatting - **File Output**: Batch writing of documentation files with customizable naming - **CLI Tool**: Command-line interface for easy usage - **TypeScript**: Full type safety and modern ES modules ## Installation This library is part of the monorepo. To use it: ```bash # Build the library pnpm nx build web-documentation # Run the CLI pnpm nx run web-documentation:scrape -- <urls...> ``` ## Usage ### CLI Usage ```bash # Basic usage pnpm nx run web-documentation:scrape -- https://docs.example.com/api # Multiple URLs with custom output directory pnpm nx run web-documentation:scrape -- \ https://docs.example.com/api \ https://docs.example.com/guide \ --output-dir ./documentation # With numbered filenames pnpm nx run web-documentation:scrape -- \ https://docs.example.com/api \ --output-dir ./docs \ --numbered # Use browser automation for dynamic API documentation pnpm nx run web-documentation:scrape -- \ https://api.example.com/docs \ --browser \ --headed \ --output-dir ./api-docs ``` ### Programmatic Usage ```typescript import { DocumentationScraper, MarkdownConverter, FileWriter } from '@mm/web-documentation'; // Initialize components const scraper = new DocumentationScraper({ userAgent: 'My-Scraper/1.0.0', timeout: 30000, }); const converter = new MarkdownConverter({ includeCodeExamples: true, includeApiReference: true, includeToc: true, }); const writer = new FileWriter(); // Scrape, convert, and save const urls = [ 'https://docs.zoominfo.com/reference/overview', 'https://docs.zoominfo.com/reference/searchinterface_searchcontact', ]; const pages = await scraper.scrapePages(urls); const docs = pages.map(page => converter.convert(page)); await writer.writeFiles(docs, './documentation-3rd-party/Zoom-Info-API'); ``` ## API Reference ### DocumentationScraper ```typescript class DocumentationScraper { constructor(options?: ScraperOptions); scrapePage(url: string): Promise<DocumentationPage>; scrapePages(urls: string[]): Promise<DocumentationPage[]>; } ``` ### MarkdownConverter ```typescript class MarkdownConverter { constructor(options?: ConverterOptions); convert(page: DocumentationPage): ScrapedDocumentation; } ``` ### FileWriter ```typescript class FileWriter { writeFile(doc: ScrapedDocumentation, outputPath: string): Promise<void>; writeFiles(docs: ScrapedDocumentation[], outputDir: string, filenamePattern?: Function): Promise<void>; } ``` ## Configuration Options ### ScraperOptions - `userAgent?: string` - Custom user agent string - `timeout?: number` - Request timeout in milliseconds (default: 30000) - `maxRetries?: number` - Maximum retry attempts (default: 3) - `retryDelay?: number` - Base delay between retries in milliseconds (default: 1000) - `useBrowser?: boolean` - Use browser automation for dynamic content (default: false) - `browserWaitTime?: number` - Wait time for dynamic content in milliseconds (default: 5000) - `headless?: boolean` - Run browser in headless mode (default: true) ### ConverterOptions - `includeCodeExamples?: boolean` - Include code blocks in output (default: true) - `includeApiReference?: boolean` - Include API reference sections (default: true) - `includeToc?: boolean` - Generate table of contents (default: true) - `frontmatter?: object` - Additional frontmatter metadata ## Output Format Each scraped page is converted to Markdown with frontmatter: ```markdown --- title: "Contacts" url: "https://docs.zoominfo.com/reference/searchinterface_searchcontact" scrapedAt: "2025-12-19T10:00:00.000Z" lastModified: "2025-12-19T09:00:00.000Z" --- # Contacts ## Overview This endpoint allows you to search for contacts... ``` ## ZoomInfo API Documentation This library was specifically designed to scrape ZoomInfo API documentation. The following URLs are commonly scraped: - `https://docs.zoominfo.com/reference/overview` - API Overview - `https://docs.zoominfo.com/reference/searchinterface_searchcontact` - Contacts Search - `https://docs.zoominfo.com/reference/enrichinterface_enrichcontact` - Contacts Enrichment - `https://docs.zoominfo.com/reference/lookupinterface_lookup` - Data Lookup - `https://docs.zoominfo.com/reference/userinterface_userusage` - Usage Data ### Example Command ```bash pnpm nx run web-documentation:scrape -- \ https://docs.zoominfo.com/reference/overview \ https://docs.zoominfo.com/reference/searchinterface_searchcontact \ https://docs.zoominfo.com/reference/enrichinterface_enrichcontact \ https://docs.zoominfo.com/reference/lookupinterface_lookup \ https://docs.zoominfo.com/reference/userinterface_userusage \ --output-dir documentation-3rd-party/Zoom-Info-API \ --numbered ``` This will create files like: - `001-overview.md` - `002-searchinterface_searchcontact.md` - `003-enrichinterface_enrichcontact.md` - `004-lookupinterface_lookup.md` - `005-userinterface_userusage.md` ## Dependencies - `jsdom` - HTML parsing and DOM manipulation - `tsx` - TypeScript execution for CLI ## Development ```bash # Build pnpm nx build web-documentation # Test pnpm nx test web-documentation # Lint pnpm nx lint web-documentation # Type check pnpm nx typecheck web-documentation ``` ## Error Handling The scraper includes robust error handling: - **Network failures**: Automatic retries with exponential backoff - **Invalid HTML**: Graceful fallback to basic text extraction - **Missing content**: Clear error messages for debugging - **Rate limiting**: Respects delays between requests ## Contributing 1. Follow the monorepo's TypeScript and ESLint standards 2. Add tests for new functionality 3. Update documentation for API changes 4. Use conventional commits for changes ==== FILE: README.md ==== ## Cursor Flow (Select → Describe → Apply → Test → Promote) Install Cursor CLI: ```bash curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash ``` Usage (default TARGET_APP=kareo): ```bash nx run kareo:dev:watch node tools/cursor/feature-bridge.cjs ``` In the app UI: 1. Go to [https://script.google.com/](https://script.google.com/) 2. Click **"New Project"** 3. Name your project (e.g., "IDE JSON to Docs Converter") ### Step 2: Copy the Script 1. Open `ide-json-to-docs.gs` from this repository 2. Copy the entire contents 3. Paste into the Google Apps Script editor (replacing any default code) ### Step 3: Configure the Script Update the `CONFIG` object at the top of the script: ```javascript const CONFIG = { // Root folder ID where ACTIVE/INACTIVE folders live rootFolderId: '1Tb5v39DqRwk2341iYwOKqMXxA3e1Iu-8', // Leave empty for auto-detection (recommended) statusFolder: '', patientName: '', // Paste your JSON here, or use jsonFileId jsonInput: '', jsonFileId: '', // Options createJsonCopy: true, includeMissingData: false, includeClinicalInferences: false, autoDetect: true, // Recommended: automatically detect patient name and status }; ``` ### Step 4: Grant Permissions 1. Click **"Run"** → **"generateRecordFromJson"** 2. When prompted, click **"Review Permissions"** 3. Select your Google account 4. Click **"Advanced"** → **"Go to [Project Name] (unsafe)"** 5. Click **"Allow"** to grant permissions: - Access to Google Drive (to create folders and files) - Access to Google Docs (to create documents) ## Usage ### Method 1: Paste JSON Directly (Recommended) 1. Copy the AI-generated JSON from your AI tool 2. In the script editor, paste it into `CONFIG.jsonInput`: ```javascript jsonInput: `{ "schemaVersion": "1.0", "encounterId": "ide-1766464684536-2022-09-01", ... }`, ``` 3. Ensure `autoDetect: true` in CONFIG 4. Click **"Run"** → **"generateRecordFromJson"** 5. The script will: - Automatically detect patient name from JSON header - Detect status (ACTIVE/INACTIVE) - Create/use the appropriate folder structure - Generate the Google Doc - Save a JSON copy in the patient folder ### Method 2: Use Drive File ID 1. Upload the JSON file to Google Drive 2. Get the file ID from the file URL: `https://drive.google.com/file/d/{FILE_ID}/view` 3. Set `CONFIG.jsonFileId` to the file ID: ```javascript jsonFileId: '1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8h9i0j', ``` 4. Click **"Run"** → **"generateRecordFromJson"** ## Folder Structure The script creates the following structure in Google Drive: ``` Root Folder (1Tb5v39DqRwk2341iYwOKqMXxA3e1Iu-8) ├── ACTIVE/ │ └── {Patient Name} - {patientId}/ │ ├── IDE - {date} - {Patient Name}.doc │ └── EncounterNoteDraft-IDE-{date}.json └── INACTIVE/ └── {Patient Name} - {patientId}/ └── ... ``` ## Auto-Detection Features When `autoDetect: true`: - **Patient Name**: Extracted from `draft.header.patientLegalName`, or searched for in existing folders by patient ID - **Status**: Detected from `draft.status` field, or defaults to "ACTIVE" for IDE notes - **Folder Matching**: If patient ID is found in encounterId (pattern: `ide-{patientId}-{date}`), searches existing folders to find the correct patient name ## Error Handling The script validates: - JSON syntax - Required fields: `schemaVersion`, `encounterId`, `noteType`, `dateOfService`, `sections`, `missingData`, `clinicalInferences` - Folder access permissions Common errors: - **"Invalid JSON"**: Check JSON syntax - **"Missing required field"**: Ensure all required fields are present - **"Cannot find folder"**: Verify `rootFolderId` is correct and you have access ## Configuration Options | Option | Description | Default | |--------|-------------|---------| | `rootFolderId` | Google Drive folder ID for patient records | Required | | `statusFolder` | "ACTIVE" or "INACTIVE" (empty for auto-detect) | '' | | `patientName` | Patient name (empty for auto-detect) | '' | | `jsonInput` | JSON string to paste directly | '' | | `jsonFileId` | Google Drive file ID containing JSON | '' | | `createJsonCopy` | Save JSON copy in patient folder | `true` | | `includeMissingData` | Include missingData section in doc | `false` | | `includeClinicalInferences` | Include clinicalInferences section | `false` | | `autoDetect` | Auto-detect patient name and status | `true` | ## Troubleshooting ### Script can't find root folder - Verify the folder ID is correct - Ensure you have access to the folder - Check that the folder exists ### Patient name not detected - Ensure `draft.header.patientLegalName` exists in JSON - Or manually set `CONFIG.patientName` - Check that patient ID pattern matches: `ide-{patientId}-{date}` ### Document not created - Check Google Apps Script execution log for errors - Verify all required permissions are granted - Ensure JSON structure matches EncounterNoteDraft schema ## Example JSON Structure The script expects JSON matching the EncounterNoteDraft schema: ```json { "schemaVersion": "1.0", "encounterId": "ide-1766464684536-2022-09-01", "noteType": "IDE", "dateOfService": "2022-09-01", "provider": "Dr. Smith", "header": { "patientLegalName": "DOE, JOHN", "dob": "1980-01-01", "mrn": "12345" }, "sections": [ { "title": "CHIEF COMPLAINT", "blocks": [ { "type": "paragraph", "text": "Patient presents with..." } ] } ], "missingData": [], "clinicalInferences": [] } ``` ## Support For issues or questions: 1. Check the execution log in Google Apps Script editor 2. Verify JSON structure matches the schema 3. Ensure all permissions are granted 4. Review error messages for specific field issues ==== FILE: tsconfig.base.json ==== { "compilerOptions": { "target": "ES2022", "module": "NodeNext", "lib": ["esnext", "dom"], "strict": true, // Error: no-floating-promises } // ✅ Solution: Await or explicitly handle async function main() { await doAsyncWork(); // or void doAsyncWork(); // Explicitly ignore } // ❌ Issue: Unsafe member access function getValue(obj: any) { return obj.nested.value; if (!validate(body)) throw new Error('invalid'); ``` ## Concurrency & Timeouts - Reject long CPU work on request threads; offload to workers/queues - Enforce per-request timeouts and sensible connection pooling ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/01-code-standards/separation-of-concerns.mdc ==== --- description: Separation of concerns for layering and responsibilities alwaysApply: true --- # Separation of Concerns (SoC) Ensure the codebase is divided into distinct layers: presentation (UI components), business logic (services), and data access (stores/adapters). Each layer should handle its specific concern without overlapping responsibilities. UI components should not contain parsing, storage, or network logic. **Justification**: Separation prevents tight coupling, making the SummerySky extension easier to maintain, test, and extend across portals and workflows. **Example**: Keep portal-specific parsing in `libs/summerysky/portal-*` and invoke it from the service worker, rather than parsing directly inside sidepanel components. **Related Rules**: [single-responsibility.mdc](mdc:.cursor/rules/01-code-standards/single-responsibility.mdc), [simplicity.mdc](mdc:.cursor/rules/01-code-standards/simplicity.mdc) ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/01-code-standards/simplicity.mdc ==== --- description: Favor simple, maintainable solutions over complexity alwaysApply: true --- # Simplicity Favor simple, straightforward solutions over complex ones, avoiding unnecessary abstractions or over-engineering. **Justification**: Simplicity reduces technical debt and enhances maintainability. **Example**: Use basic hooks in `HomeTab.tsx` instead of complex state management unless needed. **Related Rules**: [separation-of-concerns.mdc](mdc:.cursor/rules/01-code-standards/separation-of-concerns.mdc), [single-responsibility.mdc](mdc:.cursor/rules/01-code-standards/single-responsibility.mdc) ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/01-code-standards/single-responsibility.mdc ==== --- description: Single-responsibility guidance for functions and modules alwaysApply: true --- # Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) Each function, class, or module should have one, and only one, responsibility. This means focusing on a single task or concern. **Justification**: Reliability is critical, SRP reduces bug risk by limiting scope and simplifies debugging and refactoring. **Example**: `RecipeExecutor` should only handle recipe execution, while record export logic stays in `@ss/google-export` and storage logic stays in `@ss/patient-records`. **Related Rules**: [separation-of-concerns.mdc](mdc:.cursor/rules/01-code-standards/separation-of-concerns.mdc) ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/01-code-standards/ts-standards-and-strictness.mdc ==== --- alwaysApply: true description: TypeScript strictness, imports, and public API standards --- # TypeScript Standards: Strictness, Imports & Public Surfaces Enable strict compiler options across all projects, avoid `any`, and restrict imports to stable public surfaces via path aliases. **Justification:** Strict typing and stable import surfaces reduce defects, improve editor tooling, and make refactors safer across shared code. ## Compiler Options Enable strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, noImplicitOverride, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, bundler module resolution, and isolatedModules for test compatibility. ```json { "compilerOptions": { "strict": true, "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true, "noImplicitOverride": true, "exactOptionalPropertyTypes": true, "moduleResolution": "bundler", "isolatedModules": true, "esModuleInterop": true, "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true } } ``` ### Test Environment Configuration For projects using ES modules in tests, ensure tsconfig supports both build and test environments: ```json // tsconfig.json (project root) { "extends": "../../tsconfig.base.json", "compilerOptions": { "isolatedModules": true, "esModuleInterop": true, "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true, "module": "ESNext" }, "include": ["src/**/*"], "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist", "coverage"] } ``` ⚠️ **Warning:** Do not disable strict mode in project tsconfigs; request waivers via ADR if absolutely necessary. ### tsconfig.json Path Calculation (NX Best Practice) When creating `tsconfig.json` files in NX libraries, the `extends` path must correctly reference `tsconfig.base.json` at the workspace root. **Count directory levels carefully** to avoid build failures. **Path Calculation Rules:** 1. Count the number of directory levels from the library's `tsconfig.json` to the workspace root 2. Use that many `../` segments in the `extends` path 3. Always verify the path exists before committing **Examples:** ```json // For libs/Google-Chrome-Extension-Library/core/runtime/tsconfig.json // Path: libs/ -> Google-Chrome-Extension-Library/ -> core/ -> runtime/ // Levels: 4 (libs, Google-Chrome-Extension-Library, core, runtime) { "extends": "../../../../tsconfig.base.json" } // For libs/Google-Chrome-Extension-Library/ui/shared-components/tsconfig.json // Path: libs/ -> Google-Chrome-Extension-Library/ -> ui/ -> shared-components/ // Levels: 4 (libs, Google-Chrome-Extension-Library, ui, shared-components) { "extends": "../../../../tsconfig.base.json" } // For apps/chrome-extensions/job-hunt-extension/tsconfig.json // Path: apps/ -> chrome-extensions/ -> job-hunt-extension/ // Levels: 3 (apps, chrome-extensions, job-hunt-extension) { "extends": "../../../tsconfig.base.json" } ``` **Verification Command:** Before committing, verify the path resolves correctly: ```bash cd <library-directory> ls -la <calculated-path>/tsconfig.base.json ``` **Common Error:** Using too many `../` segments (e.g., `../../../../../tsconfig.base.json` when `../../../../tsconfig.base.json` is correct) causes Vite/esbuild to fail with "Cannot read file" errors. 💡 **Tip:** When copying a `tsconfig.json` from another library, always verify the path depth matches your library's location. ## No `any` & Safer Assertions Disallow `any`. Prefer `unknown` with user-defined type guards. Use `as` assertions sparingly at boundaries. ```typescript function isLead(x: unknown): x is { id: string } { return typeof x === 'object' && x !== null && 'id' in x; } ``` ## Path Aliases & Public Surfaces Expose only `src/index.ts` from each library through path aliases. Internal files are not importable across libs. ```json { "compilerOptions": { "baseUrl": ".", "paths": { "@mm/*": ["libs/*/src/index.ts"] } } } ``` 💡 **Tip:** Create explicit barrel files per library to keep public APIs small and documented. ## Examples ```json { "rules": { "@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any": "error" } } ``` ## Related Rules - architecture-and-nx-boundaries - testing-strategy ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/02-architecture/architecture-and-nx-boundaries.mdc ==== --- alwaysApply: true description: "Monorepo layout and boundary rules" --- # Architecture, Workspace Layout & Nx Boundaries Define a predictable Nx layout with strict domain boundaries and dependency constraints to keep the monorepo fast and modular. **Justification:** Clear layers and enforced constraints prevent accidental coupling, enable parallel work, and support safe refactors at scale. ## Workspace Layout Organize the monorepo into top-level directories: apps, libs, tools, e2e, and docs. Libraries follow <domain>/<type> where type ∈ feature, ui, data-access, util, config, testing. Every project declares Nx tags to enable lint rules for dependency constraints. - apps/: runnable applications and entry points - libs/: reusable libraries grouped by domain and type - tools/: repo automation, codegen, migration scripts - e2e/: Playwright-based end-to-end suites - docs/: ADRs, architecture diagrams, API references ## Cross-Initiative Reuse (SummerySky) Features for `apps/chrome-extensions/PMHNP-Administration-SummerySky` MUST be implemented as reusable libs first. The app should only wire UI, routing, and Chrome/MV3 entry points. - Place reusable code in `libs/summerysky/*` (or `libs/Google-Chrome-Extension-Library/*` for shared extension utilities). - Avoid portal-specific assumptions in shared libs; keep portal adapters in data-access libraries. - Expose clean public APIs via `index.ts`; do not import deep paths across libs. - If a feature is SummerySky-only today, still design it as a portable library so other initiatives can adopt it with minimal changes. ## Dependency Constraints Enforce domain and layer constraints using Nx and ESLint. Higher layers may depend on lower layers; never the reverse. Only import from a library's public surface (index.ts). ```json { "extends": ["plugin:@nx/typescript"], "rules": { "@nx/enforce-module-boundaries": [ "error", { "enforceBuildableLibDependency": true, "allow": [], "depConstraints": [ { "sourceTag": "type:feature", "onlyDependOnLibsWithTags": ["type:data-access","type:ui","type:util","type:config"] }, { "sourceTag": "type:data-access", "onlyDependOnLibsWithTags": ["type:util","type:config"] }, { "sourceTag": "type:ui", "onlyDependOnLibsWithTags": ["type:util","type:config"] } ] } ] } } ``` 💡 **Tip:** Prefer small, composable libraries over monolithic ones to maximize reuse and cache hits. ## Tagging Examples ```json { "name": "@mm/patients/data-access", "tags": ["scope:patients","type:data-access"] } ``` ## Examples ```json {"name":"@mm/pipeline/util","tags":["scope:eng","type:util"]} ``` ## Related Rules - ts-standards-and-strictness - dev-workflow-and-git - ci-cd-and-releases ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/03-workflow/ai-sdlc-orchestrator.mdc ==== --- alwaysApply: true description: Repo-wide SDLC orchestrator driven by Codex continuity state --- # SDLC Orchestrator (Codex + Cursor) Use this rule to keep AI work aligned with the SDLC process defined in `/.cursor/rules/03-workflow/sdlc-setup.mdc` and to apply the practical feature/bug/hotfix workflows in `/.cursor/rules/03-workflow/ship-it-workflow.mdc`. When `.codex/projects/**/current-task.json` exists, treat it as the phase source of truth for the matching project: - Phase state: `sdlcPhase`, `currentPhase`, `activeBranch` - Verification commands: `nextCommandSet` - Completion criteria: `doneCriteria` Do not re-state every checklist item here. Follow the existing SDLC and ship-it docs as the canonical text, and only use this file to orchestrate ordering and gates. ## 1) Detect change intent (silent inference) Infer the closest workflow from the user request: - If the user asks for “new feature”, “add capability”, “implement X”, follow the Feature workflow in `ship-it-workflow.mdc`. - If the user asks for “bug”, “fix”, “regression”, “broken”, follow the Bug Fix workflow in `ship-it-workflow.mdc`. - If the user asks for “urgent”, “prod break”, “sev-1”, “hotfix”, follow the Hotfix Fast Path in `ship-it-workflow.mdc`. - If the request is documentation-only, follow the SDLC phases up to and including `document` and run the smallest relevant verification gates. ## 2) Pick the SDLC state source Step A: Look for task-state continuity state (Codex first) - Search for `.codex/projects/**/current-task.json`. - Choose the project whose `project.path` matches (or is closest to) the files being changed, mentioned paths, or the primary target app. - If no matching Codex project exists: - Search for a non-Codex task-state file at a recommended path like `.cursor/sdlc/task-state/<project>/current-task.json`. - If neither exists, treat the flow as generic and follow `sdlc-setup.mdc` phase ordering. Step B: If a task-state file exists, read: - `.codex/projects/<project>/SDLC_CHARTER.md` (project-specific SDLC sequence, guardrails, and quality gates) - the active task-state file for: - `sdlcPhase` - `currentPhase` - `nextCommandSet` - `doneCriteria` ## 3) Map task-state `sdlcPhase` to SDLC checklists If task-state `sdlcPhase` is present, follow these mappings: - `plan`: Phase 1 (Project Initialization & Planning) from `sdlc-setup.mdc` - `design`: Phase 2 (Quality Gates & Development Standards) + design decisions (tests strategy, ADR if needed) from `sdlc-setup.mdc` and the “Design the Change” section in `ship-it-workflow.mdc` - `implement`: Phase 3 + Phase 4 implementation checklist from `sdlc-setup.mdc` - `verify`: Phase 4 verification checklist from `sdlc-setup.mdc`, plus the “Run Affected Targets” step in `ship-it-workflow.mdc` - `document`: Phase 7 documentation checklist from `sdlc-setup.mdc` and ADR expectations from `documentation-standards.mdc` - `release`: Phase 5 deployment & release checklist from `sdlc-setup.mdc` and the “Staging Deploy / Production Rollout” guidance in `ship-it-workflow.mdc` - `operate`: Phase 6 observability & operations checklist from `sdlc-setup.mdc` (monitoring, incident response, and improvements) If task-state `sdlcPhase` is missing, use the ordered SDLC phases from `sdlc-setup.mdc` as the default progression. ## 4) Verification command policy (Nx-first) If task-state `nextCommandSet` is non-empty: - Run commands from `nextCommandSet` in the given order. - After each command, confirm the specific gate it represents succeeded (typecheck/test/build/e2e slice). - Only proceed to the next SDLC phase when the completion criteria for the current phase are satisfied (use task-state `doneCriteria` when present, otherwise use the `sdlc-setup.mdc` quality gates). If task-state `nextCommandSet` is empty or task-state state is not present: - Prefer Nx affected pipelines: - `pnpm exec nx affected:lint --parallel` - `pnpm exec nx affected:test --parallel` - `pnpm exec nx affected:build --parallel` - Add the smallest targeted e2e/smoke verification that matches the change surface (UI vs service worker vs integration boundaries). ## 5) DoR / DoD gates (feature vs bug) Treat the “Definition of Ready (DoR)” and “Definition of Done (DoD)” as mandatory phase exit criteria: Feature DoR/DoD - DoR must include: one-sentence goal + clear acceptance criteria + identified risks + rollback strategy + test plan outline. - DoD must include: acceptance criteria pass + tests added and passing + documentation updated + staging smoke green + rollback plan validated, when applicable. Bug Fix DoR/DoD - DoR must include: a reproduction description and a failing test plan. - DoD must include: failing test now passes + minimal fix + regression coverage + verification gates green. Hotfix - DoD includes the Sev-1 fast path checklist: incident note, minimal fix with failing test, fast CI lane, production deploy, post-deploy smoke, and monitored stability window. ## 6) Branch and commit safety Use `ship-it-workflow.mdc` branching guidance: - `feat/<scope>-<short-title>` - `fix/<scope>-<issue#>` - `hotfix/<short-title>` Safety constraints from SDLC/charters: - Keep work phase-scoped and independently verifiable. - Do not work directly in the user’s dirty workspace when an applicable charter forbids it (if `.codex/**/SDLC_CHARTER.md` includes a “do not work directly” guardrail, comply). - Before switching phases or branches, update the active task-state `currentPhase` and `nextCommandSet` for the new state. ## 7) Task-state continuity updates (before phase close) If task-state state is present, maintain deterministic resumability: - Update the active task-state file when: - `currentPhase.status` changes to `verified` or `done` - `activeBranch` changes - `nextCommit` / `nextCommandSet` changes - verification gates complete and `doneCriteria` can be satisfied - Ensure the worktree matches the declared `currentPhase.branch` before continuing with the next phase. ## Canonical references (follow these) These docs are the source of detailed checklist text; this rule only orchestrates ordering: - `/.cursor/rules/03-workflow/sdlc-setup.mdc` - `/.cursor/rules/03-workflow/ship-it-workflow.mdc` - `/.cursor/rules/03-workflow/dev-workflow-and-git.mdc` - `/.cursor/rules/03-workflow/documentation-standards.mdc` - `/.cursor/rules/nx-sdlc/RULE.md` ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/03-workflow/dev-workflow-and-git.mdc ==== --- alwaysApply: true description: Development workflow, branching, and review standards --- # Development Workflow, Branching & Reviews Use Conventional Commits, short-lived branches, CODEOWNERS-based reviews, and objective quality gates. **Justification:** Consistent workflow and automated checks keep velocity high and reduce regressions. ## Conventional Commits - Aim for ≤ 400 LOC per PR where feasible - Require passing gates: lint, typecheck, unit, e2e smoke, docs - CODEOWNERS assign domain reviewers automatically ```markdown # CODEOWNERS /apps/** @mm/frontend-leads /libs/** @mm/architecture /tools/** @mm/devex ``` ## Pre-commit & Pre-push Automate formatting, linting, and typechecking with Husky/lefthook. ```json { "husky": { "hooks": { "pre-commit": "pnpm lint && pnpm format", "pre-push": "pnpm typecheck && pnpm test:ci" } } } ``` ## Related Rules - User registration data * @param options - Additional registration options * @returns Promise resolving to created user with verification token * @throws {ValidationError} When user data is invalid * @throws {DuplicateUserError} When email already exists * @example * ```typescript * const user = await createUser({ * email: 'user@example.com', * name: 'John Doe' * }); * ``` */ export async function createUser( userData: UserData, options?: RegistrationOptions ): Promise<User> { // implementation } ``` ### Documentation Requirements Checklist - [ ] **@param** - All parameters with types and descriptions - [ ] **@returns** - Return value description and type - [ ] **@throws** - All possible error types and conditions - [ ] **@example** - At least one runnable usage example - [ ] **@since** - Version when feature was added (for major APIs) - [ ] **@deprecated** - Deprecation notice with migration path ## README Standards ### Project README Structure Every project must have a comprehensive README.md: ```markdown # Project Name Brief description of what this project does and its purpose. ## Installation ```bash pnpm install ``` ## Quick Start ```typescript import { mainFunction } from '@mm/project-name'; const result = await mainFunction(); ``` ## API Reference ### Core Functions #### `mainFunction(options: Options): Promise<Result>` Main entry point for the library. **Parameters:** - `options` - Configuration options **Returns:** Promise resolving to operation result **Example:** ```typescript const result = await mainFunction({ debug: true }); ``` ## Environment Variables | Variable | Description | Required | Default | |----------|-------------|----------|---------| | `API_KEY` | API authentication key | Yes | - | | `LOG_LEVEL` | Logging verbosity | No | `info` | ## Nx Targets | Target | Description | Command | |--------|-------------|---------| | `build` | Build the library | `nx build project-name` | | `test` | Run unit tests | `nx test project-name` | | `lint` | Lint the codebase | `nx lint project-name` | ## Development ### Prerequisites - Node.js 18+ - pnpm 8+ ### Setup ```bash pnpm install pnpm build ``` ### Testing ```bash pnpm test pnpm test:watch ``` ## Architecture [Include diagrams or flowcharts showing key components] ## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) for development guidelines. ## License MIT ``` ## ADR (Architecture Decision Records) ### When to Create ADRs Create an ADR for any non-trivial architectural decision: - Choosing between major technology options - Significant API design changes - Performance vs maintainability trade-offs - Security implementation decisions - Breaking changes to existing patterns ### ADR Structure ```markdown # ADR-001: Decision Title ## Status Accepted | Proposed | Rejected ## Context What problem are we solving? What constraints exist? ## Decision What did we decide and why? ## Consequences What becomes easier/harder? What are the trade-offs? ## Alternatives Considered What other options did we evaluate? - **Option A**: Pros/cons - **Option B**: Pros/cons ## Implementation How will this be implemented? Timeline? Migration plan? ``` ### ADR Organization ``` docs/ adr/ 001-use-typescript-strict-mode.md 002-adopt-nx-monorepo.md 003-implement-error-boundaries.md ``` ## API Documentation ### OpenAPI/Swagger Standards For HTTP APIs, maintain OpenAPI specifications: ```yaml openapi: 3.0.3 info: title: User Management API version: 1.0.0 description: User account and profile management paths: /users: post: summary: Create new user requestBody: required: true content: application/json: schema: $ref: '#/components/schemas/UserInput' responses: '201': description: User created successfully content: application/json: schema: $ref: '#/components/schemas/User' components: schemas: UserInput: type: object required: - email - name properties: email: type: string format: email name: type: string ``` ## Auto-Generated Documentation ### CI Documentation Generation Configure CI to automatically generate and publish documentation: ```yaml # .github/workflows/docs.yml name: Generate Docs on: push: branches: [main] pull_request: jobs: docs: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v3 - uses: actions/setup-node@v3 with: node-version: 18 cache: 'pnpm' - run: pnpm install - run: pnpm docs:generate - run: pnpm docs:publish ``` ### TypeDoc Configuration ```javascript // typedoc.config.js module.exports = { entryPoints: ['./src/index.ts'], out: './docs/api', exclude: ['**/*.spec.ts', '**/*.test.ts'], includeVersion: true, disableSources: false, excludePrivate: true, excludeProtected: true, hideGenerator: true, theme: 'default', readme: './README.md', name: 'My Library', tsconfig: './tsconfig.json' }; ``` ## Code Comments Standards ### When to Comment - **Complex business logic** - Explain why, not what - **Workarounds** - Document temporary solutions and TODOs - **Public APIs** - JSDoc as specified above - **Configuration choices** - Why specific values were chosen ### Comment Style ```typescript // ❌ Bad: states the obvious const total = price * quantity; // multiply price by quantity // ✅ Good: explains business logic const total = price * quantity; // Apply volume discount threshold check // ✅ Good: documents workaround // TODO: Remove when API supports bulk operations // Using individual requests due to rate limiting for (const item of items) { await api.update(item); } ``` ## Diagrams and Visual Documentation ### Mermaid Diagrams Use Mermaid for architecture and flow diagrams: ```mermaid graph TD A[User Request] --> B[API Gateway] B --> C[Authentication] C --> D[Business Logic] D --> E[Database] D --> F[External API] E --> G[Response] F --> G ``` ### Architecture Diagrams Include diagrams for: - System architecture overview - Data flow diagrams - Component interaction diagrams - Deployment diagrams ## Documentation Quality Checklist ### Code Documentation - [ ] All public APIs have JSDoc comments - [ ] Examples are runnable and tested - [ ] Error conditions are documented - [ ] Breaking changes are versioned and documented ### Project Documentation - [ ] README includes setup, usage, and API reference - [ ] Environment variables are documented - [ ] Nx targets are listed and described - [ ] Architecture diagrams exist for complex systems ### Process Documentation - [ ] ADRs exist for major decisions - [ ] Development workflow is documented - [ ] Deployment process is clear - [ ] Troubleshooting guides exist ### Maintenance - [ ] Documentation is reviewed in PRs - [ ] Outdated docs are updated with code changes - [ ] CI validates documentation generation - [ ] Documentation is versioned with releases ## Success Metrics - **Documentation Coverage**: > 90% of public APIs documented - **README Completeness**: All projects have comprehensive READMEs - **ADR Compliance**: Major decisions have corresponding ADRs - **Documentation Freshness**: < 30 days since last update - **Developer Satisfaction**: > 80% of developers can find needed information ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/03-workflow/sdlc-setup.mdc ==== --- description: Apply to all files when setting up new projects, services, or major features to ensure complete SDLC coverage alwaysApply: false --- # SDLC Setup & Quality Gates - Freshworks App Monorepo Comprehensive checklist for managing the Software Development Life Cycle in a Freshworks CRM app environment. Use this when spinning up new apps, services, or major features. **Justification:** Structured SDLC prevents technical debt, ensures quality, and reduces production incidents in enterprise CRM integrations. ## SDLC Phases Overview 1. **Plan & Spec** → Define goals, users, scope, success criteria, risks 2. **Design** → Architecture, data models, APIs, UI flows, test strategy 3. **Implement** → Code + tests + configs (with continuous quality gates) 4. **Verify** → Automated + manual testing, QA 5. **Release** → Deploy, migrate, feature toggles 6. **Operate** → Monitor, alert, incident response 7. **Improve** → Learnings, backlog, iteration ## SDLC Checklist - Order of Operations Use this checklist for new apps/services or major features. Each phase builds on the previous. ## Task Progress Tracking & Verification Orchestration (Codex optional) Use this checklist for human-readable SDLC gates, but drive *phase progress* and *verification execution order* from a task-state file. ### Source of truth (use Codex when available) - Codex projects: - Machine-readable task state: `.codex/projects/<project>/current-task.json` - Project charter / guardrails: `.codex/projects/<project>/SDLC_CHARTER.md` (optional but preferred) - Non-Codex projects (fallback): - Create and maintain a task-state file using the same schema fields at a recommended path like `.cursor/sdlc/task-state/<project>/current-task.json`. - Use `.codex/schemas/task-state.schema.json` as the reference shape for required fields. ### Task-state fields and how they map to SDLC progression - `sdlcPhase` selects the SDLC phase to target (`plan/design/implement/verify/document/release/operate`). - `currentPhase` drives phase-level tracking: - `currentPhase.id` identifies the current phase artifact/bundle. - `currentPhase.status` must move through `pending` → `in_progress` → (`verified` or `blocked`) → `done`. - `currentPhase.branch` is the worktree/branch that must be checked out when continuing work for that phase. - `nextCommandSet` is the verification execution plan for the *current* phase: - Prefer running those commands in order. - Only mark phase progress complete when the represented quality gates succeed. - `doneCriteria` defines the completion/exit conditions for the phase: - Use it as the “can we close this phase?” checklist in addition to the SDLC quality gates below. - `blockedBy` indicates known blockers: - If non-empty, set `currentPhase.status` to `blocked` and do not advance until blockers are resolved/cleared. - `artifacts` is where required phase outputs (handoff docs, diagrams, exports, runbook snippets) should be created/updated before phase close. ### Resume protocol (deterministic restart) Before continuing from an interruption, ensure the repo state matches the active task-state: - Verify `activeBranch` and `currentPhase.branch`. - Verify `nextCommit` and `nextCommandSet` match the intended phase. - Run the commands in `nextCommandSet` and only continue when the phase’s `doneCriteria` can be satisfied. ### 🚀 Phase 1: Project Initialization & Planning **Repository & Workspace Setup** - [ ] Create repository with main branch protection rules - [ ] Initialize pnpm workspace (monorepo structure) - [ ] Set up Nx workspace configuration - [ ] Add appropriate Nx tags for dependency constraints **Documentation & Governance** - [ ] Add runtime config validation (fail fast on boot) **CI/CD Pipeline** - [ ] Configure GitHub Actions with Nx affected commands - [ ] Set up pnpm store caching for faster builds - [ ] Implement PR pipeline: install → typecheck → lint → test → build - [ ] Test database operations with test containers - [ ] Verify authentication and authorization flows **End-to-End Testing** - [ ] Implement smoke tests (basic functionality verification) - [ ] Add sanity tests for critical user journeys - [ ] Create regression tests for existing features - [ ] Set up Playwright for UI component testing - [ ] Automate webhook service integration tests ### 🚀 Phase 5: Deployment & Release **Preview & Staging** - [ ] Configure health checks and monitoring - [ ] Set up alerting for production incidents ### 📊 Phase 6: Observability & Operations **Logging & Monitoring** - [ ] Implement structured JSON logging - [ ] Add OpenTelemetry traces and metrics - [ ] Document runbook (local dev, deploy, rollback) - [ ] Set up on-call rotation and alerting - [ ] Create incident response procedures - [ ] Add post-deployment smoke tests - [ ] Configure backup and disaster recovery ### 📚 Phase 7: Documentation & Knowledge **Technical Documentation** - [ ] Document deployment procedures - [ ] Create monitoring and alerting runbooks - [ ] Add security incident response guides - [ ] Document backup and recovery procedures - [ ] Create performance tuning guidelines ## Quality Gates by Phase ### Pre-commit (Automatic) - [ ] Code formatting (Prettier) - [ ] Linting (ESLint) - [ ] Type checking (TypeScript) - [ ] Unit tests pass ### Pre-merge (PR Review) - [ ] All pre-commit checks pass - [ ] Code review by domain experts - [ ] Integration tests pass - [ ] Accessibility checks pass (for UI) - [ ] Security scanning clean ### Pre-deploy (CI/CD) - [ ] Full test suite passes - [ ] Build artifacts generated - [ ] SBOM and vulnerability scan complete - [ ] Smoke tests pass in staging ### Post-deploy (Production) - [ ] Health checks pass - [ ] Monitoring alerts configured - [ ] Rollback plan documented - [ ] Incident response team notified ## Success Metrics - **Development Velocity**: PR merge time < 24 hours - **Code Quality**: 0 critical linting errors, 80%+ test coverage - **Reliability**: 99.9% uptime, < 5 min incident response - **Security**: 0 critical vulnerabilities in production - **User Experience**: All accessibility standards met ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/03-workflow/ship-it-workflow.mdc ==== --- description: Battle-tested order of operations for shipping features and fixing bugs in modern Nx monorepos with strict TypeScript, CI/CD, and feature flags alwaysApply: false --- # Ship It! - Battle-Tested Order of Operations Complete workflow for shipping features and fixing bugs in modern Nx monorepos. Follow these steps every time for predictable, safe deployments. **Justification:** Consistent process prevents production incidents, ensures quality, and maintains velocity in enterprise CRM integrations. ## 🎯 Shared Principles ### Branching Strategy ```bash # Features feat/<scope>-<short-title> # Example: feat/intake-guard-dedupe # Bug fixes fix/<scope>-<issue#> # Example: fix/telephony-asserted-id-421 # Hotfixes (Sev-1) hotfix/<short-title> # Example: hotfix/critical-auth-bypass ``` ### Definition of Ready (DoR) ✅ **A task is ready when you can write:** - One-sentence goal - Clear acceptance criteria - Identified risks - Rollback strategy - Test plan outline ❌ **If you can't write these, it's not ready to start** ### Definition of Done (DoD) ✅ **A task is done when:** - All acceptance criteria pass - Tests added and passing - Documentation updated - Post-deploy smoke tests green - Monitoring alerts quiet - Ticket closed --- ## 🚀 FEATURE WORKFLOW - Order of Operations ### 1️⃣ Triage & Spec (30-60 min) ```markdown ## User Story Template As a [user type] I want to [action] So that [benefit] ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] AC-1: Specific measurable outcome - [ ] AC-2: Another measurable outcome - [ ] AC-3: Edge case handling ## Dependencies - APIs: [List external APIs] - Database: [Schema changes needed] - Libraries: [New packages required] - Feature Flag: `feature_<name>_enabled` ## Observability Plan - Logs: Key events to log - Metrics: Counters/timers to add - Dashboard: Panels to create ``` ### 2️⃣ Branch & Scaffold ```bash # Create feature branch git checkout -b feat/<scope>-<short-title> # Generate Nx module/lib if needed nx g @nx/js:lib features/<feature-name> --tags=scope:feature,type:feature # Add feature flag (default OFF) echo "FEATURE_<NAME>_ENABLED=false" >> .env.example ``` ### 3️⃣ Test Plan First ```typescript // Define test cases BEFORE coding // Unit Tests (Pure/Fast) describe('FeatureName Core Logic', () => { it('should handle happy path') it('should validate inputs') it('should handle edge cases') }); // Integration Tests (API ↔ DB) describe('FeatureName Integration', () => { it('should persist data correctly') it('should handle concurrent requests') it('should respect feature flag') }); // E2E Test (User Flow) describe('FeatureName E2E', () => { it('should complete user journey when flag enabled') it('should gracefully degrade when flag disabled') }); // Smoke Test (Critical Path) describe('FeatureName Smoke', () => { it('should not break existing flows') it('should respond to health check') }); ``` ### 4️⃣ Design the Change ```markdown ## ADR Template (if changing patterns) # ADR-XXX: [Decision Title] ## Status Proposed | Accepted | Deprecated ## Context What problem are we solving? ## Decision What are we doing? ## Consequences What becomes easier/harder? ``` ### 5️⃣ Implement Incrementally (Flag-First) ```typescript // Always check feature flag first if (process.env.FEATURE_<NAME>_ENABLED === 'true') { // New implementation return newFeatureLogic(); } else { // Existing behavior return existingLogic(); } // Tracer bullet approach - vertical slice // 1. Route → 2. Controller → 3. Service → 4. Repository → 5. Database ``` ### 6️⃣ Integration & E2E ```bash # Add integration tests with test containers docker-compose -f docker-compose.test.yml up -d nx test <project> --testPathPattern=integration # Add E2E test behind flag FEATURE_<NAME>_ENABLED=true nx e2e <project>-e2e ``` ### ⚠️ Testing Pitfalls to Avoid #### Constructor Signature Changes ```typescript // ❌ Don't test with hard-coded constructor params const service = new Service({ logger, db, cache }); // ✅ Use dependency injection with mocks const mockLogger = createMockLogger(); const mockDb = createMockDb(); const service = new Service(mockLogger, mockDb); ``` #### Private Method Testing ```typescript // ❌ Don't test private methods directly (service as any).privateMethod(); // ✅ Test public behavior instead await expect(service.publicMethod()).toThrow('Validation error'); ``` #### Node.js Built-in Module Imports ```typescript // ❌ ES module syntax for Node.js built-ins import fs from 'fs'; // Fails in Jest // ✅ Namespace imports for Node.js built-ins import * as fs from 'fs'; ``` #### Mock Typing Issues ```typescript // ❌ Incorrect mock return types mockPage.innerText.mockResolvedValue('text'); // Type error // ✅ Proper type assertions mockPage.innerText.mockResolvedValue('text' as any); ``` ### 7️⃣ Local Affected Checks (Nx) ```bash # Run all affected checks in parallel nx affected:lint --parallel nx affected:test --parallel nx affected:build --parallel # If infrastructure changes nx run <infra-project>:synth cdk diff ``` ### 8️⃣ Open PR Early (Draft) ```markdown ## PR Template **Title:** feat(scope): short intent **Summary:** What & why in 2-3 sentences **Acceptance Criteria:** - [ ] AC-1: Specific outcome - [ ] AC-2: Another outcome **Changes:** - Endpoints: `/api/v1/new-endpoint` - Schema: Added `field_name` to table - Environment: `FEATURE_X_ENABLED` - Feature Flag: `feature_x_enabled` **Test Plan:** - Unit: 15 new tests added - Integration: 5 API tests added - E2E: 1 user journey test - Smoke: Health check verified **Migration/Infra:** - [ ] Run migration script - [ ] Update CDK stack - Rollback: `git revert` + flag OFF **Observability:** - Metrics: `feature_x_usage_count` - Logs: Search for `feature_x` - Dashboard: Link to dashboard **Risks/Mitigations:** - Risk: Performance impact - Mitigation: Added caching layer **Screenshots/GIFs:** [If UI changes] ``` ### 9️⃣ CI Gates ```yaml # CI must pass these gates jobs: quality-gates: steps: - Typecheck # TypeScript strict mode - Lint # ESLint rules pass - Unit Tests # 80% coverage - Integration # API contracts valid - Build # Artifacts created - E2E Preview # Tests against preview URL ``` ### 🔟 Review & Iterate ```bash # Address review comments # Keep commits clean git commit -m "feat(intake): address review feedback" # Re-run affected checks nx affected:test --base=origin/main ``` ### 1️⃣1️⃣ Staging Deploy (Flag OFF) ```bash # Deploy with flag OFF FEATURE_<NAME>_ENABLED=false npm run deploy:staging # Run post-deploy smoke npm run test:smoke:staging # Enable for internal testing FEATURE_<NAME>_ENABLED=true npm run test:e2e:staging # Monitor logs/metrics tail -f logs/staging.log | grep "feature_x" ``` ### 1️⃣2️⃣ Production Rollout ```typescript // Progressive flag ramp const rolloutSchedule = { day1: { percentage: 1, cohort: 'internal' }, day2: { percentage: 10, cohort: 'beta_users' }, day3: { percentage: 50, cohort: 'all_users' }, day4: { percentage: 100, cohort: 'all_users' } }; // Monitor KPIs const monitoring = { errorRate: '< 0.1%', latencyP95: '< 500ms', businessMetric: 'conversion_rate' }; ``` ### 1️⃣3️⃣ Finish & Cleanup ```bash # Update documentation npm run docs:generate # Update CHANGELOG echo "### Added - Feature X: Description" >> CHANGELOG.md # Remove temporary code git grep "TODO(feature_x)" | xargs -I {} sed -i '' 's/TODO(feature_x)//' {} # Close ticket gh issue close <issue-number> --comment "Feature shipped successfully" ``` --- ## 🐛 BUG FIX WORKFLOW - Order of Operations ### 1️⃣ Triage ```markdown ## Bug Report Template **Symptom:** What's broken? **Scope/Impact:** How many users affected? **First Bad Release:** v1.2.3 **Suspected Area:** Authentication module **Severity:** P0 | P1 | P2 | P3 ## For Sev-1/Hotfix - Skip normal queue - Write incident note - Follow hotfix fast path ``` ### 2️⃣ Reproduce & Add Failing Test ```typescript // FIRST: Write a test that fails describe('Bug #421', () => { it('should preserve caller ID on transfer', () => { // This test MUST fail before the fix const result = transferCall({ assertedId: '+1234567890' }); expect(result.callerId).toBe('+1234567890'); // Currently fails }); }); ``` ### 3️⃣ Branch ```bash git checkout -b fix/<scope>-<issue#> # Example: fix/telephony-421 ``` ### 4️⃣ Root Cause & Minimal Fix ```typescript // Prefer smallest change that addresses root cause // BAD: Refactor entire module // GOOD: Fix the specific line causing the issue // Before (buggy) const callerId = call.id; // Wrong field // After (fixed) const callerId = call.assertedId || call.id; // Correct field with fallback ``` ### 5️⃣ Run Affected Targets ```bash nx affected:test --base=origin/main nx affected:build --base=origin/main # If infrastructure changed nx run <infra-project>:synth cdk diff ``` ### 6️⃣ PR (Can be marked "hotfix") ```markdown ## Bug Fix PR Template **Root Cause:** Caller ID field was using wrong property **Before:** System used `call.id` instead of `call.assertedId` **After:** System correctly uses `call.assertedId` with fallback **How to Verify:** Run test case in PR description **Risk:** Low - isolated change with fallback **Rollback:** `git revert` this commit ``` ### 7️⃣ CI + Staging ```bash # Deploy to staging npm run deploy:staging # Run focused sanity tests npm run test:sanity --area=telephony # Run global smoke tests npm run test:smoke:staging ``` ### 8️⃣ Production ```bash # Deploy (with flag if added for safety) BUGFIX_421_ENABLED=true npm run deploy:production # Verify metrics curl https://metrics.example.com/api/telephony/errors # Post incident resolution echo "Incident resolved: Bug #421 fixed and deployed" >> incidents.log ``` --- ## 🚨 HOTFIX FAST PATH (Sev-1) ### Immediate Response ```bash # 1. Create hotfix branch from prod tag git checkout -b hotfix/<short-title> production-v1.2.3 # 2. Reproduce → Failing test → Minimal fix npm run test:reproduce-bug # 3. Fast CI lane (skip non-critical) nx run-many -t lint,test,build --projects=affected # 4. Deploy directly to prod npm run deploy:production:hotfix # 5. Post-deploy smoke npm run test:smoke:production # 6. Monitor for 15-30 minutes watch -n 5 'curl https://api.example.com/health' # 7. Back-merge to main git checkout main git merge hotfix/<short-title> # 8. Create postmortem gh issue create --title "Postmortem: <incident>" \ --body "Root cause, timeline, action items" ``` --- ## 🎛️ ROLLOUT & SAFETY PATTERNS ### Feature Flags ```typescript // Ship dark, test safely, instant rollback const featureFlag = { name: 'feature_x_enabled', defaultValue: false, rollout: { internal: true, beta: false, production: false } }; ``` ### Migration Strategy ```typescript // 1. Deploy forward-compatible code function readData() { return newSchema || oldSchema; // Works with both } // 2. Run migration await runMigration(); // 3. Flip to new path function readData() { return newSchema; // Only new } // 4. Remove old code // Delete oldSchema references ``` ### Canary/Blue-Green ```yaml deployment: strategy: canary stages: - weight: 5% # 5% traffic duration: 1h - weight: 25% # If metrics good duration: 2h - weight: 100% # Full rollout ``` ### Observability ```typescript // Add instrumentation const timer = metrics.startTimer('feature_x_duration'); try { logger.info('feature_x_started', { userId, timestamp }); const result = await featureXLogic(); metrics.increment('feature_x_success'); return result; } catch (error) { metrics.increment('feature_x_error'); logger.error('feature_x_failed', { error, userId }); throw error; } finally { timer.end(); } ``` ### Kill Switch ```typescript // Emergency bypass if (process.env.KILL_FEATURE_X === 'true') { return legacyImplementation(); } ``` --- ## ✅ COMMIT HYGIENE (Conventional Commits) ```bash # Features feat(intake): de-duplicate leads on create feat(api): add webhook retry mechanism # Fixes fix(telephony): preserve asserted caller id on transfer fix(auth): handle expired tokens gracefully # Other types refactor(crm): extract lead normalizer test(api): add regression for empty policy_id docs(readme): update deployment instructions perf(query): optimize contact search chore(deps): update nx to v20 ``` --- ## 🛠️ MINIMAL COMMAND SET (Nx-Friendly) ```bash # Branch management git checkout -b feat/<scope>-<title> git checkout -b fix/<scope>-<issue#> # Code generation nx g @nx/js:lib <lib-name> nx g @nx/node:application <app-name> nx g @nx/react:component <component-name> # Development loop nx affected:lint --parallel nx affected:test --parallel nx affected:build --parallel # E2E testing nx run <app>-e2e:e2e nx run <app>-e2e:e2e --watch # Infrastructure (CDK) nx run <infra-project>:synth nx run <infra-project>:deploy --require-approval never nx run <infra-project>:destroy --force # Full pipeline simulation nx run-many -t lint,test,build,e2e --parallel # Deploy commands (handled by CI, but available locally) npm run deploy:preview # PR preview npm run deploy:staging # Staging environment npm run deploy:production # Production (requires auth) ``` --- ## 📋 TINY CHECKLISTS ### Feature DoR (Definition of Ready) ```markdown - [ ] One-sentence goal & acceptance criteria written - [ ] Feature flag name chosen: `feature_<name>_enabled` - [ ] Data changes & migration plan documented - [ ] Test plan sketched (unit/integration/e2e/smoke) - [ ] Observability plan noted (logs/metrics/dashboards) - [ ] Dependencies identified (APIs/packages/services) - [ ] Risk assessment completed ``` ### Feature DoD (Definition of Done) ```markdown - [ ] All acceptance criteria pass - [ ] Tests added & passing (unit/integration/e2e) - [ ] Documentation/ADR updated - [ ] Code reviewed and approved - [ ] CI/CD pipeline green - [ ] Deployed to staging with flag OFF - [ ] Post-deploy smoke tests green (staging) - [ ] Progressive rollout plan executed - [ ] Production smoke tests green - [ ] Monitoring dashboards show healthy metrics - [ ] Feature flag at 100% or removed - [ ] Rollback steps documented and tested - [ ] CHANGELOG updated - [ ] Ticket closed ``` ### Bug Fix DoD ```markdown - [ ] Failing test written that reproduces bug - [ ] Root cause identified and documented - [ ] Minimal fix implemented (no scope creep) - [ ] Failing test now passes - [ ] Regression tests added for edge cases - [ ] No new bugs introduced (all tests green) - [ ] Code reviewed with focus on fix - [ ] Deployed to staging and verified - [ ] Deployed to production and verified - [ ] Metrics monitored for 30 minutes post-deploy - [ ] Incident note posted (if severity requires) - [ ] Postmortem scheduled (if P0/P1) ``` ### Hotfix Checklist (Sev-1) ```markdown - [ ] Incident commander assigned -
