process multiple URLs/tasks concurrently using the BatchRunner library or custom batch implementations. **Justification:** Batch operations require careful concurrency control, state persistence, error handling, and MV3 lifecycle management. Standardized patterns ensure reliable, resumable batch execution. ## Architecture Use `@chrome-ext/automation-batch` BatchRunner for all batch operations: ``` Sidepanel → Service Worker → BatchRunner → TaskExecutor → Recipe Execution ↓ BatchStateStore (persistence) ↓ TabSessionManager (concurrency) ``` ## BatchRunner Integration ### Required Components 1. **BatchRunner**: Core scheduler (from library) 2. **TaskExecutor**: Executes individual tasks (implement or use `RecipeTaskExecutor`) 3. **RowSink**: Handles task results (use `StorageTableSink` for UI integration) 4. **BatchStateStore**: Persists state (from library, auto-configured) ### Basic Setup ```typescript import { BatchRunner } from '@chrome-ext/automation-batch'; import { RecipeTaskExecutor } from '@chrome-ext/automation-batch'; import { StorageTableSink } from '@chrome-ext/automation-batch'; const batchRunner = new BatchRunner(); // Create executor const executor = new RecipeTaskExecutor({ appId: 'my-app', recipeId: 'my-recipe', dependencies: { createContentRuntime, executeRecipe, getRecipe, }, }); // Create sink const sink = new StorageTableSink({ appId: 'my-app', operationId: 'my-operation', broadcastEvents: true, // Enable UI updates }); ``` ## Task Definition ### Task Structure ```typescript import type { BatchTask } from '@chrome-ext/automation-batch'; const tasks: BatchTask[] = urls.map((url, index) => ({ id: `task-${index}`, // Deterministic ID for resume urlRef: url, // URL string or secure storage key (PHI mode) input: { /* task-specific input */ }, meta: { /* task metadata */ }, })); ``` ### Task ID Requirements - **Deterministic**: Same input → same ID (required for resume) - **Unique**: No duplicates within a batch run - **Stable**: Don't change IDs between runs for same data ```typescript // ✅ Good - deterministic id: `patient-${patientId}` // ✅ Good - hash-based id: `hash-${sha256(url)}` // ❌ Bad - non-deterministic id: `task-${Date.now()}-${Math.random()}` ``` ## Batch Run Options ### Required Options ```typescript const options: BatchRunOptions = { maxConcurrency: 2, // Worker pool size closeTabsOnComplete: true, // Clean up tabs after task focusTabs: false, // Don't focus tabs (better UX) phiMode: false, // Enable PHI-safe storage if needed timeouts: { tabLoadMs: 30000, contentReadyMs: 5000, taskExecutionMs: 300000, // 5 minutes per task }, retryPolicy: { maxAttempts: 3, initialDelayMs: 1000, maxDelayMs: 30000, backoffMultiplier: 2, jitter: true, }, }; ``` ### Concurrency Guidelines - **Default**: 2-3 concurrent tasks (balance speed vs resource usage) - **High-volume**: 3-5 concurrent tasks (if system can handle) - **PHI-sensitive**: 1-2 concurrent tasks (reduce risk) - **Rate-limited APIs**: 1 concurrent task (respect limits) ## Service Worker Handlers ### Message Handlers ```typescript chrome.runtime.onMessage.addListener((msg, sender, sendResponse) => { if (msg.type === 'START_BATCH') { batchRunner.start({ runId: msg.runId, appId: 'my-app', operationId: 'my-operation', tasks: msg.tasks, executor, sink, options: msg.options, correlationId: msg.correlationId, }).then(() => { sendResponse({ ok: true }); }).catch(error => { sendResponse({ ok: false, error: error.message }); }); return true; // Async response } if (msg.type === 'PAUSE_BATCH') { batchRunner.pause(msg.runId).then(() => { sendResponse({ ok: true }); }); return true; } if (msg.type === 'RESUME_BATCH') { batchRunner.resume(msg.runId).then(() => { sendResponse({ ok: true }); }); return true; } if (msg.type === 'ABORT_BATCH') { batchRunner.abort(msg.runId).then(() => { sendResponse({ ok: true }); }); return true; } if (msg.type === 'RESUME_DEFERRED_BATCH') { batchRunner.resumeDeferred(msg.runId).then(() => { sendResponse({ ok: true }); }); return true; } }); ``` ## State Persistence ### Automatic Persistence BatchRunner automatically persists: - Run snapshots (status, metrics, options) - Task states (status, attempts, errors) - Deferred tasks (captcha/timeout) ### Resume After Suspension ```typescript // On service worker wake async function rehydrateBatches() { const allRuns = await batchRunner.getAllRuns('my-app', 'my-operation'); for (const runId of allRuns) { const snapshot = await batchRunner.getRunSnapshot('my-app', 'my-operation', runId); if (snapshot.status === 'paused') { // Auto-resume paused runs await batchRunner.resume(runId); } else if (snapshot.status === 'running') { // Check if actually running (may have been suspended mid-run) // Optionally resume or mark as paused await batchRunner.pause(runId); } } } ``` ## Error Handling ### Error Classification BatchRunner distinguishes: - **Transient Errors** (`BatchTransientError`): Retryable (timeout, network, captcha) - **Permanent Errors** (`BatchPermanentError`): Don't retry (invalid input, auth failure) ### Custom Executor Error Handling ```typescript class MyTaskExecutor implements TaskExecutor { async execute({ task, signal, emitProgress }) { try { // Execute task return result; } catch (error) { const errorMessage = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error); // Classify error if (this.isTransientError(errorMessage)) { throw new BatchTransientError(errorMessage, error); } else { throw new BatchPermanentError(errorMessage, error); } } } private isTransientError(message: string): boolean { const transientPatterns = [ 'timeout', 'network', 'captcha', 'rate limit', 'temporary', ]; return transientPatterns.some(pattern => message.toLowerCase().includes(pattern) ); } } ``` ### Retry Policy ```typescript const retryPolicy: RetryPolicy = { maxAttempts: 3, // Total attempts (initial + 2 retries) initialDelayMs: 1000, // First retry delay maxDelayMs: 30000, // Cap on delay backoffMultiplier: 2, // Exponential backoff jitter: true, // Add randomness to prevent thundering herd }; ``` ## Deferred Tasks ### Automatic Deferral Tasks are automatically deferred on: - Captcha detection (if `captchaPolicy` configured) - Timeout (if task exceeds `taskExecutionMs`) - Manual deferral (via executor) ### Resume Deferred ```typescript // Resume all deferred tasks await batchRunner.resumeDeferred(runId); // Or handle deferred tasks separately const deferred = await batchRunner.getDeferredTasks(runId); // Process deferred tasks with different strategy ``` ## UI Integration ### Subscribe to Events ```typescript useEffect(() => { const listener = (msg: any) => { if (msg.type === 'BATCH_ROW_UPDATE' && msg.runId === runId) { // Reload table state loadTableState(); } if (msg.type === 'BATCH_RUN_STARTED') { // Update UI setRunStatus('running'); } if (msg.type === 'BATCH_RUN_COMPLETE') { // Update UI setRunStatus('completed'); } }; chrome.runtime.onMessage.addListener(listener); return () => chrome.runtime.onMessage.removeListener(listener); }, [runId]); ``` ### Load Table State ```typescript import { StorageTableSink } from '@chrome-ext/automation-batch'; const tableState = await StorageTableSink.getTableState( 'my-app', 'my-operation', runId ); // tableState.rowsById contains all task rows const rows = Object.values(tableState.rowsById); ``` ## PHI-Safe Batch Operations ### Enable PHI Mode ```typescript const options: BatchRunOptions = { phiMode: true, storage: { useSecureStorage: true, }, }; // Initialize secure storage const stateStore = new BatchStateStore({ useSecureStorage: true, }); await stateStore.initSecureStorage(passphrase); // Optional ``` ### PHI-Safe Guidelines - **URLs**: Store only in secure storage (never in `chrome.storage.local`) - **Logs**: Redact URLs using `maskUrl()` helper - **Errors**: Don't include URLs in error messages - **Task IDs**: Use non-PHI identifiers (patient IDs, not URLs) ## Logging ### Batch Operation Logging ```typescript logger.info('Batch run started', { runId, appId, operationId, taskCount: tasks.length, maxConcurrency: options.maxConcurrency, correlationId, }); logger.info('Task started', { runId, taskId: task.id, attempt: taskState.attempts + 1, correlationId, }); logger.info('Task completed', { runId, taskId: task.id, status: 'succeeded', duration: Date.now() - startTime, correlationId, }); logger.error('Task failed', error, { runId, taskId: task.id, attempts: taskState.attempts, willRetry: shouldRetry, correlationId, }); ``` ## Best Practices ### Concurrency - Start with low concurrency (2), increase based on performance - Monitor tab count and memory usage - Close tabs promptly (`closeTabsOnComplete: true`) ### State Management - Don't store large payloads in task states - Use result references for large data - Implement cleanup policies (TTL for old runs) ### Error Recovery - Classify errors correctly (transient vs permanent) - Use appropriate retry policies - Defer captcha/timeout tasks for manual handling ### Testing - Test pause/resume scenarios - Test service worker suspension/rehydration - Test error classification and retry logic - Test deferred task handling ## Checklist When implementing batch operations: - [ ] Use BatchRunner from `@chrome-ext/automation-batch` - [ ] Implement TaskExecutor (or use RecipeTaskExecutor) - [ ] Configure appropriate concurrency limits - [ ] Set up retry policies - [ ] Handle deferred tasks (captcha/timeout) - [ ] Implement service worker message handlers - [ ] Subscribe to batch events in UI - [ ] Test pause/resume functionality - [ ] Test service worker suspension recovery - [ ] Enable PHI-safe mode if handling sensitive data - [ ] Add comprehensive logging with correlation IDs ## Related Rules - Standardized patterns ensure reliable state persistence and resumption. ## Checkpoint System Overview Checkpoints save execution state at key milestones, allowing recipes to resume from saved points after interruption. ### When to Use Checkpoints - **Long-running recipes**: Extractions that take > 5 minutes - **Pagination**: Multi-page scraping operations - **User interruptions**: Allow users to pause and resume - **Error recovery**: Resume after transient failures - **State preservation**: Save progress before risky operations ## Checkpoint Storage ### Storage Location ```typescript // Checkpoints stored in chrome.storage.local const checkpointKey = `checkpoint:${checkpointId}`; await chrome.storage.local.set({ [checkpointKey]: { id: checkpointId, savedAt: new Date().toISOString(), tabId: context.tabId, baseFolder: context.baseDownloadFolder, variables: context.variables, credentials: context.credentials, metadata: { /* custom metadata */ }, correlationId: context.correlationId, }, }); ``` ### Checkpoint Structure ```typescript interface Checkpoint { id: string; // Unique checkpoint ID savedAt: string; // ISO timestamp tabId: number; // Tab ID (may be stale after resume) baseFolder: string; // Base download folder variables: Record<string, unknown>; // Recipe variables credentials?: { username: string; password: string }; // Optional credentials metadata?: Record<string, unknown>; // Custom metadata correlationId: string; // Correlation ID for tracing } ``` ## Recipe Step Types ### Save Checkpoint ```json { "type": "saveCheckpoint", "id": "page-{{currentPage}}", "description": "Save checkpoint before processing page", "metadata": { "currentPage": "{{currentPage}}", "totalPages": "{{totalPages}}" } } ``` ### Restore Checkpoint ```json { "type": "restoreCheckpoint", "id": "page-{{resumePage}}", "description": "Restore checkpoint to resume from page", "fallbackSteps": [ { "type": "goto", "url": "{{baseUrl}}/page/{{resumePage}}" } ] } ``` ## Checkpoint Implementation ### Saving Checkpoints ```typescript // In recipe executor if (step.type === 'saveCheckpoint') { const checkpointId = substituteVariables(step.id, context.variables); const checkpoint: Checkpoint = { id: checkpointId, savedAt: new Date().toISOString(), tabId: context.tabId, baseFolder: context.baseDownloadFolder, variables: { ...context.variables }, credentials: context.credentials, metadata: step.metadata ? substituteVariables(step.metadata, context.variables) : {}, correlationId: context.correlationId, }; await chrome.storage.local.set({ [`checkpoint:${checkpointId}`]: checkpoint, }); logger.info('Checkpoint saved', { checkpointId, correlationId: context.correlationId, variables: Object.keys(checkpoint.variables), }); } ``` ### Restoring Checkpoints ```typescript // In service worker if (msg.type === 'RESUME_RECIPE') { const { checkpointId, app, recipeId, tabId } = msg; // Load checkpoint const checkpointKey = `checkpoint:${checkpointId}`; const result = await chrome.storage.local.get(checkpointKey); const checkpoint = result[checkpointKey]; if (!checkpoint) { throw new Error(`Checkpoint not found: ${checkpointId}`); } // Restore execution context const executionContext: ExecutionContext = { tabId, // Use provided tabId (may differ from checkpoint.tabId) credentials: checkpoint.credentials, correlationId: checkpoint.correlationId || generateCorrelationId(), variables: checkpoint.variables || {}, baseDownloadFolder: checkpoint.baseFolder || getBaseDownloadFolder(), }; // Get recipe const recipe = getRecipe(app, recipeId); // Create runtime const runtime = createContentRuntime(tabId, { baseDownloadFolder: executionContext.baseDownloadFolder, variables: executionContext.variables, recipeKey: `${app}:${recipeId}`, }); // Execute recipe (will restore checkpoint if recipe has restoreCheckpoint step) const result = await executeRecipe(recipe, runtime, executionContext); } ``` ## Checkpoint Hooks ### Content Runtime Hooks ```typescript import type { ContentRuntimeHooks } from '@chrome-ext/automation-recipes'; export function createCheckpointHooks(): ContentRuntimeHooks { return { onCheckpointSaved: async ( checkpointId: string, checkpoint: Record<string, unknown> ) => { logger.info('Checkpoint hook triggered', { checkpointId, checkpointType: checkpointId.startsWith('job-') ? 'job' : checkpointId.startsWith('page-') ? 'page' : 'other', metadataKeys: Object.keys(checkpoint), correlationId: checkpoint.correlationId, }); // Process checkpoint (e.g., convert to postings, update UI) // This runs after checkpoint is saved }, }; } // Use in runtime creation const runtime = createContentRuntime(tabId, config, { onCheckpointSaved: createCheckpointHooks().onCheckpointSaved, }); ``` ## Checkpoint Naming Conventions ### Recommended Patterns - **Page checkpoints**: `page-{{pageNumber}}` - **Item checkpoints**: `item-{{itemId}}` or `job-{{jobId}}` - **Status checkpoints**: `status-{{statusName}}` - **Milestone checkpoints**: `milestone-{{milestoneName}}` ### Deterministic IDs Checkpoint IDs should be deterministic based on recipe variables: ```typescript // ✅ Good - deterministic id: `page-${currentPage}` // ✅ Good - includes context id: `patient-${patientId}-encounter-${encounterId}` // ❌ Bad - non-deterministic id: `checkpoint-${Date.now()}` ``` ## UI Integration ### List Available Checkpoints ```typescript async function listCheckpoints(app: string, recipeId: string): Promise<Checkpoint[]> { const allData = await chrome.storage.local.get(null); const checkpoints: Checkpoint[] = []; for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(allData)) { if (key.startsWith('checkpoint:')) { const checkpoint = value as Checkpoint; // Filter by app/recipe if needed checkpoints.push(checkpoint); } } return checkpoints.sort((a, b) => new Date(b.savedAt).getTime() - new Date(a.savedAt).getTime() ); } ``` ### Resume from UI ```typescript async function resumeFromCheckpoint( checkpointId: string, app: string, recipeId: string ) { // Get current tab or create new one const tabs = await chrome.tabs.query({ active: true, currentWindow: true }); const tabId = tabs[0]?.id; if (!tabId) { throw new Error('No active tab'); } // Send resume message const response = await chrome.runtime.sendMessage({ type: 'RESUME_RECIPE', checkpointId, app, recipeId, tabId, }); if (!response.ok) { throw new Error(response.error); } } ``` ## Error Handling ### Checkpoint Not Found ```typescript try { const checkpoint = await loadCheckpoint(checkpointId); // Resume... } catch (error) { if (error.message.includes('not found')) { logger.error('Checkpoint not found', { checkpointId, correlationId, }); // Execute fallback steps if provided if (fallbackSteps) { await executeSteps(fallbackSteps, runtime, context); } else { throw error; } } else { throw error; } } ``` ### Stale Checkpoints ```typescript // Check if checkpoint is too old const checkpointAge = Date.now() - new Date(checkpoint.savedAt).getTime(); const maxAge = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000; // 7 days if (checkpointAge > maxAge) { logger.warn('Checkpoint is stale', { checkpointId, age: checkpointAge, maxAge, }); // Optionally skip or warn user } ``` ## Best Practices ### When to Save Checkpoints - **Before pagination**: Save before navigating to next page - **After major milestones**: Save after completing significant work - **Before risky operations**: Save before operations that might fail - **Periodic saves**: Save every N items processed ### Checkpoint Granularity - **Too fine**: Checkpoints every step (overhead, storage bloat) - **Too coarse**: Checkpoints only at start/end (poor resume granularity) - **Just right**: Checkpoints at natural breakpoints (page boundaries, item boundaries) ### Variable Management - **Include all necessary variables**: Variables needed to resume - **Don't include large data**: Store references, not full data - **Validate variables**: Ensure variables are valid before saving ### Storage Management - **Cleanup old checkpoints**: Implement TTL or manual cleanup - **Limit checkpoint count**: Keep only N most recent checkpoints - **Archive important checkpoints**: Move to separate storage if needed ## Logging ### Checkpoint Logging ```typescript logger.info('Checkpoint saved', { checkpointId, checkpointType: checkpointId.startsWith('page-') ? 'page' : 'item', variables: Object.keys(checkpoint.variables), metadata: Object.keys(checkpoint.metadata || {}), correlationId: checkpoint.correlationId, }); logger.info('Checkpoint restored', { checkpointId, restoredVariables: Object.keys(checkpoint.variables), tabId: context.tabId, correlationId: checkpoint.correlationId, }); logger.info('Resume from checkpoint', { checkpointId, app, recipeId, tabId, correlationId, }); ``` ## Checklist When implementing checkpoints: - [ ] Define checkpoint structure with required fields - [ ] Implement `saveCheckpoint` step handler - [ ] Implement `restoreCheckpoint` step handler - [ ] Add checkpoint hooks for post-processing - [ ] Use deterministic checkpoint IDs - [ ] Include all necessary variables in checkpoints - [ ] Handle checkpoint not found errors - [ ] Implement UI for listing/resuming checkpoints - [ ] Add logging for checkpoint operations - [ ] Test resume after interruption - [ ] Test resume after service worker suspension - [ ] Implement checkpoint cleanup policy ## Directory Layout (SummerySky example) ```text apps/chrome-extensions/PMHNP-Administration-SummerySky/ ├─ src/ │ ├─ service_worker/ # MV3 background orchestration + storage + messaging │ ├─ content/ # Content scripts (DOM extraction + guidance) │ ├─ sidepanel/ # Side panel UI (React) │ ├─ popup/ # Optional popup entry │ ├─ recipes/ # JSON recipes + loader/registry │ ├─ utils/ # Shared utilities │ └─ tests/ # unit/integration/e2e ├─ scripts/ # manifest/build helpers ├─ vite.config.mjs # UI bundle ├─ vite.config.content.ts # content/service worker bundles ├─ tsconfig.json ├─ project.json # nx targets (build/test/e2e) └─ README.md ``` ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/15-chome-extension/chrome-extension-e2e-testing.mdc ==== --- description: End-to-end testing standards for Chrome Extension UI and hooks with comprehensive logging alwaysApply: false --- # Chrome Extension E2E Testing Standards Apply to all E2E tests for Chrome extensions, especially when integrating new features that involve UI components, React hooks, or messaging between sidepanel and service worker. **Justification:** Chrome extensions have unique testing challenges (MV3 service workers, sidepanel UI, cross-context messaging). Standardized patterns ensure reliable, debuggable tests with comprehensive logging. ## Test Structure & Organization ### Directory Layout ``` src/tests/e2e/ ├── specs/ │ ├── framework/ # Framework/infrastructure tests │ │ ├── ui-components.spec.ts │ │ ├── message-handlers.spec.ts │ │ ├── service-worker.spec.ts │ │ └── ... │ ├── recipes/ # Recipe execution tests │ │ └── recipe-execution.spec.ts │ └── smoke.spec.ts # Smoke tests ├── utils/ │ ├── console-logger.ts # Logging utility │ ├── framework-helpers.ts # Common test helpers │ └── global-setup.ts # Playwright global setup └── playwright.config.ts # Playwright configuration ``` ### Test File Structure Every E2E test file should follow this pattern: ```typescript import { test, expect, chromium, BrowserContext } from '@playwright/test'; import path from 'path'; import { existsSync } from 'fs'; import { fileURLToPath } from 'url'; import { ConsoleLogger } from '../../utils/console-logger'; import { getExtensionId, waitForServiceWorkerReady, openSidepanel, waitForSidepanelReady, navigateToTab, sendMessageToServiceWorker, } from '../../utils/framework-helpers'; import os from 'os'; const __filename = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url); const __dirname = path.dirname(__filename); const extensionPath = path.join(__dirname, '../../../../../dist'); const getUserProfilePath = () => { if ((global as any).__CHROME_USER_PROFILE__) { return (global as any).__CHROME_USER_PROFILE__; } if (process.env.CHROME_USER_PROFILE) { return process.env.CHROME_USER_PROFILE; } return path.join( os.homedir(), 'Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Profile 2' ); }; const getOutputDir = (testInfo?: any) => { const outputDir = testInfo?.outputDir; if (outputDir !== null && outputDir !== undefined && outputDir !== '' && typeof outputDir === 'string') { return outputDir; } if ((global as any).__OUTPUT_DIR__) { return (global as any).__OUTPUT_DIR__; } const timestamp = new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, '-').slice(0, -5); return path.join(__dirname, '../../../../test-results', timestamp); }; test.describe('Test Suite Name', () => { let userDataDir: string; let sharedContext: BrowserContext; test.beforeAll(async () => { if (!existsSync(extensionPath)) { throw new Error(`Extension dist directory not found: ${extensionPath}`); } userDataDir = getUserProfilePath(); // Create ONE shared context for all tests in the suite const headlessEnv = process.env.HEADLESS; sharedContext = await chromium.launchPersistentContext(userDataDir, { headless: headlessEnv === 'true', // or !== 'false' depending on default args: [ `--disable-extensions-except=${extensionPath}`, `--load-extension=${extensionPath}`, ], }); }); test.afterAll(async () => { if (sharedContext) { await sharedContext.close(); } }); test('@framework test name', async ({}, testInfo) => { const testOutputDir = getOutputDir(testInfo); const logger = new ConsoleLogger('test-name', testOutputDir); try { await logger.captureContextLogs(sharedContext); await waitForServiceWorkerReady(sharedContext); // Test implementation here } finally { await logger.cleanup(); } }); }); ``` ## Logging Requirements ### ConsoleLogger Usage **Every test MUST use ConsoleLogger** to capture logs from all contexts: ```typescript const logger = new ConsoleLogger('test-name', testOutputDir); try { // Capture logs BEFORE any actions await logger.captureContextLogs(sharedContext); // Test actions... } finally { // Always cleanup to write summary await logger.cleanup(); } ``` ### What Gets Logged ConsoleLogger captures: - **Page console logs**: All `console.log()`, `console.error()`, etc. from regular pages - **Extension page logs**: Console output from `chrome-extension://` pages - **Service worker logs**: Via CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol) for MV3 service workers - **Page errors**: Uncaught exceptions and page errors - **Runtime exceptions**: Service worker exceptions via CDP ### Log File Structure Logs are written to: ``` test-results/ <timestamp>/ logs/ <sanitized-test-name>.log ``` Each log entry includes: - Timestamp (ISO format) - Log level (INFO, WARN, ERROR, DEBUG) - Source (page, extension, service-worker, console) - Location (file:line:column when available) - Message ## Browser Context Management ### Shared Context Pattern Use a **single shared BrowserContext** per test suite (`beforeAll`/`afterAll`): ```typescript let sharedContext: BrowserContext; test.beforeAll(async () => { sharedContext = await chromium.launchPersistentContext(userDataDir, { headless: process.env.HEADLESS === 'true', args: [ `--disable-extensions-except=${extensionPath}`, `--load-extension=${extensionPath}`, ], }); }); test.afterAll(async () => { await sharedContext.close(); }); ``` **Why:** Chrome extensions persist state across page navigations. A shared context ensures: - Extension state is preserved between tests - Service worker stays alive - Storage (chrome.storage.local/session) persists - Faster test execution (no extension reload) ### Extension Loading Always load the extension with: - `--disable-extensions-except=${extensionPath}`: Disable other extensions - `--load-extension=${extensionPath}`: Load the extension from dist directory ## Service Worker Testing ### Wait for Service Worker Ready **Always wait for service worker initialization** before testing: ```typescript await waitForServiceWorkerReady(sharedContext); ``` This helper: 1. Waits for service worker to be registered 2. Pings the service worker with `{ type: 'PING' }` message 3. Verifies response includes `{ ok: true, initialized: true }` 4. Times out after 10 seconds (configurable) ### Testing Service Worker Messages Use `sendMessageToServiceWorker` helper: ```typescript const response = await sendMessageToServiceWorker<{ ok: boolean; recipes: any[]; }>(sidepanel, { type: 'LIST_RECIPES' }); expect(response.ok).toBe(true); expect(Array.isArray(response.recipes)).toBe(true); ``` **Note:** The helper automatically adds correlation IDs for tracing. ## Sidepanel UI Testing ### Opening the Sidepanel ```typescript const extensionId = await getExtensionId(sharedContext); const sidepanel = await openSidepanel(sharedContext, extensionId); await waitForSidepanelReady(sidepanel); ``` ### Waiting for Sidepanel Ready `waitForSidepanelReady` ensures: - Root element (`#root`) is visible - Navigation container (`.nav-container`) is rendered - React components are initialized (1 second wait) ### Tab Navigation ```typescript await navigateToTab(sidepanel, 'recipes'); const activeTab = await getActiveTab(sidepanel); expect(activeTab.toLowerCase()).toBe('recipes'); ``` ### UI Component Testing Patterns #### Testing Component Rendering ```typescript test('@framework ComponentName should render', async ({}, testInfo) => { const logger = new ConsoleLogger('component-render', testOutputDir); try { await logger.captureContextLogs(sharedContext); await waitForServiceWorkerReady(sharedContext); const extensionId = await getExtensionId(sharedContext); const sidepanel = await openSidepanel(sharedContext, extensionId); await waitForSidepanelReady(sidepanel); await navigateToTab(sidepanel, 'tab-name'); // Wait for component to load await sidepanel.waitForTimeout(2000); // Use resilient selectors const component = sidepanel.locator('text=Component Title, .component-class').first(); await expect(component).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5000 }); await sidepanel.close(); } finally { await logger.cleanup(); } }); ``` #### Testing User Interactions ```typescript // Click button const button = sidepanel.locator('button:has-text("Submit")'); await button.click(); await sidepanel.waitForTimeout(500); // Wait for state update // Fill form inputs const input = sidepanel.locator('input[type="text"]'); await input.fill('test value'); const value = await input.inputValue(); no `any`. Repo already standardized on TS + ESLint/Prettier + Vite. - All modules must be **pure** where possible; keep DOM side effects in content scripts. - Each `content/*.ts` should export **one** capability (waits, actions, selection utilities). - Use **functional** helpers for selectors (`byTestId`, `first`, `withinFrame`) and **never** inline long query strings in steps. ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/15-chome-extension/error-recovery.mdc ==== --- globs: apps/chrome-extensions/**/src/service_worker/**,apps/chrome-extensions/**/src/content/**,libs/Google-Chrome-Extension-Library/automation/** alwaysApply: false description: Graceful error handling, retry logic, and recovery patterns for recipe execution --- # Error Recovery Standards Apply when implementing error handling, retry logic, and recovery mechanisms for recipe execution, batch operations, and content script interactions. **Justification:** Robust error handling with appropriate retries and recovery ensures reliable automation even when facing transient failures, network issues, or unexpected conditions. ## Error Classification ### Error Types Classify errors as **transient** (retryable) or **permanent** (non-retryable): ```typescript class TransientError extends Error { constructor(message: string, cause?: Error) { super(message); this.name = 'TransientError'; this.cause = cause; } } class PermanentError extends Error { constructor(message: string, cause?: Error) { super(message); this.name = 'PermanentError'; this.cause = cause; } } ``` ### Transient Error Patterns ```typescript function isTransientError(error: Error): boolean { const message = error.message.toLowerCase(); const transientPatterns = [ 'timeout', 'network', 'connection', 'econnrefused', 'etimedout', 'captcha', 'rate limit', '429', // HTTP 429 Too Many Requests '503', // HTTP 503 Service Unavailable 'temporary', 'retry', 'unavailable', ]; return transientPatterns.some(pattern => message.includes(pattern)); } ``` ### Permanent Error Patterns ```typescript function isPermanentError(error: Error): boolean { const message = error.message.toLowerCase(); const permanentPatterns = [ 'not found', '404', // HTTP 404 Not Found '401', // HTTP 401 Unauthorized '403', // HTTP 403 Forbidden 'invalid', 'malformed', 'syntax error', 'permission denied', 'unauthorized', ]; return permanentPatterns.some(pattern => message.includes(pattern)); } ``` ## Retry Logic ### Exponential Backoff with Jitter ```typescript interface RetryConfig { maxRetries: number; // Total attempts (initial + retries) baseDelayMs: number; // Initial delay maxDelayMs: number; // Maximum delay cap backoffMultiplier: number; // Exponential multiplier jitter: boolean; // Add randomness } function calculateBackoffDelay( attempt: number, config: RetryConfig ): number { const exponentialDelay = config.baseDelayMs * Math.pow(config.backoffMultiplier, attempt); const cappedDelay = Math.min(exponentialDelay, config.maxDelayMs); if (config.jitter) { // Add ±20% jitter const jitterAmount = cappedDelay * 0.2; const jitter = (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * jitterAmount; return Math.max(0, cappedDelay + jitter); } return cappedDelay; } ``` ### Retry Implementation ```typescript async function executeWithRetry<T>( operation: () => Promise<T>, config: RetryConfig, context: ExecutionContext ): Promise<T> { let lastError: Error | null = null; for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= config.maxRetries; attempt++) { try { // Check cancellation assertNotCancelled(context); // Execute operation return await operation(); } catch (error) { lastError = error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error)); // Don't retry permanent errors if (isPermanentError(lastError)) { throw lastError; } // Don't retry if max attempts reached if (attempt >= config.maxRetries) { throw lastError; } // Calculate delay const delayMs = calculateBackoffDelay(attempt, config); logger.warn('Operation failed, retrying', { attempt: attempt + 1, maxRetries: config.maxRetries + 1, delayMs, error: lastError.message, correlationId: context.correlationId, }); // Wait before retry await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs)); } } throw lastError || new Error('Operation failed after retries'); } ``` ## Circuit Breaker Pattern ### Circuit Breaker Implementation ```typescript class CircuitBreaker { private failureCount = 0; private lastFailureTime: number | null = null; private state: 'closed' | 'open' | 'half-open' = 'closed'; constructor( private failureThreshold: number = 5, private timeoutMs: number = 60000, // 1 minute private successThreshold: number = 2 ) {} recordError(errorMessage: string): boolean { this.failureCount++; this.lastFailureTime = Date.now(); if (this.failureCount >= this.failureThreshold) { this.state = 'open'; logger.warn('Circuit breaker opened', { failureCount: this.failureCount, errorMessage, }); return true; // Should break } return false; // Continue } recordSuccess(): void { if (this.state === 'half-open') { // Count successes in half-open state this.failureCount--; if (this.failureCount <= 0) { this.state = 'closed'; this.failureCount = 0; logger.info('Circuit breaker closed', { state: this.state, }); } } else { // Reset on success in closed state this.failureCount = 0; } } shouldBreak(): boolean { if (this.state === 'open') { // Check if timeout expired if (this.lastFailureTime && Date.now() - this.lastFailureTime > this.timeoutMs) { this.state = 'half-open'; this.failureCount = this.successThreshold; logger.info('Circuit breaker half-open', { state: this.state, }); return false; // Try again } return true; // Still open } return false; // Closed or half-open } getState(): string { return this.state; } } ``` ### Using Circuit Breaker ```typescript const circuitBreaker = new CircuitBreaker(5, 60000, 2); async function executeStepWithCircuitBreaker( step: RecipeStep, runtime: FlowRuntime, context: ExecutionContext ): Promise<unknown> { // Check circuit breaker if (circuitBreaker.shouldBreak()) { throw new Error('Circuit breaker is open - too many failures'); } try { const result = await executeStep(step, runtime, context); circuitBreaker.recordSuccess(); return result; } catch (error) { const errorMessage = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error); const shouldBreak = circuitBreaker.recordError(errorMessage); if (shouldBreak) { throw new Error('Circuit breaker opened due to repeated failures'); } throw error; // Re-throw for retry logic } } ``` ## Idempotent Operations ### Step Idempotency All recipe steps should be idempotent (safe to retry): ```typescript // ✅ Idempotent - checks state before acting async function clickButton(selector: string): Promise<void> { const button = await waitForSelector(selector); const isVisible = await button.isVisible(); if (!isVisible) { return; // Already clicked or not needed } await button.click(); } // ✅ Idempotent - checks if already done async function fillInput(selector: string, value: string): Promise<void> { const input = await waitForSelector(selector); const currentValue = await input.inputValue(); if (currentValue === value) { return; // Already filled } await input.fill(value); } // ❌ Not idempotent - will fail on retry async function clickButtonBad(selector: string): Promise<void> { const button = await waitForSelector(selector); await button.click(); // May fail if already clicked } ``` ## Error Recovery Strategies ### Retry with Different Strategy ```typescript async function executeWithFallback<T>( primary: () => Promise<T>, fallback: () => Promise<T>, context: ExecutionContext ): Promise<T> { try { return await primary(); } catch (error) { if (isTransientError(error as Error)) { logger.warn('Primary operation failed, trying fallback', { error: (error as Error).message, correlationId: context.correlationId, }); try { return await fallback(); } catch (fallbackError) { logger.error('Fallback operation also failed', fallbackError as Error, { correlationId: context.correlationId, }); throw fallbackError; } } throw error; } } ``` ### Graceful Degradation ```typescript async function executeWithGracefulDegradation<T>( operation: () => Promise<T>, fallbackValue: T, context: ExecutionContext ): Promise<T> { try { return await operation(); } catch (error) { if (isTransientError(error as Error)) { logger.warn('Operation failed, using fallback value', { error: (error as Error).message, correlationId: context.correlationId, }); return fallbackValue; } throw error; } } ``` ## Error Logging ### Structured Error Logging ```typescript logger.error('Operation failed', error, { operation: 'executeStep', stepType: step.type, stepDescription: step.description, attempt: attempt + 1, maxRetries: config.maxRetries + 1, willRetry: attempt < config.maxRetries && isTransientError(error), errorType: isTransientError(error) ? 'transient' : 'permanent', correlationId: context.correlationId, tabId: context.tabId, }); ``` ### Error Context Always include context in error logs: - Correlation ID - Tab ID - Step information - Retry attempt number - Error classification (transient/permanent) - Will retry flag ## Best Practices ### Retry Configuration - **Max retries**: 3-5 attempts (balance reliability vs time) - **Base delay**: 1-2 seconds (not too aggressive) - **Max delay**: 30-60 seconds (cap exponential growth) - **Jitter**: Always enable (prevent thundering herd) ### Error Classification - **Be conservative**: When unsure, classify as transient - **Update patterns**: Add new patterns as you encounter errors - **Log classifications**: Log why errors are classified as transient/permanent ### Circuit Breaker - **Failure threshold**: 5-10 failures - **Timeout**: 60 seconds (1 minute) - **Success threshold**: 2-3 successes to close ### Idempotency - **Check state first**: Verify current state before acting - **Safe to retry**: All steps should be safe to retry - **No side effects**: Avoid operations with irreversible side effects ## Checklist When implementing error recovery: - [ ] Classify errors as transient or permanent - [ ] Implement exponential backoff with jitter - [ ] Add circuit breaker for repeated failures - [ ] Ensure all steps are idempotent - [ ] Add retry configuration to recipe options - [ ] Log errors with full context - [ ] Test retry logic with simulated failures - [ ] Test circuit breaker behavior - [ ] Handle cancellation signals during retries - [ ] Implement graceful degradation where appropriate ## Related Rules - Service worker owns orchestration; content scripts execute DOM actions. - Prefer deterministic selectors (role + name) and include `description` on steps for better logs. - Retry only idempotent waits; avoid re-clicking if a step already caused navigation. - Store recipe overrides locally when selector repair is applied; export override JSON for repo updates. ## Packaging - JSON recipes live in `apps/chrome-extensions/**/src/recipes/jsons/**`. - Loader/registry registers promoted recipes and merges overrides at startup. ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/15-chome-extension/logging-and-observability.mdc ==== --- globs: apps/chrome-extensions/**/src/** alwaysApply: false description: Logging, telemetry, and run status expectations for extension flows --- # Logging and Observability Standards Apply to all logging, telemetry, and observability implementations across service worker, content scripts, and sidepanel. **Justification:** Comprehensive logging with correlation IDs, structured data, and proper log levels enables debugging, monitoring, and troubleshooting of complex automation workflows. ## Logger Usage ### Logger Wrapper Use `@chrome-ext/core-telemetry` logger with levels: `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`. ```typescript import { logger } from '@chrome-ext/core-telemetry'; logger.debug('Detailed debugging information', { /* context */ }); logger.info('Informational message', { /* context */ }); logger.warn('Warning message', { /* context */ }); logger.error('Error occurred', error, { /* context */ }); ``` ### App Tag Prefixing Prefix automation logs with app tag for filtering: ```typescript logger.info('[Bravado] Patient extraction started', { patientId, correlationId, }); logger.info('[Indeed] Job scraping completed', { jobCount, correlationId, }); ``` ## Structured Logging ### Required Context Fields Always include these fields in log context: ```typescript logger.info('Operation started', { operation: 'executeRecipe', app: 'bravado', recipeId: 'patients-export-v3', tabId: context.tabId, correlationId: context.correlationId, runId: runId, // If batch operation stepId: step.id, // If recipe step }); ``` ### Log Levels - **debug**: Detailed debugging information (development only) - **info**: Normal operation events (start, progress, completion) - **warn**: Warning conditions (retries, fallbacks, degraded performance) - **error**: Error conditions (failures, exceptions) ## Run Log Storage ### Session Storage Store last 1000 entries in `chrome.storage.session` keyed by `runId`: ```typescript const RUN_LOG_KEY = `run_log:${runId}`; const MAX_LOG_ENTRIES = 1000; interface LogEntry { timestamp: string; level: 'debug' | 'info' | 'warn' | 'error'; message: string; context?: Record<string, unknown>; } async function appendToRunLog( runId: string, entry: LogEntry ): Promise<void> { const key = `run_log:${runId}`; const result = await chrome.storage.session.get(key); const logs = (result[key] as LogEntry[]) || []; logs.push(entry); // Keep only last MAX_LOG_ENTRIES if (logs.length > MAX_LOG_ENTRIES) { logs.splice(0, logs.length - MAX_LOG_ENTRIES); } await chrome.storage.session.set({ [key]: logs }); } ``` ## Recipe Execution Logging ### Step Execution ```typescript logger.info('Step started', { stepType: step.type, stepDescription: step.description, stepId: step.id, tabId: context.tabId, correlationId: context.correlationId, }); logger.info('Step completed', { stepType: step.type, stepDescription: step.description, stepId: step.id, duration: Date.now() - startTime, tabId: context.tabId, correlationId: context.correlationId, }); ``` ### Step Progress ```typescript logger.info('Step progress', { stepType: step.type, stepId: step.id, progress: { current: currentIndex, total: totalItems, percentage: (currentIndex / totalItems) * 100, }, correlationId: context.correlationId, }); ``` ## Batch Operation Logging ### Batch Run Events ```typescript logger.info('Batch run started', { runId, appId, operationId, taskCount: tasks.length, maxConcurrency: options.maxConcurrency, correlationId, }); logger.info('Task started', { runId, taskId: task.id, attempt: taskState.attempts + 1, correlationId, }); logger.info('Task completed', { runId, taskId: task.id, status: 'succeeded', duration: Date.now() - startTime, correlationId, }); logger.error('Task failed', error, { runId, taskId: task.id, attempts: taskState.attempts, willRetry: shouldRetry, correlationId, }); ``` ## Checkpoint Logging ### Checkpoint Operations ```typescript logger.info('Checkpoint saved', { checkpointId, checkpointType: checkpointId.startsWith('page-') ? 'page' : 'item', variables: Object.keys(checkpoint.variables), metadata: Object.keys(checkpoint.metadata || {}), correlationId: checkpoint.correlationId, }); logger.info('Checkpoint restored', { checkpointId, restoredVariables: Object.keys(checkpoint.variables), tabId: context.tabId, correlationId: checkpoint.correlationId, }); ``` ## Error Logging ### Error Context ```typescript logger.error('Operation failed', error, { operation: 'executeStep', stepType: step.type, stepDescription: step.description, attempt: attempt + 1, maxRetries: config.maxRetries + 1, willRetry: attempt < config.maxRetries && isTransientError(error), errorType: isTransientError(error) ? 'transient' : 'permanent', correlationId: context.correlationId, tabId: context.tabId, errorDetails: { name: error.name, message: error.message, stack: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' ? error.stack : undefined, }, }); ``` ## State Transition Logging ### State Changes ```typescript logger.info('State transition', { from: previousState, to: newState, reason: 'user_action' | 'error' | 'completion' | 'timeout', correlationId, runId, // If batch operation }); ``` ## Sidepanel Log Display ### Live Tail Sidepanel should show live tail of run logs: ```typescript function useRunLog(runId: string) { const [logs, setLogs] = useState<LogEntry[]>([]); useEffect(() => { // Load initial logs chrome.storage.session.get(`run_log:${runId}`).then(result => { setLogs(result[`run_log:${runId}`] || []); }); // Subscribe to updates const listener = (changes: { [key: string]: chrome.storage.StorageChange }) => { if (changes[`run_log:${runId}`]) { setLogs(changes[`run_log:${runId}`].newValue || []); } }; chrome.storage.onChanged.addListener(listener); return () => chrome.storage.onChanged.removeListener(listener); }, [runId]); return logs; } ``` ### Log Export Export run log as JSON: ```typescript async function exportRunLog(runId: string): Promise<string> { const result = await chrome.storage.session.get(`run_log:${runId}`); const logs = result[`run_log:${runId}`] || []; return JSON.stringify(logs, null, 2); } ``` ## PHI-Safe Logging ### Redaction Never log PHI in plaintext: ```typescript function redactUrl(url: string): string { // Mask URLs in PHI mode if (phiMode) { return '[REDACTED]'; } return url; } logger.info('Navigation', { url: redactUrl(url), correlationId, }); ``` ### Secure Logging ```typescript // Store sensitive logs in secure storage if (phiMode) { await secureStorage.append('secure_log', logEntry); } else { await appendToRunLog(runId, logEntry); } ``` ## Performance Logging ### Duration Tracking ```typescript const startTime = Date.now(); // ... operation ... logger.info('Operation completed', { operation: 'executeRecipe', duration: Date.now() - startTime, correlationId, }); ``` ### Metrics ```typescript logger.info('Metrics', { operation: 'batchRun', metrics: { totalTasks: 100, completedTasks: 95, failedTasks: 3, deferredTasks: 2, averageTaskDuration: 5000, totalDuration: 500000, }, correlationId, }); ``` ## Best Practices ### Logging Guidelines - **Be concise**: Include only necessary context - **Use structured data**: Always use context objects, not string interpolation - **Include correlation IDs**: Every log entry should have correlation ID - **Log at appropriate levels**: Don't log debug info in production - **Don't log PHI**: Redact sensitive data - **Log state transitions**: Important state changes should be logged - **Log errors with context**: Always include full error context ### Log Volume - **Limit log entries**: Keep last 1000 entries per run - **Rotate logs**: Clean up old logs periodically - **Use log levels**: Filter by level to reduce noise ## Checklist When implementing logging: - [ ] Use `@chrome-ext/core-telemetry` logger - [ ] Prefix logs with app tag - [ ] Include correlation ID in all logs - [ ] Include tabId, stepId, runId where applicable - [ ] Store run logs in chrome.storage.session - [ ] Implement live tail in sidepanel - [ ] Implement log export functionality - [ ] Redact PHI in logs - [ ] Log state transitions - [ ] Log errors with full context - [ ] Track performance metrics - [ ] Limit log volume (1000 entries per run) ## Contracts (TypeScript types) - `HelloMsg { kind:'HELLO', tabId:number, url:string, frameId:number }` - `SyncMsg { kind:'SYNC', flow?: FlowSnapshot }` - `StepRequest { kind:'STEP_REQUEST', step: StepSpec, runId:string }` - `StepResult { kind:'STEP_RESULT', stepId:string, status:'ok'|'retry'|'fail', detail?:any }` - `IntentMsg { kind:'INTENT', action:'StartFlow'|'Pause'|'Resume'|'Abort'|'ExportLog', payload?:any }` ## Ports vs onMessage - **Long-lived**: use `chrome.tabs.connect(tabId, {name:'content' })` for content ↔ background; use `chrome.runtime.connect({name:'sidepanel'})` for side panel. - **One-shots**: `chrome.runtime.sendMessage` for simple triggers from popup. ## Robustness - On `onDisconnect`, background sets a **reconnect timer** and marks tab as **dehydrated**; content on reload resends `HELLO` to rebind the port. > Your own README emphasizes “Web Automation Bridge” and typed message contracts—so we codify it here. ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/15-chome-extension/mv3-lifecycle-and-state.mdc ==== --- globs: apps/chrome-extensions/**/src/service_worker/**,apps/chrome-extensions/**/src/** alwaysApply: false description: MV3 service worker lifecycle, rehydration, and state handling --- ## Goals Make the AI handle **service worker suspension**, **tab reloads**, and **content-script rehydration** without losing in-flight flow state. ## Golden Rules 1) **Single source of truth in background** - Keep runtime state (active flow, current step, timers) in **background**. Persist a minimal snapshot to `chrome.storage.session` on every step so worker suspension or tab navigations can be recovered. - On worker wake (`chrome.runtime.onStartup`, `onInstalled`, `onMessage`, `onConnect`), rehydrate snapshot and **probe** all live tabs to rebuild ports (see “Messaging Contracts” rule). 2) **Rehydrate after navigation** - Content script on `document_start` immediately sends a **HELLO(port, tabId, url, frameId)**. Background responds with **SYNC(flowState)** if a flow is in progress for that tab. - If background knows a step was “Navigate to first result → then wait for contact page”, it must **arm phased waits** again after `goto()`. (Your README already frames phased waits/pagination—apply the same robustness for SPA routes.) 3) **Never rely on `setInterval` keep-alives** - MV3 workers sleep. Use **events**: `onMessage`, `onConnect`, `chrome.alarms` lightweight pings for long gaps, and **idempotent step execution** (steps re-run safely after resume). 4) **Flow step idempotency** - Every step should accept re-entry. Example: a `waitFor(selector)` that already found the node simply resolves; a `click(selector)` ensures visibility/attached DOM before acting. 5) **Durable step log** - Append each step result to a **ring buffer** in `chrome.storage.session` and mirror to a **per-run log** file only when the user requests export from the popup/panel (see “Logging & Observability”). ## Implementation nudges for Cursor - Add `rehydrateContent(tabId)` in `service_worker/index.ts` that: a) looks up `flowState[tabId]`, b) posts `SYNC` to content, c) re-arms any **post-navigation waits**. - Add a `content/handshake.ts` (or `content.ts` handler) that sends `HELLO` on load and on `visibilitychange` when it returns to `visible`. - Require **typed** messages: `HelloMsg`, `SyncMsg`, `StepRequest`, `StepResult`. ## Build/Test Anchors - The extension is **MV3 + Vite multi-entry**; the build outputs `background.js`, `content.js`, `popup.js` to `apps/chrome-extensions/PMHNP-Administration-SummerySky/dist` and ships `manifest.json`/`popup.html`. Keep that artifact map stable. ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/15-chome-extension/playwright-and-e2e.mdc ==== --- globs: apps/chrome-extensions/**/src/tests/**,apps/chrome-extensions/**/src/** alwaysApply: false description: Playwright/E2E expectations for Chrome extensions --- ## Use existing targets & tags - Smoke: `pnpm nx run pmhnp-administration-summerysky:e2e -- --grep @smoke` - Recipe slices: use `pnpm nx run pmhnp-administration-summerysky:e2e -- --grep "@recipes"` and extend existing tags. - Side panel slice: `pnpm nx run pmhnp-administration-summerysky:e2e -- --grep @sidepanel` ## Authoring rules - Tests must **load the unpacked extension** and **exercise the exact waits** used by content scripts (spy on logs if needed). - Prefer **route-anchored** assertions over hard sleeps: `expect(page.url()).toMatch(/contacts\/\d+/)` **before** waiting for `[data-test-id="fieldSectionWrapperShowAll"]`. ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/15-chome-extension/prompts-and-workflows.mdc ==== --- globs: apps/chrome-extensions/** alwaysApply: false description: Workflow expectations for extension feature changes and e2e slices --- - For any flow edits, ask Cursor to: 1) Generate the **plan** (files touched, commands run, test tags to update), 2) Execute the change with **typed contracts** + **phased waits**, 3) Update **E2E slices** under `@smoke`, `@sidepanel`, or the app-specific tag. - Keep prompts grounded in your **UI integration and flow system** notes; If already expanded, **no-op**. 5) **Instrumentation** - Each phase logs `phase:start` → `phase:ok|timeout`, emits ms duration, stored in session log for panel playback. > Keep this consistent with the “robust page load detection”/phased approach your README uses for pagination. ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/15-chome-extension/sidepanel-application-model.mdc ==== --- globs: apps/chrome-extensions/**/src/sidepanel/**,apps/chrome-extensions/**/src/service_worker/**,apps/chrome-extensions/**/src/sidepanel.tsx alwaysApply: false description: Sidepanel state model and messaging expectations --- ## Goals Treat the **Side Panel** as a **view** bound to background state; never as the source of truth. ## Rules 1) **Open/close orchestration in background** - Background owns `chrome.sidePanel.setOptions` and `open` flows; panel UI only requests actions. 2) **Panel <-> Background contract** - Establish a `chrome.runtime.connect({name:'sidepanel'})` port when panel mounts. - On connect, background pushes current `RunStatus` + steps log. - Panel sends **INTENT** messages (StartFlow, Pause, Resume, Abort, ExportLog). 3) **Panel survives reloads** - If panel is reopened or side panel toggled for the active tab, background re-sends last `RunStatus` + last 100 log entries from `chrome.storage.session`. 4) **E2E targets already exist** - Keep the `@sidepanel` E2E slice in Playwright; extend only in-place (don’t invent new configs): `pnpm nx run pmhnp-administration-summerysky:e2e -- --grep @sidepanel` 5) **Static assets are copied at build** - Don’t forget to copy `panel.html` and panel styles to `dist`—your build pipeline already does this with a `cp` chain; Bundlers like Vite may inject error handling code that attempts to access `window` and `document`, causing runtime errors. This rule defines comprehensive DOM API mocks to prevent these errors. ## Required Implementation ### 1. Mock Placement **CRITICAL:** DOM API mocks MUST be placed at the very top of the service worker file, BEFORE any imports. ```typescript // ✅ CORRECT: Mocks at top, before imports if (typeof window === 'undefined') { (globalThis as any).window = { /* ... */ }; } if (typeof document === 'undefined') { (globalThis as any).document = { /* ... */ }; } import { bootstrapBackground } from '@chrome-ext/core-runtime'; // ✅ After mocks // ❌ WRONG: Imports before mocks import { bootstrapBackground } from '@chrome-ext/core-runtime'; if (typeof window === 'undefined') { /* ... */ } // ❌ Too late! ``` ### 2. Window Mock Requirements The `window` mock MUST include: ```typescript if (typeof window === 'undefined') { (globalThis as any).window = { dispatchEvent: () => true, addEventListener: () => {}, removeEventListener: () => {}, postMessage: () => {}, location: { href: '', origin: '', protocol: '', host: '', hostname: '', port: '', pathname: '', search: '', hash: '', }, } as Window; } ``` **Required Methods:** - `dispatchEvent` - Used by Vite's error handler - `addEventListener` / `removeEventListener` - Event handling - `postMessage` - Cross-context messaging - `location` - URL access (for parsers that check `window.location.href`) ### 3. Document Mock Requirements The `document` mock MUST include: ```typescript if (typeof document === 'undefined') { // Create a mock element with appendChild support const createMockElement = () => ({ appendChild: () => ({} as Node), removeChild: () => ({} as Node), setAttribute: () => {}, getAttribute: () => null, querySelector: () => null, querySelectorAll: () => [], textContent: '', innerHTML: '', style: {}, id: '', className: '', href: '', } as HTMLElement); const mockBody = createMockElement(); const mockHead = createMockElement(); const mockDocumentElement = createMockElement(); (globalThis as any).document = { getElementsByTagName: () => [], querySelector: () => null, querySelectorAll: () => [], createElement: () => createMockElement(), addEventListener: () => {}, removeEventListener: () => {}, body: mockBody, // ✅ Required for appendChild head: mockHead, // ✅ Required for script injection documentElement: mockDocumentElement, // ✅ Required for appendChild } as Document; } ``` **Required Properties:** - `body` - Used by Vite's error handler for `document.body.appendChild()` - `head` - Used for script injection - `documentElement` - Used as fallback append target - `querySelector` / `querySelectorAll` - Used by parser code - `createElement` - Must return element with `appendChild` method **Required Methods:** - `getElementsByTagName` - Used by Vite's error handler - `querySelector` / `querySelectorAll` - Used by parser code - `createElement` - Must return mock element with `appendChild` - `addEventListener` / `removeEventListener` - Event handling ### 4. Mock Element Requirements Elements created by `createElement` MUST support: - `appendChild()` - Returns a mock Node - `removeChild()` - Returns a mock Node - `setAttribute()` / `getAttribute()` - Attribute manipulation - `querySelector()` / `querySelectorAll()` - Element querying - `textContent` / `innerHTML` - Content properties - `style` - Style object - `id` / `className` - Element identifiers - `href` - For anchor elements ## Common Error Patterns & Fixes ### Error: "window is not defined" **Cause:** Mock not placed before imports, or mock missing required methods. **Fix:** 1. Move mock to top of file (before all imports) 2. Ensure `dispatchEvent`, `addEventListener`, `postMessage` are included ### Error: "document.querySelector is not a function" **Cause:** `querySelector` method missing from document mock. **Fix:** Add `querySelector: () => null` to document mock. ### Error: "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'appendChild')" **Cause:** `document.body` is undefined, or `createElement` doesn't return element with `appendChild`. **Fix:** 1. Add `body: createMockElement()` to document mock 2. Ensure `createElement` returns element with `appendChild` method ### Error: "window.location.href is not a function" **Cause:** `window.location` is undefined or not an object. **Fix:** Add `location` object with `href` property to window mock. ### Error: "import() is disallowed on ServiceWorkerGlobalScope" **Cause:** Using dynamic `import()` in service worker, which is not allowed by HTML spec. **Fix:** Replace all `await import()` calls with static imports at the top of the file. Use helper functions to check module availability for optional modules. ## Verification Checklist Before committing a service worker file, verify: - [ ] Window mock is at the very top of the file (before imports) - [ ] Document mock is at the very top of the file (before imports) - [ ] Window mock includes: `dispatchEvent`, `addEventListener`, `removeEventListener`, `postMessage`, `location` - [ ] Document mock includes: `body`, `head`, `documentElement`, `querySelector`, `querySelectorAll`, `createElement` - [ ] `createElement` returns element with `appendChild` method - [ ] All mock methods are no-ops (don't throw errors) - [ ] Mock elements support common DOM operations - [ ] No dynamic `import()` calls - all imports are static - [ ] Optional modules use helper functions to check availability ## Testing ### Manual Test 1. Load extension in Chrome 2. Reload extension 5+ times 3. Check service worker console for errors 4. Verify no "window is not defined" or "document is not defined" errors ### Automated Test ```typescript test('service worker has DOM mocks', async () => { const swCode = readFileSync('src/service_worker/index.ts', 'utf-8'); // Verify mocks are before imports const mockIndex = swCode.indexOf('if (typeof window === \'undefined\')'); const importIndex = swCode.indexOf('import'); expect(mockIndex).toBeLessThan(importIndex); // Verify required methods exist expect(swCode).toContain('dispatchEvent'); expect(swCode).toContain('querySelector'); expect(swCode).toContain('appendChild'); expect(swCode).toContain('document.body'); }); ``` ## Static Imports Only **CRITICAL:** Dynamic `import()` is disallowed in service workers by the HTML specification. All imports MUST be static. ```typescript // ✅ CORRECT: Static import at top of file import * as zoomInfoModule from '@chrome-ext/integrations-zoominfo'; // ❌ WRONG: Dynamic import (disallowed) const module = await import('@chrome-ext/integrations-zoominfo'); ``` **For Optional Modules:** Use a helper function to check module availability: ```typescript // Static import at top import * as zoomInfoModule from '@chrome-ext/integrations-zoominfo'; // Helper function function getZoomInfoModule(): typeof zoomInfoModule | null { try { if ( zoomInfoModule && typeof zoomInfoModule.getZoomInfoCredentials === 'function' ) { return zoomInfoModule; } return null; } catch (error) { return null; } } // Usage const module = getZoomInfoModule(); if (!module) { // Handle missing module gracefully return; } ``` ## Related Rules - [browser-injection-standards](./browser-injection-standards.mdc) - Browser script injection - [flow-standards](./flow-standards.mdc) - Automation flow definitions - [web-automation-development](./web-automation-development.mdc) - Development standards ## Examples ### ✅ Good: Complete Mock Implementation ```typescript // Top of service_worker/index.ts if (typeof window === 'undefined') { (globalThis as any).window = { dispatchEvent: () => true, addEventListener: () => {}, removeEventListener: () => {}, postMessage: () => {}, location: { href: '', origin: '', /* ... */ }, } as Window; } if (typeof document === 'undefined') { const createMockElement = () => ({ appendChild: () => ({} as Node), removeChild: () => ({} as Node), querySelector: () => null, querySelectorAll: () => [], // ... other methods } as HTMLElement); (globalThis as any).document = { body: createMockElement(), head: createMockElement(), documentElement: createMockElement(), querySelector: () => null, querySelectorAll: () => [], createElement: () => createMockElement(), // ... other methods } as Document; } // Now imports are safe import { bootstrapBackground } from '@chrome-ext/core-runtime'; ``` ### ❌ Bad: Missing Required Methods ```typescript // Missing appendChild support if (typeof document === 'undefined') { (globalThis as any).document = { querySelector: () => null, // ❌ Missing body, head, documentElement // ❌ createElement doesn't return element with appendChild } as Document; } ``` ## Version History - **2025-01-XX:** Initial rule created - **2025-01-XX:** Added appendChild mock requirements - **2025-01-XX:** Added comprehensive element mock requirements ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/16-web-automation/browser-injection-standards.mdc ==== --- description: Standards for browser script injection and content security in web automation globs: ["apps/**", "libs/**", "tools/**"] alwaysApply: true --- # Browser Injection Standards ## Content Validation Validate all content being injected into browser contexts for security and compatibility. ### Security Checks - **No template literals**: Avoid template literals in injected scripts as they can introduce XSS vulnerabilities - **No Unicode characters**: Use escaped sequences or avoid Unicode in injected JavaScript - **ES module compatibility**: Ensure injected scripts work in browser environments - **Input sanitization**: Validate and sanitize all dynamic content before injection ### Code Quality - **Strict TypeScript**: Use TypeScript strict mode for all injection scripts - **Error handling**: Include proper try-catch blocks and error reporting - **Performance**: Minimize script size and execution time - **Compatibility**: Test across target browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) ## Injection Patterns ```typescript // 👍 Good - static, validated content const script = ` (function() { const button = document.querySelector('[data-automation-id="submit"]'); if (button) { button.addEventListener('click', function() { console.log('Button clicked'); }); } })(); `; // 👎 Avoid - template literals with dynamic content const script = ` (function() { const selector = '${dynamicSelector}'; // XSS vulnerability document.querySelector(selector); })(); `; ``` ## Validation Checklist - [ ] No template literals in injected scripts - [ ] No Unicode characters that could cause encoding issues - [ ] Scripts tested in target browser environments - [ ] Error handling included for runtime failures - [ ] Content properly escaped and sanitized - [ ] Scripts follow CSP (Content Security Policy) requirements ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/16-web-automation/flow-standards.mdc ==== --- description: Standards for automation flow definitions and structure globs: ["**/flows/*.json"] alwaysApply: true --- # Flow Standards ## Flow Structure Automation flows should follow consistent, maintainable patterns for reliability and reusability. ### Required Fields Every flow step must include: - **id**: Unique identifier for the step - **type**: Action type (click, type, wait, etc.) - **locator**: Robust locator object (prefer data-attributes, roles, text) - **description**: Human-readable description of the action ### Locator Standards - **Prefer data attributes**: Use `data-automation-id`, `data-testid`, or similar - **ARIA roles**: Use `role` and `aria-label` when available - **Text-based**: Use visible text as fallback, but prefer explicit locators - **Avoid CSS/XPath**: Only use as last resort when semantic locators unavailable ```json { "steps": [ { "id": "login-button-click", "type": "click", "locator": { "type": "data-attribute", "value": "data-automation-id=login-button" }, "description": "Click the login button to proceed" }, { "id": "username-input", "type": "type", "locator": { "type": "role", "value": "textbox", "name": "Username" }, "value": "{{username}}", "description": "Enter username in the login form" } ] } ``` ## Flow Validation - **Dependency checking**: Ensure no circular dependencies in flow prerequisites - **Required parameters**: All referenced variables must be defined - **Step sequencing**: Steps should be logically ordered and reversible where possible - **Error handling**: Include recovery steps for common failure scenarios ## Best Practices - **Modular flows**: Break complex flows into smaller, reusable components - **Parameterization**: Use variables for environment-specific values - **Documentation**: Include clear descriptions for maintenance - **Testing**: Each flow should have corresponding test coverage - **Versioning**: Track flow changes with semantic versioning ## Flow Checklist - [ ] All steps have required id, type, locator, and description fields - [ ] Locators use semantic attributes over CSS selectors - [ ] No circular dependencies in prerequisites - [ ] Parameters are properly defined and validated - [ ] Flow includes error recovery steps where appropriate - [ ] Flow is documented with usage examples - [ ] Corresponding tests exist and pass ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/16-web-automation/web-automation-development.mdc ==== --- description: Development standards for web automation projects globs: ["apps/**", "libs/**", "tools/**"] alwaysApply: true --- # Web Automation Development Standards ## Code Organization Maintain clean separation between automation logic, UI components, and business rules. ### Architecture Patterns - **Single Responsibility**: Each module handles one automation concern - **Composition over inheritance**: Build complex flows from simple, reusable components - **Dependency injection**: Make modules testable by injecting dependencies ### UI Integration - **Overlay registration**: Register UI elements in injected overlays with clear action mapping - **Event routing**: Route user interactions through centralized handlers - **State management**: Maintain automation state separate from application state ## Selector Strategy Robust selectors are critical for reliable automation. ### Preferred Selectors (in order) 1. **Data attributes**: `data-automation-id`, `data-testid`, `data-cy` 2. **ARIA attributes**: `role`, `aria-label`, `aria-describedby` 3. **Semantic HTML**: `button[name="submit"]`, `input[type="email"]` 4. **Text content**: Only when above options unavailable 5. **CSS/XPath**: Last resort, avoid `nth-child()` and complex selectors ### Selector Examples ```typescript // 👍 Preferred - semantic and robust page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save Changes' }) page.getByTestId('user-profile') page.getByLabel('Email Address') // 👎 Avoid - brittle and maintenance-heavy page.locator('.btn-primary:nth-child(2)') page.locator('#main > div > form > input[type="text"]') ``` ## Error Handling & Recovery Automation must gracefully handle failures and edge cases. ### Recovery Patterns - **Retry logic**: Implement exponential backoff for transient failures - **Fallback selectors**: Provide alternative locators for the same element - **State validation**: Check expected state before and after actions - **Logging**: Comprehensive logging for debugging and monitoring ### Error Types ```typescript class AutomationError extends Error { constructor( message: string, public readonly code: string, public readonly recoverable: boolean = false ) { super(message); this.name = 'AutomationError'; } } // Usage throw new AutomationError( 'Element not found after retries', 'ELEMENT_NOT_FOUND', true // Can retry ); ``` ## Testing Strategy Comprehensive testing ensures automation reliability. ### Test Categories - **Unit tests**: Individual functions and utilities - **Integration tests**: Component interactions and API calls - **E2E tests**: Complete user workflows - **Visual regression**: UI consistency across browsers ### Test Organization - **Page Objects**: Encapsulate page-specific logic and selectors - **Fixtures**: Reusable test data and setup/teardown - **Parallel execution**: Run tests concurrently for efficiency - **Cross-browser**: Test compatibility across target browsers ## Performance Considerations Optimize for speed and resource efficiency. ### Performance Best Practices - **Lazy loading**: Load automation features only when needed - **Debouncing**: Prevent excessive API calls and UI updates - **Caching**: Cache expensive operations and DOM queries - **Monitoring**: Track execution times and failure rates ### Resource Management - **Memory leaks**: Clean up event listeners and DOM references - **Connection pooling**: Reuse connections for external services - **Timeout management**: Set appropriate timeouts for all async operations ## Security Standards Protect sensitive data and maintain user privacy. ### Data Protection - **No credential storage**: Never store real credentials in code or configs - **Input sanitization**: Validate and sanitize all user inputs - **Session isolation**: Keep automation sessions separate from user sessions - **Audit logging**: Log automation actions for compliance ### Compliance - **GDPR**: Handle personal data appropriately - **CSP compliance**: Ensure injected scripts follow Content Security Policies - **Rate limiting**: Respect API rate limits and implement backoff ## Development Workflow Streamlined process for automation development. ### Version Control - **Small commits**: Commit frequently with clear, descriptive messages - **Branch strategy**: Feature branches with clear naming conventions - **Code reviews**: Mandatory reviews for all automation changes ### Documentation - **Flow documentation**: Document all automation flows with examples - **API references**: Maintain up-to-date API documentation - **Troubleshooting**: Include common issues and solutions - **Changelog**: Track changes and breaking updates ## Quality Checklist - [ ] Code follows TypeScript strict mode standards - [ ] Selectors use semantic, robust patterns - [ ] Error handling includes recovery mechanisms - [ ] Tests cover happy path and error scenarios - [ ] Performance optimized for target environments - [ ] Security best practices implemented - [ ] Documentation updated with changes - [ ] Code reviewed by at least one other developer ==== RULE FILE: .cursor/rules/00-master-index/RULE.md ==== --- description: Master index of development rules (reference when editing rules) globs: .cursor/rules/** alwaysApply: false --- # 🎯 Master Development Rules Index -
