return false; } async function loadSectionsFromFilesystem(source) { const workspaceRoot = source.workspaceRoot; const files = await listFilesRecursive(workspaceRoot, { includeMatcher: (fullPath) => { const relativePath = path.relative(workspaceRoot, fullPath).replace(/\\/g, '/'); return shouldReadFilesystemPath(relativePath) || (relativePath.startsWith('docs/') && TEXT_FILE_PATTERN.test(relativePath)); } }); const sections = []; for (const file of files) { const relativePath = path.relative(workspaceRoot, file.path).replace(/\\/g, '/'); if (file.skipped) { sections.push({ source: 'filesystem', path: relativePath, rawPath: file.path, skipped: true, content: '' }); continue; } sections.push({ source: 'filesystem', path: relativePath, rawPath: file.path, skipped: false, content: await readText(file.path) }); } return dedupeSections(sections); } function parseYamlList(text) { return [...text.matchAll(/^\s*-\s*['"]?([^'"\n]+)['"]?\s*$/gm)].map((match) => match[1]); } function parseRuleFile(section) { const descriptionMatch = section.content.match(/^description:\s*(.+)$/m); const alwaysApplyMatch = section.content.match(/^alwaysApply:\s*(.+)$/m); const folder = section.path.split('/').slice(0, 3).join('/'); return { id: makeId('rule', section.path), path: section.path, title: path.basename(section.path), description: descriptionMatch ? descriptionMatch[1].replace(/^['"]|['"]$/g, '') : 'No description provided', alwaysApply: alwaysApplyMatch ? alwaysApplyMatch[1].trim() === 'true' : false, folder, summary: section.content.split('\n').slice(0, 18).join('\n') }; } function projectNameFromPath(relativePath) { const segments = relativePath.split('/'); if (segments[0] === 'apps' && segments.length >= 3) return segments[2]; if (segments[0] === 'libs' && segments.length >= 3) return segments[2] === 'Google-Chrome-Extension-Library' && segments.length >= 5 ? `${segments[2]}/${segments[3]}/${segments[4]}` : segments[2]; if (segments[0] === 'tools' && segments.length >= 2) return segments[1]; return segments[segments.length - 2] ?? segments[segments.length - 1]; } function titleFromPath(relativePath) { return path.basename(relativePath).replace(/\.[^.]+$/, '').replace(/[-_]+/g, ' '); } function groupBy(items, keyFn) { const map = new Map(); for (const item of items) { const key = keyFn(item); if (!map.has(key)) map.set(key, []); map.get(key).push(item); } return map; } function extractRootConfig(sections, targetPath) { return tryJson(sections.find((section) => section.path === targetPath)?.content ?? '', null); } function extractPathAliases(tsconfigBase) { const aliases = []; const paths = tsconfigBase?.compilerOptions?.paths ?? {}; for (const [alias, destinations] of Object.entries(paths)) { for (const destination of destinations) { aliases.push({ alias, destination }); } } return aliases; } function detectTopology(sections, rootPackage) { const reasons = []; let kind = 'single-repo'; let confidence = 0.6; if (sections.some((section) => section.path === 'nx.json')) { kind = 'nx-monorepo'; confidence = 0.99; reasons.push('nx.json present'); } if (sections.some((section) => section.path === 'pnpm-workspace.yaml')) { reasons.push('pnpm-workspace.yaml present'); confidence = Math.max(confidence, 0.9); } if (rootPackage?.workspaces || sections.some((section) => section.path.endsWith('/project.json'))) { reasons.push('multiple package/project manifests detected'); confidence = Math.max(confidence, 0.85); } if (kind !== 'nx-monorepo') { const packageCount = sections.filter((section) => section.path.endsWith('/package.json') || section.path === 'package.json').length; if (packageCount > 3) { kind = 'polyrepo-or-loose-monorepo'; reasons.push('multiple package.json files without Nx control plane'); confidence = Math.max(confidence, 0.8); } } return { kind, confidence, reasons }; } function extractProjectManifests(sections) { const projectSections = sections.filter((section) => section.path.endsWith('/project.json')); const projects = []; for (const section of projectSections) { const json = tryJson(section.content, null); if (!json) continue; const root = path.dirname(section.path).replace(/\\/g, '/'); const category = root.split('/')[0] ?? 'project'; projects.push({ id: makeId('project', json.name ?? root), name: json.name ?? projectNameFromPath(root), projectType: json.projectType ?? 'unknown', root, category, sourceRoot: json.sourceRoot ?? null, tags: json.tags ?? [], targets: Object.keys(json.targets ?? {}), targetCommands: Object.fromEntries( Object.entries(json.targets ?? {}).map(([name, value]) => [name, value?.options?.command ?? null]) ) }); } return projects; } function collectSectionsForPrefix(sections, prefix) { return sections.filter((section) => section.path === prefix || section.path.startsWith(`${prefix}/`)); } function countChromeApis(sections) { const counts = new Map(); for (const section of sections) { for (const match of section.content.matchAll(/chrome\.([A-Za-z0-9_]+)/g)) { const api = match[1]; counts.set(api, (counts.get(api) ?? 0) + 1); } } return [...counts.entries()].sort((left, right) => right[1] - left[1]).map(([api, count]) => ({ api, count })); } function inferProjectAttributes(project, allSections, rootPackage, pathAliases) { const sections = collectSectionsForPrefix(allSections, project.root); const filePaths = sections.map((section) => section.path); const dependencyNames = new Set([ ...Object.keys(rootPackage?.dependencies ?? {}), ...Object.keys(rootPackage?.devDependencies ?? {}) ]); const frameworkIds = new Set(['framework:typescript']); const platformIds = new Set(); const capabilities = new Set(); if (project.targets.length > 0) frameworkIds.add('framework:nx'); if (dependencyNames.has('react') || sections.some((section) => section.path.endsWith('.tsx'))) frameworkIds.add('framework:react'); if (dependencyNames.has('vite') || filePaths.some((entry) => entry.includes('vite.config'))) frameworkIds.add('framework:vite'); if (dependencyNames.has('playwright') || project.targets.some((target) => target.includes('e2e'))) frameworkIds.add('framework:playwright'); if (dependencyNames.has('vitest') || dependencyNames.has('jest') || project.targets.some((target) => target.includes('test'))) frameworkIds.add('framework:test-harness'); if (dependencyNames.has('puppeteer') || dependencyNames.has('playwright-extra')) frameworkIds.add('framework:web-automation'); if (dependencyNames.has('googleapis') || dependencyNames.has('@google/clasp')) frameworkIds.add('framework:google-apps-script'); if (project.tags.includes('platform:web') || project.root.startsWith('apps/chrome-extensions/')) { platformIds.add('platform:web-runtime'); } if (project.tags.includes('platform:node') || project.category === 'tools' || project.root.startsWith('apps/documentation-scraper')) { platformIds.add('platform:node-runtime'); } if (project.root.startsWith('apps/chrome-extensions/') || project.tags.includes('scope:chrome-ext')) { platformIds.add('platform:chrome-extension-mv3'); capabilities.add('chrome-extension'); } if (dependencyNames.has('googleapis') || filePaths.some((filePath) => filePath.includes('google-apps-script'))) { platformIds.add('platform:google-apps-script'); } const capabilityMatchers = [ ['service-worker', /service_worker\/|background\./], ['content-script', /\/content(?:\/|\.ts|\.tsx)/], ['sidepanel-ui', /sidepanel/], ['popup-ui', /popup/], ['watch-runtime', /watch/], ['inspector-runtime', /inspector/], ['telemetry', /telemetry|metrics|run-log/], ['storage-contracts', /storage|session-state|config/], ['authentication', /auth/], ['automation', /automation|recipe|flow/], ['documentation', /documentation|README|docs\//], ['provider-integration', /platforms|integrations/] ]; for (const [capability, pattern] of capabilityMatchers) { if (filePaths.some((filePath) => pattern.test(filePath))) { capabilities.add(capability); } } const imports = new Set(); for (const section of sections) { for (const match of section.content.matchAll(/(?:from|import)\s*[('"`]([^'"`]+)['"`]/g)) { imports.add(match[1]); } } const dependencyRoots = new Set(); for (const imported of imports) { for (const alias of pathAliases) { if (alias.alias === imported) { dependencyRoots.add(alias.destination.split('/src/')[0]); } else if (alias.alias.endsWith('*')) { const prefix = alias.alias.slice(0, -1); if (imported.startsWith(prefix)) { const remainder = imported.slice(prefix.length); dependencyRoots.add(alias.destination.replace('*', remainder).split('/src/')[0]); } } } } const verificationCommands = []; for (const command of Object.values(project.targetCommands)) { if (command) verificationCommands.push(command); } if (verificationCommands.length === 0) { verificationCommands.push(`pnpm exec nx run ${project.name}:test`); verificationCommands.push(`pnpm exec nx run ${project.name}:build`); } const chromeApis = countChromeApis(sections); return { ...project, frameworkIds: [...frameworkIds], platformIds: [...platformIds], capabilities: [...capabilities], dependencyRoots: [...dependencyRoots], verificationCommands: verificationCommands.slice(0, 6), chromeApis, fileCount: sections.length, sectionHashes: sections.slice(0, 20).map((section) => sha1(section.path)) }; } function buildSystems(projects) { const systems = new Map(); for (const project of projects) { const rootSegments = project.root.split('/'); const systemPath = rootSegments.length >= 2 ? `${rootSegments[0]}/${rootSegments[1]}` : project.root; const systemId = makeId('system', systemPath); const existing = systems.get(systemId) ?? { id: systemId, name: systemPath, path: systemPath, projectIds: [] }; existing.projectIds.push(project.id); systems.set(systemId, existing); project.systemId = systemId; } return [...systems.values()].sort((left, right) => left.name.localeCompare(right.name)); } function buildFrameworkCatalog(projects, rootPackage) { const frameworkNameMap = { 'framework:typescript': 'TypeScript', 'framework:nx': 'Nx', 'framework:react': 'React', 'framework:vite': 'Vite', 'framework:playwright': 'Playwright', 'framework:test-harness': 'Test Harnesses', 'framework:web-automation': 'Browser Automation', 'framework:google-apps-script': 'Google Apps Script' }; const frameworkIds = new Set(projects.flatMap((project) => project.frameworkIds)); if (Object.keys(rootPackage?.dependencies ?? {}).includes('docx')) frameworkIds.add('framework:document-generation'); if (frameworkIds.has('framework:document-generation')) { frameworkNameMap['framework:document-generation'] = 'Document Generation'; } return [...frameworkIds].map((frameworkId) => ({ id: frameworkId, name: frameworkNameMap[frameworkId] ?? frameworkId.replace(/^framework:/, '').replace(/-/g, ' ') })); } function buildPlatformCatalog(projects) { const platformNameMap = { 'platform:web-runtime': 'Web Runtime', 'platform:node-runtime': 'Node Runtime', 'platform:chrome-extension-mv3': 'Chrome Extension MV3', 'platform:google-apps-script': 'Google Apps Script' }; const platformIds = new Set(projects.flatMap((project) => project.platformIds)); return [...platformIds].map((platformId) => ({ id: platformId, name: platformNameMap[platformId] ?? platformId.replace(/^platform:/, '').replace(/-/g, ' ') })); } function buildRulePacks(ruleFiles) { const grouped = groupBy(ruleFiles, (ruleFile) => ruleFile.folder); return [...grouped.entries()].map(([folder, files]) => ({ id: makeId('rule-pack', folder), name: folder.split('/').slice(-1)[0].replace(/[-_]+/g, ' '), folder, ruleIds: files.map((file) => file.id), descriptions: files.map((file) => file.description).slice(0, 5) })); } function buildExistingVisualizations(diagramSections) { return diagramSections.map((section) => ({ id: makeId('diagram', section.path), path: section.path, title: titleFromPath(section.path), projectName: projectNameFromPath(section.path), content: section.content })); } function buildTaskStates(taskStateSections) { return taskStateSections.map((section) => { const json = tryJson(section.content, {}); return { id: makeId('task-state', section.path), path: section.path, project: json.project ?? projectNameFromPath(section.path), currentPhase: json.currentPhase ?? json.sdlcPhase ?? 'unknown', activeBranch: json.activeBranch ?? null, verificationCommands: json.nextCommandSet ?? [], doneCriteria: json.doneCriteria ?? [], objective: json.objective ?? null }; }); } function buildAgentEnvironments(sections) { const environments = []; const paths = sections.map((section) => section.path); const cursorRuleCount = paths.filter((entry) => entry.startsWith('.cursor/rules/') && entry.endsWith('.mdc')).length; const claudeSettings = sections.find((section) => section.path === '.claude/settings.json'); const codexConfig = sections.find((section) => section.path === '.codex/config.toml'); const mcpConfig = sections.find((section) => section.path === '.mcp.json'); const claudeGuide = sections.find((section) => section.path === 'CLAUDE.md'); const agentsGuide = sections.find((section) => section.path === 'AGENTS.md'); if (cursorRuleCount > 0 || paths.includes('.cursor/rules')) { environments.push({ id: makeId('environment', 'cursor'), tool: 'cursor', name: 'Cursor', ruleCount: cursorRuleCount, paths: paths.filter((entry) => entry.startsWith('.cursor/')).slice(0, 40), hasProjectRules: cursorRuleCount > 0, hasAgentMarkdown: paths.includes('AGENTS.md') }); } if (claudeSettings || claudeGuide) { const settingsJson = claudeSettings ? tryJson(claudeSettings.content, {}) : {}; environments.push({ id: makeId('environment', 'claude'), tool: 'claude', name: 'Claude Code', paths: paths.filter((entry) => entry.startsWith('.claude/') || entry === 'CLAUDE.md').slice(0, 40), hasSettings: Boolean(claudeSettings), hasGuide: Boolean(claudeGuide), hasHooks: Boolean(settingsJson?.hooks), hasMcpConfig: Boolean(mcpConfig) }); } if (paths.some((entry) => entry.startsWith('.codex/')) || codexConfig || agentsGuide) { environments.push({ id: makeId('environment', 'codex'), tool: 'codex', name: 'Codex', paths: paths.filter((entry) => entry.startsWith('.codex/') || entry === 'AGENTS.md').slice(0, 40), hasConfig: Boolean(codexConfig), hasAgentsMd: Boolean(agentsGuide), hasMcpConfig: Boolean(mcpConfig) }); } if (paths.some((entry) => entry.startsWith('.foundry/'))) { environments.push({ id: makeId('environment', 'foundry'), tool: 'foundry', name: 'Flagship Foundry', paths: paths.filter((entry) => entry.startsWith('.foundry/')).slice(0, 40), hasContinuity: paths.some( (entry) => entry.includes('.foundry/projects/') && entry.endsWith('current-task.json') ) }); } if (mcpConfig) { const json = tryJson(mcpConfig.content, {}); environments.push({ id: makeId('environment', 'mcp'), tool: 'mcp', name: 'Shared MCP Config', paths: ['.mcp.json'], serverCount: Object.keys(json?.mcpServers ?? {}).length }); } return environments; } function buildManifest({ request, sections }) { const rootPackage = extractRootConfig(sections, 'package.json'); const nxConfig = extractRootConfig(sections, 'nx.json'); const tsconfigBase = extractRootConfig(sections, 'tsconfig.base.json'); const pnpmWorkspaceText = sections.find((section) => section.path === 'pnpm-workspace.yaml')?.content ?? ''; const pathAliases = extractPathAliases(tsconfigBase ?? {}); const topology = detectTopology(sections, rootPackage); const rawProjects = extractProjectManifests(sections); const projects = rawProjects.map((project) => inferProjectAttributes(project, sections, rootPackage ?? {}, pathAliases)); const systems = buildSystems(projects); const frameworks = buildFrameworkCatalog(projects, rootPackage ?? {}); const platforms = buildPlatformCatalog(projects); const ruleFiles = sections.filter((section) => section.path.endsWith('.mdc') || section.path.includes('.cursor/rules/')).map(parseRuleFile); const rulePacks = buildRulePacks(ruleFiles); const existingVisualizations = buildExistingVisualizations(sections.filter((section) => section.path.endsWith('.mmd'))); const taskStates = buildTaskStates(sections.filter((section) => section.path.endsWith('current-task.json'))); const agentEnvironments = buildAgentEnvironments(sections); const chromeApiUsage = countChromeApis(sections.filter((section) => section.path.startsWith('apps/') || section.path.startsWith('libs/') || section.path.startsWith('tools/'))); const workspacePackages = parseYamlList(pnpmWorkspaceText); const projectRootsByRoot = new Map(projects.map((project) => [project.root, project])); for (const project of projects) { project.dependencies = project.dependencyRoots .map((root) => projectRootsByRoot.get(root)?.id) .filter(Boolean); } return { id: request.ecosystemId ?? slugify(request.name ?? request.source.workspaceRoot ?? 'imported-ecosystem'), name: request.name ?? 'Imported Ecosystem', importedAt: nowIso(), source: request.source, topology, workspacePackages, manifests: { rootPackageName: rootPackage?.name ?? 'unknown', packageManager: rootPackage?.packageManager ?? 'unknown', nodeEngine: rootPackage?.engines?.node ?? null, nxDefaultBase: nxConfig?.defaultBase ?? null, pathAliasCount: pathAliases.length }, frameworks, platforms, projects, systems, ruleFiles, rulePacks, existingVisualizations, taskStates, agentEnvironments, knowledgeBase: { chromeApiDocsAvailable: sections.some((section) => section.source === 'chrome-api-docs'), chromeApiUsage: chromeApiUsage.slice(0, 20), ruleCount: ruleFiles.length, diagramCount: existingVisualizations.length, taskStateCount: taskStates.length, agentEnvironmentCount: agentEnvironments.length }, findings: [ `${projects.length} projects detected`, `${systems.length} system groups detected`, `${ruleFiles.length} rule files imported`, `${existingVisualizations.length} existing Mermaid diagrams ingested`, `${taskStates.length} current task states ingested`, `${agentEnvironments.length} agent environments detected` ] }; } function renderImportReport(ecosystem) { const topApis = ecosystem.knowledgeBase.chromeApiUsage.slice(0, 8) .map((entry) => `- \`${entry.api}\`: ${entry.count} references`) .join('\n'); const topSystems = ecosystem.systems .map((system) => `- ${system.name}: ${system.projectIds.length} projects`) .join('\n'); const topFrameworks = ecosystem.frameworks.map((framework) => `- ${framework.name}`).join('\n'); const topPlatforms = ecosystem.platforms.map((platform) => `- ${platform.name}`).join('\n'); const topEnvironments = (ecosystem.agentEnvironments ?? []).length > 0 ? ecosystem.agentEnvironments.map((environment) => `- ${environment.name}: ${environment.paths.join(', ')}`).join('\n') : '- none detected'; return `# Current Workspace Import Report\n\n## Topology\n- Kind: **${ecosystem.topology.kind}**\n- Confidence: **${ecosystem.topology.confidence}**\n- Reasons: ${ecosystem.topology.reasons.join(', ')}\n\n## Detected Scope\n- Projects: **${ecosystem.projects.length}**\n- Systems: **${ecosystem.systems.length}**\n- Rule files: **${ecosystem.ruleFiles.length}**\n- Existing Mermaid diagrams: **${ecosystem.existingVisualizations.length}**\n- Current task states: **${ecosystem.taskStates.length}**\n- Agent environments: **${ecosystem.agentEnvironments.length}**\n\n## Agent Environment Parity\n${topEnvironments}\n\n## System Groups\n${topSystems}\n\n## Framework Coverage\n${topFrameworks}\n\n## Platform Coverage\n${topPlatforms}\n\n## Highest Chrome API Usage Signals\n${topApis || '- none detected'}\n\n## Immediate Planning Implications\n- Treat the repository as a graph of apps, libs, tools, rules, diagrams, task states, and agent-environment contracts.\n- Expand blast radius beyond touched files when a change touches shared Chrome extension patterns, shared libraries, workflow rule packs, or shared environment rules.\n- Preserve manual approval as the default until a plan explicitly opts into auto approval.\n- Use imported diagrams and task states as continuity artifacts, not as decoration.\n`; } function buildGraph(ecosystem) { const graph = createEmptyGraph({ ecosystemId: ecosystem.id, ecosystemName: ecosystem.name }); upsertNode(graph, { id: `ecosystem:${ecosystem.id}`, type: 'ecosystem', name: ecosystem.name, tags: [ecosystem.topology.kind], refs: ['manifest.json'], properties: { topology: ecosystem.topology.kind, importedAt: ecosystem.importedAt, projectCount: ecosystem.projects.length } }); upsertNode(graph, { id: `repo:${ecosystem.id}`, type: 'repo', name: ecosystem.manifests.rootPackageName, properties: { packageManager: ecosystem.manifests.packageManager, nodeEngine: ecosystem.manifests.nodeEngine } }); addEdge(graph, { id: makeId('edge', `${ecosystem.id}-contains-repo`), type: 'contains', source: `ecosystem:${ecosystem.id}`, target: `repo:${ecosystem.id}` }); for (const system of ecosystem.systems) { upsertNode(graph, { id: system.id, type: 'system', name: system.name, properties: { path: system.path, projectCount: system.projectIds.length } }); addEdge(graph, { id: makeId('edge', `${ecosystem.id}-${system.id}`), type: 'contains', source: `repo:${ecosystem.id}`, target: system.id }); } for (const framework of ecosystem.frameworks) { upsertNode(graph, { id: framework.id, type: 'framework', name: framework.name, properties: { category: 'framework' } }); addEdge(graph, { id: makeId('edge', `${ecosystem.id}-${framework.id}`), type: 'uses-framework', source: `repo:${ecosystem.id}`, target: framework.id }); } for (const platform of ecosystem.platforms) { upsertNode(graph, { id: platform.id, type: 'platform', name: platform.name, properties: { category: 'platform' } }); addEdge(graph, { id: makeId('edge', `${ecosystem.id}-${platform.id}`), type: 'targets-platform', source: `repo:${ecosystem.id}`, target: platform.id }); } for (const pack of ecosystem.rulePacks) { upsertNode(graph, { id: pack.id, type: 'rule-pack', name: pack.name, properties: { folder: pack.folder, ruleCount: pack.ruleIds.length } }); addEdge(graph, { id: makeId('edge', `${ecosystem.id}-${pack.id}`), type: 'governed-by', source: `repo:${ecosystem.id}`, target: pack.id }); } for (const environment of ecosystem.agentEnvironments ?? []) { upsertNode(graph, { id: environment.id, type: 'environment', name: environment.name, refs: environment.paths, properties: { tool: environment.tool, pathCount: environment.paths.length, ruleCount: environment.ruleCount ?? 0, hasMcpConfig: environment.hasMcpConfig ?? false } }); addEdge(graph, { id: makeId('edge', `${ecosystem.id}-${environment.id}`), type: 'configured-with', source: `repo:${ecosystem.id}`, target: environment.id }); } for (const project of ecosystem.projects) { upsertNode(graph, { id: project.id, type: 'project', name: project.name, tags: project.tags, refs: [project.root, ...(project.sourceRoot ? [project.sourceRoot] : [])], properties: { path: project.root, projectType: project.projectType, targets: project.targets, targetCommands: project.targetCommands, frameworkIds: project.frameworkIds, platformIds: project.platformIds, capabilityIds: project.capabilities, verificationCommands: project.verificationCommands, systemId: project.systemId, topChromeApis: project.chromeApis.slice(0, 8) } }); addEdge(graph, { id: makeId('edge', `${project.systemId}-${project.id}`), type: 'contains', source: project.systemId, target: project.id }); for (const frameworkId of project.frameworkIds) { addEdge(graph, { id: makeId('edge', `${project.id}-${frameworkId}`), type: 'uses-framework', source: project.id, target: frameworkId }); } for (const platformId of project.platformIds) { addEdge(graph, { id: makeId('edge', `${project.id}-${platformId}`), type: 'targets-platform', source: project.id, target: platformId }); } for (const dependencyId of project.dependencies ?? []) { addEdge(graph, { id: makeId('edge', `${project.id}-${dependencyId}`), type: 'depends-on', source: project.id, target: dependencyId }); } for (const pack of ecosystem.rulePacks) { const pathTokens = project.root.split('/'); if (pack.folder.includes('15-chome-extension') && project.platformIds.includes('platform:chrome-extension-mv3')) { addEdge(graph, { id: makeId('edge', `${project.id}-${pack.id}-pack`), type: 'governed-by', source: project.id, target: pack.id }); } else if (pack.folder.includes('10-observability') && project.capabilities.includes('telemetry')) { addEdge(graph, { id: makeId('edge', `${project.id}-${pack.id}-pack`), type: 'governed-by', source: project.id, target: pack.id }); } else if (pack.folder.includes('03-workflow')) { addEdge(graph, { id: makeId('edge', `${project.id}-${pack.id}-pack`), type: 'governed-by', source: project.id, target: pack.id }); } else if (pack.folder.includes('02-architecture') && pathTokens[0] === 'libs') { addEdge(graph, { id: makeId('edge', `${project.id}-${pack.id}-pack`), type: 'governed-by', source: project.id, target: pack.id }); } } } for (const project of ecosystem.projects) { for (const otherProject of ecosystem.projects) { if (project.id >= otherProject.id) continue; const sharedTags = project.tags.filter((tag) => otherProject.tags.includes(tag)); if (sharedTags.length >= 2) { addEdge(graph, { id: makeId('edge', `${project.id}-${otherProject.id}-pattern`), type: 'shares-pattern', source: project.id, target: otherProject.id, properties: { sharedTags } }); } } } for (const diagram of ecosystem.existingVisualizations) { const diagramNodeId = diagram.id; upsertNode(graph, { id: diagramNodeId, type: 'diagram', name: diagram.title, refs: [diagram.path], properties: { path: diagram.path, projectName: diagram.projectName } }); const owningProject = ecosystem.projects.find((project) => project.name === diagram.projectName); if (owningProject) { addEdge(graph, { id: makeId('edge', `${owningProject.id}-${diagramNodeId}`), type: 'visualized-by', source: owningProject.id, target: diagramNodeId }); } } for (const taskState of ecosystem.taskStates) { const stateNodeId = taskState.id; upsertNode(graph, { id: stateNodeId, type: 'task-state', name: `${taskState.project} ${taskState.currentPhase}`, refs: [taskState.path], properties: { project: taskState.project, currentPhase: taskState.currentPhase, activeBranch: taskState.activeBranch, verificationCommands: taskState.verificationCommands } }); const owningProject = ecosystem.projects.find((project) => project.name === taskState.project); if (owningProject) { addEdge(graph, { id: makeId('edge', `${owningProject.id}-${stateNodeId}`), type: 'has-state', source: owningProject.id, target: stateNodeId }); } } graph.generatedAt = ecosystem.importedAt; return graph; } async function writeEcosystemArtifacts(ecosystem, graph) { const ecosystemRoot = path.join(stateRoot, 'ecosystems', ecosystem.id); const visualizationsDir = path.join(ecosystemRoot, 'visualizations'); const profilesDir = path.join(ecosystemRoot, 'profiles'); const analysisDir = path.join(ecosystemRoot, 'analysis'); await ensureDir(ecosystemRoot); await writeJson(path.join(ecosystemRoot, 'manifest.json'), ecosystem); await saveGraph(graph); const visualizationSpecs = buildVisualizationSpecs({ ecosystem, graph }); await writeVisualizationSet(visualizationsDir, visualizationSpecs); const profiles = generateSmeProfiles({ ecosystem }); ===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/packages/core/src/ralph-compiler.mjs===import path from 'node:path'; import { readJson, writeJson, slugify } from './io.mjs'; /** * Derives a branch name suggestion from a task title and id. * * @param {string} taskId * @param {string} title * @returns {string} */ function branchName(taskId, title) { const shortId = taskId.split(':').pop() ?? taskId; return `ralph/${slugify(shortId)}-${slugify(title).slice(0, 40)}`; } /** * Extracts all tasks from a Foundry plan into a flat array. * * Supports two plan shapes: * - createPlan() output: { projectPlans: [{ tasks: [...] }] } * - scope-chunker output: { workOrders: [...] } * * @param {object} plan * @returns {Array<object>} */ function extractTasks(plan) { // createPlan() shape if (Array.isArray(plan.projectPlans)) { return plan.projectPlans.flatMap((projectPlan) => projectPlan.tasks ?? ===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/packages/core/src/ralph-state-sync.mjs===import path from 'node:path'; import { readJson, writeJson, readText, exists } from './io.mjs'; import { transitionPhase } from './continuity.mjs'; /** * Parses the Ralph progress.txt log to extract which story IDs Ralph * has explicitly reported as completed within its progress entries. * * Ralph progress entries follow the format: * ## [Date/Time] - [Story ID] * * @param {string} progressText * @returns {Set<string>} Set of story IDs mentioned in progress entries. */ function parseCompletedFromProgress(progressText) { const completed = new Set(); // Match lines like: ## 2024-01-01 - US-001 const entryPattern = /^##\s+[^\-]+-\s*(.+)$/gm; let match; while ((match = entryPattern.exec(progressText)) !== null) { const storyId = match[1].trim(); if (storyId) { completed.add(storyId); } } return completed; } /** * Reads the prd.json at prdPath and applies progress from the sibling * progress.txt back into Foundry continuity state. * * For each story where `passes === true` (set by Ralph after it verifies a * story), the sync marks it completed in the report. JSON.stringify(result.body) : result.body; res.writeHead(result.statusCode, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }); res.end(responseBody); } async function handleHealth(config) { const providerNames = Object.keys(config.providers || {}); const checks = await Promise.all( providerNames.map(async (name) => { const providerConfig = config.providers[name]; const reachable = await isReachable(providerConfig.baseUrl); return { name, baseUrl: providerConfig.baseUrl, reachable }; }) ); const status = checks.every((c) => c.reachable) ? 'ok' : 'degraded'; return { status, providers: checks }; } // --------------------------------------------------------------------------- // Server factory // --------------------------------------------------------------------------- export function createGatewayServer() { const config = loadRoutingConfig(); if (!config) { process.stderr.write( '[model-gateway] WARN: Running without routing config — all requests will fail\n' ); } // Warn early if Anthropic key is absent if (config && config.providers?.anthropic?.apiKeyEnv) { if (!process.env[config.providers.anthropic.apiKeyEnv]) { process.stderr.write( `[model-gateway] WARN: ${config.providers.anthropic.apiKeyEnv} is not set — running in local-only mode\n` ); } } return http.createServer(async (req, res) => { try { if (req.method === 'POST' && req.url === '/v1/chat/completions') { if (!config) { res.writeHead(503, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }); res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Gateway misconfigured: routing config not loaded' })); return; } await handleChatCompletions(config, req, res); return; } if (req.method === 'GET' && req.url === '/health') { if (!config) { res.writeHead(503, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }); res.end(JSON.stringify({ status: 'error', error: 'Routing config not loaded' })); return; } const healthPayload = await handleHealth(config); const code = healthPayload.status === 'ok' ? 200 : 207; res.writeHead(code, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }); res.end(JSON.stringify(healthPayload)); return; } res.writeHead(404, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }); res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Not found' })); } catch (err) { process.stderr.write(`[model-gateway] ERROR: ${err.message}\n`); res.writeHead(500, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }); res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Internal gateway error', details: err.message })); } }); } // --------------------------------------------------------------------------- // Entrypoint (direct execution) // --------------------------------------------------------------------------- if (import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`) { const server = createGatewayServer(); server.listen(GATEWAY_PORT, () => { process.stderr.write(`[model-gateway] Listening on http://localhost:${GATEWAY_PORT}\n`); }); }

===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/QUICKSTART.md===# Flagship Foundry — Quickstart Guide This guide gets you from zero to a running project graph in about five minutes. It assumes Node.js 18+ is installed and that you have a project directory you want to ingest. --- ## Section 1: Glossary of Terms **Ecosystem** — Your entire project, repo, or monorepo treated as a single named entity in the Foundry graph. Every import, plan, and blast-radius query is scoped to an ecosystem ID. **Graph** — The structured map of your project: systems, components, dependencies, rules, and task states. The graph is the single source of truth the orchestrator and all agents reason against. **Phase** — One of 11 lifecycle stages that work moves through: `discover → define → visualize → architect → plan → implement → verify → release → operate → diagnose → improve`. Each phase has explicit entry criteria (Definition of Ready) and exit criteria (Definition of Done). **Work Order** — A bounded task assigned to a specific agent. A work order contains a goal, explicit file scope, input contracts, acceptance criteria, and a verification plan. The builder will not start without one. **Continuity State** — Machine-readable JSON stored at `.codex/projects/<project>/current-task.json`. It records exactly where you are in the lifecycle so any agent — or a fresh Claude Code session — can resume deterministically without relying on chat history. **Guardrail Pack** — A policy set that constrains what an agent can do in a given context. Examples: "TypeScript strict mode with no `any`", "no new npm dependencies without explicit approval", "do not modify files outside declared scope". Guardrails live in `.cursor/rules/` and are referenced in work orders. **Principle Card** — An operating principle attached to a piece of work. Examples: `blast-radius-before-build` (understand downstream impact before starting), `contract-first` (define interfaces before writing implementation). Principle cards are lightweight, portable reminders that travel with work orders. **Agent** — A specialized AI role in the Foundry system. Each agent has a defined phase binding, a set of allowed tools, and a forbidden-behaviors list. See Section 6 for the full roster. **Skill** — A slash command that triggers a structured, multi-step workflow. `/define-intent` walks through the full discover-to-architect pipeline; `/scope-chunker` decomposes a feature into typed work orders. Skills are listed in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and invoked in Claude Code. **DoR / DoD** — Definition of Ready (gates that must pass before a phase starts) and Definition of Done (gates that must pass before a phase closes). The orchestrator evaluates both automatically. No work moves forward without them. **Artifact Authority Stack** — A precedence hierarchy that resolves conflicts: doctrine and operating principles beat everything; charter and guardrails beat schemas; schemas and ADRs beat diagrams; diagrams beat code; code beats tests. When two artifacts contradict each other, the higher-authority artifact wins. **MCP** — Model Context Protocol. The interoperability layer that lets Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex all share the same Foundry tools and graph state without duplicating logic. MCP servers expose Foundry capabilities as callable tools. **Focus View** — A filtered, query-scoped slice of the graph showing only the systems and components relevant to a specific change or question. Focus views reduce noise and keep agents working on what matters. **Blast Radius** — The set of systems, components, and consumers that would be affected by a proposed change. Always compute blast radius before starting implementation to understand scope and risk. **Intent Packet** — The structured output of the discover-to-architect pipeline: a problem statement, scope boundaries, acceptance criteria, C4 diagrams, and principle cards. The intent packet is the contract between human intent and implementation work. --- ## Section 2: 5-Minute Setup ```bash cd flagship-foundry-work npm install # Ingest your project node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs import path/to/your-import-config.json # Start the API node apps/control-plane/src/server.mjs # Browse your project graph curl http://localhost:4010/ecosystems ``` The `import` command reads your project directory, builds a graph, and writes the result to `state/ecosystems/<ecosystemId>/`. Subsequent commands (blast, focus, plan) all read from that persisted state. --- ## Section 3: Import Config for emcnotary-website The import config is a small JSON file that tells the ingestion pipeline which project to read and what to call it. The config for the EMC Notary Website project is at `examples/emcnotary/import-config.json`: ```json { "ecosystemId": "emcnotary-website", "name": "EMC Notary Website", "source": { "type": "filesystem", "workspaceRoot": "/Users/evanmccall/Projects/emcnotary-website" } } ``` Run it with: ```bash node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs import examples/emcnotary/import-config.json ``` ### Generic template Use this template as the starting point for any other project: ```json { "ecosystemId": "your-project-id", "name": "Your Project Name", "source": { "type": "filesystem", "workspaceRoot": "/absolute/path/to/your/project" } } ``` - `ecosystemId` must be a lowercase, hyphen-separated identifier. It is used as the directory name under `state/ecosystems/` and as the primary key in all blast-radius and plan queries. - `workspaceRoot` must be an absolute path to the root of the project you want to ingest. --- ## Section 4: Using the SDLC Workflow in Claude Code 1. Open Claude Code in the workspace root (`SDLC - Visual - Workflow - SoftwareEngineering-NewAge/`). 2. Say "I want to add a feature to my-project." The orchestrator reads the continuity state, determines the current phase, and routes you to `discover` if this is a new feature. 3. Use `/define-intent` to walk through structured intent capture: problem statement, scope, acceptance criteria, C4 diagrams, and principle cards. This produces an intent packet. 4. Use `/scope-chunker` to decompose the intent packet into typed work orders with explicit file scope, model routing, and acceptance criteria for each slice. 5. The builder agent receives each work order and implements within the declared scope. The verifier validates independently — it does not trust the builder's claims, it re-runs the verification commands itself. 6. The orchestrator evaluates the Definition of Done, updates the continuity state, and advances to the next phase. Each phase transition writes to `.codex/projects/<project>/current-task.json`, so you can close Claude Code, come back the next day, and resume from exactly where you left off by running the `nextCommandSet` commands listed in that file. --- ## Section 5: CLI Command Reference All commands are run from the `flagship-foundry-work/` directory: ``` node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs <command> [args] ``` | Command | Description | Example | |---------|-------------|---------| | `import` | Ingest a project from the filesystem into the Foundry graph. Reads an import config JSON and writes ecosystem state to `state/ecosystems/`. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs import examples/emcnotary/import-config.json` | | `visualize` | Run import and return the visualization data (Mermaid diagrams, graph views) for the ingested ecosystem. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs visualize examples/emcnotary/import-config.json` | | `profiles` | Run import and return the component profiles (tags, types, scopes, platform assignments) for the ecosystem. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs profiles examples/emcnotary/import-config.json` | | `blast` | Compute the blast radius for a given change query against an already-imported ecosystem. Reads a blast-request JSON with `ecosystemId` and `query`. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs blast path/to/blast-request.json` | | `knowledge` | Ingest a knowledge manifest (documentation, runbooks, ADRs) into the knowledge base for a project. Reads a manifest JSON that lists source documents. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs knowledge path/to/knowledge-manifest.json` | | `gap` | Analyze gaps between the project graph and the knowledge base — surfaces undocumented components, missing ADRs, and unknown dependencies. Reads a gap-request JSON with `ecosystemId` and optional `knowledgeBaseId`. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs gap path/to/gap-request.json` | | `focus` | Generate a focus view — a filtered slice of the graph scoped to a specific query. Reads a focus-request JSON with `ecosystemId` and `query`. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs focus path/to/focus-request.json` | | `plan` | Create an implementation plan from a change request. Reads a change-request JSON and produces a structured plan with work orders. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs plan path/to/change-request.json` | | `bootstrap` | One-shot command that runs import, optional knowledge ingestion, and optional plan creation in sequence. Useful for cold-starting a new project. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs bootstrap examples/emcnotary/import-config.json` | | `run` | Execute a plan in simulate mode. Takes a plan ID (from a previous `plan` command) and runs through all work orders, reporting outcomes without applying changes. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs run <planId>` | | `show-plan` | Print a previously created plan in full. Takes a plan ID. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs show-plan <planId>` | | `scaffold-env` | Scaffold a new environment configuration from a named preset. Use `--dry-run` to preview the output without writing files. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs scaffold-env node-ts ./my-new-service --dry-run` | | `init-project` | Initialize a new project with SDLC continuity state. Creates `.codex/projects/<name>/current-task.json` and a project charter. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs init-project emcnotary "Notary website SDLC"` | | `status` | Show the current SDLC phase, blockers, and done criteria for a project. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs status emcnotary` | | `resume` | Print a resume checklist for interrupted work — current phase, next commands, blockers, and done criteria. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs resume emcnotary` | | `transition` | Transition a project to a new SDLC phase. Validates the transition and updates continuity state. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs transition emcnotary define "Scope defined"` | | `add-blocker` | Record a blocker on the current phase. Sets the phase status to blocked. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs add-blocker emcnotary "Waiting on API keys"` | | `resolve-blocker` | Resolve a blocker by index (0-based). Restores the phase to in-progress if no blockers remain. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs resolve-blocker emcnotary 0` | | `compile-ralph` | Compile a Foundry plan into a Ralph-compatible PRD (prd.json) for autonomous execution. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs compile-ralph state/ecosystems/my-project/plans/plan-001.json` | | `sync-ralph` | Sync Ralph execution progress back to Foundry continuity state. | `node apps/orchestrator-cli/src/main.mjs sync-ralph ./ralph-prd.json emcnotary` | Pass no arguments or `--help` to print the command list and usage summary. --- ## Section 6: What Each Agent Does (Plain English) **Orchestrator** — The conductor. It activates at the start of any new feature, bug triage, or resumed session. It reads the continuity state, determines which lifecycle phase you are in, evaluates the Definition of Ready for the next phase, and routes the work to the right specialist. It also enforces the Definition of Done before closing a phase and writes the updated continuity state. The orchestrator never writes code directly — it only delegates. Its outputs are updated task state, phase completion summaries, and handoff documents. **Context Curator** — The research assistant. It activates before a specialist agent begins work whenever a clean, bounded working context is needed. It reads the continuity state, searches the codebase for relevant files and schemas, identifies applicable cursor rules and ADRs, and assembles a structured context packet. It is read-only — it never modifies files. Its output is a markdown context packet that the receiving agent uses to avoid hallucination and stay focused. **Systems Architect** — The designer. It activates during the discover, define, visualize, and architect phases. It clarifies ambiguous intent, defines system boundaries, produces C4 diagrams (context, container, component, sequence), writes Architecture Decision Records, and defines the contracts and schemas that constrain implementation. It does not write implementation code. Its outputs are ADRs, interface definitions, scope documents, and acceptance criteria. **Builder** — The implementer. It activates only during the implement phase, after the orchestrator has issued a work order with explicit file scope and contracts. It reads existing code before writing, makes the minimal changes required by the work order, writes tests for new behavior, and runs the verification commands from the work order before reporting completion. It will not touch files outside its declared scope. Its outputs are changed source files, test files, and a verification report. **Verifier** — The skeptic. It activates after the builder reports completion and during the verify and release phases. It re-runs all verification commands independently — it does not trust the builder's claimed results. It inspects changed files for contract compliance, test coverage, scope violations, and regressions. It is read-only and cannot modify source files. Its output is a PASS / FAIL / MIXED / INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE verdict with a per-criterion evidence table. **Security Reviewer** — The threat modeler. It activates during the architect and verify phases, and whenever security-sensitive changes are in scope. It checks for hardcoded secrets, trust boundary violations, supply-chain risks, overly broad permissions, and OWASP Top 10 patterns. It is read-only. Its output is a security review report with severity-rated findings and a release recommendation (CLEAR / FINDINGS / BLOCKS RELEASE). **Performance Reviewer** — The profiler. It activates during the verify and diagnose phases. It checks for bundle size regressions, unnecessary re-renders, memory leaks, blocking I/O, and algorithmic hot paths. It is read-only and will not claim performance issues without measurement or code evidence. Its output is a performance review report with severity-rated findings and a release recommendation. **Docs & Release Agent** — The packager. It activates during the document, improve, and release phases. It converts execution history into handoff documents, release notes, continuity patches, and learning records. It updates runbooks when operational procedures change. It will not fabricate test results or merge speculation into documented fact. Its outputs are the release package, updated runbooks, continuity state patches, and learning records that feed back into future work. --- ## Section 7: Three Operating Loops The Foundry lifecycle is organized into three loops. Each loop feeds the next. ### Loop 1: Intent to Architecture Phases: `discover → define → visualize → architect` This loop answers "what are we building and why?" before any code is written. The context curator assembles available information, the systems architect clarifies scope and constraints, C4 diagrams make the structure explicit, and ADRs capture the key decisions. The loop exits when the intent packet is complete and the Definition of Ready for the plan phase is satisfied. Use this loop for new features, significant refactors, or any time the problem is not yet well-defined. Skipping it is the most common cause of rework. ### Loop 2: Architecture to Implementation Phases: `plan → implement → verify → release` This loop answers "how do we build it correctly?" The orchestrator breaks the architecture into bounded implementation slices, the builder implements each slice within declared scope, the verifier validates each slice independently, and the docs agent packages the release. Every phase transition updates the continuity state. The loop exits when all acceptance criteria have passed verification and the release artifact is ready. ### Loop 3: Operate to Improve Phases: `operate → diagnose → improve` This loop answers "is it working in production, and what do we learn?" The performance reviewer baselines runtime behavior, the verifier and security reviewer diagnose production issues with evidence, and the docs agent captures learning records that update standards, runbooks, and future work orders. The loop feeds back into Loop 1 by enriching the context available for the next discover phase. --- ## Section 8: Next Steps - **CHARTER.md** (`.claude/CHARTER.md`) — The authority document for the Foundry system. Defines operating principles, agent hierarchy, and what humans own versus what agents own. - **RUNBOOK.md** (`.claude/RUNBOOK.md`) — Operational procedures for agent orchestration: how to resume interrupted work, how to recover from context collapse, how to escalate blockers. - **Flagship Handbook** (`docs/flagship_systems_sdlc_handbook.docx.md`) — The full reference for the SDLC system: phase definitions, artifact schemas, guardrail conventions, and the reasoning behind the design. - **Schemas** (`flagship-foundry-work/schemas/`) — JSON schemas for continuity state, work orders, and agent outputs. Useful when integrating external tools or writing custom scripts. - **Cursor Rules** (`.cursor/rules/`) — The guardrail packs applied during code review and agent execution. Start with `03-workflow/ai-sdlc-orchestrator.mdc` and the `nx-sdlc/RULE.md` for module boundary rules.
===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/README.md===# Flagship Foundry Flagship Foundry is a graph-native SDLC control plane for human plus AI orchestration. This repository now includes a working import, knowledge-ingestion, gap-analysis, focus-view, approval-aware planning, and run-control slice that starts from an existing workspace rather than assuming a greenfield implementation path. ## What is here - `apps/control-plane/` - HTTP API for import, knowledge ingestion, gap analysis, focus views, planning, approval, run control, and graph patching - `apps/orchestrator-cli/` - CLI for bootstrap, import, knowledge ingestion, gap analysis, focus views, planning, environment scaffold, and run simulation - `apps/cursor-companion/` - VS Code and Cursor companion surface with start, import, ingest, gap, plan, focus, approve, and run control actions - `packages/core/` - import pipeline, graph store, plans, runs, visualizations, focus views, knowledge ingestion, environment scaffold, SME profile generation, and catalogs - `knowledge/` - domain packs, framework registries, source presets, and agent plus skill blueprints - `schemas/` - contracts for import, graph, plans, runs, knowledge sources, documents, gap reports, focus views, runbooks, personas, guardrails, and fix memory - `runbooks/`, `personas/`, `guardrails/`, `configs/`, `ontology/` - process, role, policy, and routing catalogs - `environments/` - project-local parity templates for Cursor, Codex, and Claude Code - `examples/current-workspace/` - current ecosystem export bundle, requests, and generated artifacts - `examples/knowledge-sources/` - seed knowledge manifest and local documentation sources - `state/` - generated ecosystem manifests, graphs, knowledge bases, plans, runs, visualizations, and profile outputs ## Quick start ```bash npm run bootstrap:full-sample npm run api npm test ``` ## CI and release gates Blocking automation and the release evidence threshold are documented in **[docs/ci-release-gates.md](docs/ci-release-gates.md)** (ADR-009). GitHub Actions runs **`npm test`** plus **`npm run ci:targeted`** (orchestrator visualize smoke) from `flagship-foundry-work/`; workflow definition lives at **`.github/workflows/flagship-foundry-ci.yml`** in the parent workspace repository. Rollout, rollback, and incident documentation (how operator records link to plans, runs, and evidence) are defined in **[docs/rollout-rollback-incident-model.md](docs/rollout-rollback-incident-model.md)** (ADR-010). ## Continuity and `.foundry` Per **ADR-011**, machine-readable **project continuity** (task state) lives under **`.foundry/projects/<project>/current-task.json`** at the **workspace root** you choose when running `init-project`—not under `flagship-foundry-work/state/`. See **[docs/guides/ecosystem-onboarding.md](docs/guides/ecosystem-onboarding.md)** for a full import → knowledge → gap → plan → continuity walkthrough. - **Docker (optional):** [docs/docker-and-local-dev.md](docs/docker-and-local-dev.md) - **Cursor extension init patterns:** [docs/guides/cursor-extension-foundry-init.md](docs/guides/cursor-extension-foundry-init.md) ## Control-plane auth and trust boundary config ADR-006 Option B is enforced in the control plane: - non-loopback requests require a scoped bearer token - loopback (`127.0.0.1` / `::1`) can bypass auth in local dev - CORS only allows explicit origins (no wildcard) Set these variables before `npm run api`: ```bash # Required for non-loopback access export FLAGSHIP_CONTROL_PLANE_BEARER_TOKEN="replace-me" export FLAGSHIP_CONTROL_PLANE_BEARER_SCOPES="control-plane:read,control-plane:write,control-plane:execute" # Optional: multiple scoped tokens (overrides *_BEARER_* when set) # export FLAGSHIP_CONTROL_PLANE_TOKENS='[{"token":"token-a","scopes":["control-plane:read"]}]' # Optional local dev exception (default 1 = enabled) export FLAGSHIP_ALLOW_LOOPBACK_NO_AUTH=1 # Explicit CORS allowlist (comma-separated; no wildcard) export FLAGSHIP_CORS_ORIGINS="http://localhost:3000,http://localhost:4010" ``` ## Runtime adapter isolation and rollback boundary ADR-008 indicators are enforced for execute-mode runs: - run records include an explicit `isolation` contract (`run-scoped` workspace, default `workspace-only` writes) - run records include explicit `rollback` semantics (`pause`/`stop` preserve task evidence and timeline) - local-shell executor persists per-task evidence JSON under `state/run-workspaces/<run-id>/` - non-zero local-shell exits mark the task and run as failed while preserving artifacts for diagnosis ## Sample commands ```bash npm run import:sample npm run knowledge:sample npm run gap:sample npm run focus:sample npm run plan:sample ``` ## Primary URLs - `GET /health` - `POST /ingestion/workspace-import` - `POST /knowledge/ingest` - `POST /analysis/gaps` - `POST /analysis/focus` - `POST /planning/create` - `GET /planning/context?ecosystemId=&knowledgeBaseId=` - `POST /runs/start` (use `mode: execute` + `adapterId: adapter:local-shell` for real local execution) - `GET /runs/:id/evidence-bundle` - `POST /runs/:id/ralph-sync` (body: `prdPath`, `projectName`) - `POST /plans/:id/approve` - `GET|POST /plans/:id/debate` - `GET /projects/:id/gates` - `GET /swarm/registry` — `POST /swarm/orchestration-stub` - `GET /trace/forward|backward|file` — graph trace helpers - `GET /environments/detect?targetDir=` - `POST /environments/scaffold` See [docs/REPOSITORY_LAYOUT.md](docs/REPOSITORY_LAYOUT.md) for repo boundaries and [docs/source-of-truth-matrix.md](docs/source-of-truth-matrix.md) for artifact authority and sync direction. ## Current direction Start with the Cursor companion and terminal adapters while keeping the control plane framework-agnostic. Use import plus knowledge plus gap analysis to identify where doctrine, skills, runbooks, personas, and environment parity are still incomplete before wiring a real executor.

===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/runbooks/learning-and-memory-curation.md===# Learning and Memory Curation Runbook ## Purpose Convert completed work and resolved incidents into reusable intelligence. ## Inputs - work orders - evidence bundles - diffs - postmortem notes ## Steps 1. Confirm the issue was actually resolved. 2. Capture environment, symptoms, and validated root cause. 3. Summarize the solution and design paradigm. 4. Extract reusable patterns and prevention rules. 5. Tag by domain, platform, language, and risk. 6. Mark whether the record is training-corpus eligible. ## Outputs - fix-memory record - training-corpus candidate - guardrail updates

===FILE:apps/flagship-foundry/services/system-orchestrator/src/swarm-consensus.mjs===import { getAdapter } from '../../../packages/runtime-adapters/src/registry.mjs'; /** * Executes a Model Swarm Consensus pipeline for a specific plan. * Specifier -> Architect -> Adversary -> Verifier */ export async function executeSwarmConsensus(plan) { const shards = []; for (const projectPlan of plan.projectPlans) { for (const phase of projectPlan.phases) { console.log(`[swarm-consensus] Executing phase: ${phase} for project ${projectPlan.name}`); let adapter; if (phase === 'inspect' || phase === 'propose') { // Architect adapter = getAdapter('claudeCode'); console.log(`[swarm-consensus] -> Assigned to Specifier/Architect (${adapter.name})`); } else if (phase.startsWith('challenge')) { // Adversary adapter = getAdapter('claudeCode'); // Different logical persona using the same adapter console.log(`[swarm-consensus] -> Assigned to Adversary Analyst (${adapter.name})`); } else if (phase.startsWith('reconcile')) { // Reconciler adapter = getAdapter('cursor'); console.log(`[swarm-consensus] -> Assigned to Reconciler (${adapter.name})`); } else if (phase === 'verify') { adapter = getAdapter('codex'); console.log(`[swarm-consensus] -> Assigned to Verifier (${adapter.name})`); } else if (phase === 'design') { console.log(`[swarm-consensus] -> Generating PRD Shards & Diagrams...`); shards.push({ shardId: `shard-${Date.now()}`, ownerNodeId: projectPlan.projectId, objective: plan.objective, acceptanceCriteria: ["All unit tests pass", "Component renders properly"], blastRadius: { impactedSystems: [projectPlan.projectId], couplingRisk: "low" }, verificationPlan: ["Run npm test"] }); } // Simulating time to execute swarm step await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 200)); } } return { complete: true, shardsGenerated: shards }; }

===FILE:README.md===# Flagship Foundry Flagship Foundry is a graph-native SDLC control plane for human plus AI orchestration. **Runnable product code** for this effort lives in [`apps/flagship-foundry/`](apps/flagship-foundry/). See [`apps/flagship-foundry/docs/REPOSITORY_LAYOUT.md`](apps/flagship-foundry/docs/REPOSITORY_LAYOUT.md) for canonical layout and how this repo relates to research docs at the root. This repository now includes a working import, knowledge-ingestion, gap-analysis, focus-view, approval-aware planning, and run-control slice that starts from an existing workspace rather than assuming a greenfield implementation path. ## What is here Inside [`apps/flagship-foundry/`](apps/flagship-foundry/): - `apps/control-plane/` — HTTP API for import, knowledge ingestion, gap analysis, focus views, planning, approval, run control, and graph patching - `apps/orchestrator-cli/` — CLI for bootstrap, import, knowledge, gaps, focus, planning, environment scaffold, and runs - `apps/cursor-companion/` — VS Code and Cursor companion - `packages/core/` — import pipeline, graph store, plans, runs, knowledge, environment scaffold, catalogs - `knowledge/`, `schemas/`, `runbooks/`, `personas/`, `guardrails/`, `configs/`, `ontology/`, `environments/`, `examples/`, `state/` ## Quick start ```bash # From repo root (Nx monorepo) pnpm install pnpm exec nx run flagship-foundry:test pnpm exec nx run flagship-foundry:ci-targeted # Or from the app directory cd apps/flagship-foundry npm run bootstrap:full-sample npm run api npm test ``` ## Sample commands ```bash cd apps/flagship-foundry npm run import:sample npm run knowledge:sample npm run gap:sample npm run focus:sample npm run plan:sample ``` ## Primary URLs - `GET /health` - `POST /ingestion/workspace-import` - `POST /knowledge/ingest` - `POST /analysis/gaps` - `POST /analysis/focus` - `POST /planning/create` - `POST /runs/start` - `POST /plans/:id/approve` - `POST /runs/:id/pause|resume|stop` - `POST /environments/scaffold` ## Current direction Start with the Cursor companion and terminal adapters while keeping the control plane framework-agnostic. Use import plus knowledge plus gap analysis to identify where doctrine, skills, runbooks, personas, and environment parity are still incomplete before wiring a real executor.
===FILE:tools/ai-context/chunk-export.mjs===#!/usr/bin/env node /** * Split a minified AI export (one line per file record after header) into N parts. * Loads all lines into memory first: awaiting writes inside a readline `for await` loop * can backpressure the stream and drop lines on huge exports. * * Byte-split (sub-chunk a chunk file to a max UTF-8 size; use sibling parts 1–3 as reference): * node tools/ai-context/chunk-export.mjs <chunk-file.txt> --byte-split --max-bytes-from-parts * node tools/ai-context/chunk-export.mjs <chunk-file.txt> --byte-split --max-bytes-from-parts max * node tools/ai-context/chunk-export.mjs <chunk-file.txt> --byte-split --max-bytes 8000000 * * Usage: * node tools/ai-context/chunk-export.mjs <path-to-export.txt> [--parts 4] */ import { createReadStream } from 'node:fs'; import { createInterface } from 'node:readline'; import { promises as fs } from 'node:fs'; import path from 'node:path'; import process from 'node:process'; function parseArgs(argv) { const args = { input: null, parts: 4, byteSplit: false, maxBytes: null, maxBytesFromParts: false, referencePartsAgg: 'min' }; const rest = argv.filter((t) => t !== '--'); if (rest[0] && !rest[0].startsWith('--')) { args.input = rest[0]; } for (let i = 0; i < rest.length; i += 1) { if (rest[i] === '--parts' && rest[i + 1]) { const n = Number(rest[i + 1]); if (!Number.isInteger(n) || n < 2) { throw new Error('--parts must be an integer >= 2'); } args.parts = n; i += 1; } else if (rest[i] === '--byte-split') { args.byteSplit = true; } else if (rest[i] === '--max-bytes' && rest[i + 1]) { const n = Number(rest[i + 1]); if (!Number.isFinite(n) || n < 1024) { throw new Error('--max-bytes must be a number >= 1024'); } args.maxBytes = Math.floor(n); i += 1; } else if (rest[i] === '--max-bytes-from-parts') { args.maxBytesFromParts = true; if (rest[i + 1] === 'min' || rest[i + 1] === 'max') { args.referencePartsAgg = rest[i + 1]; i += 1; } } } if (!args.input) { throw new Error( 'Usage: node chunk-export.mjs <export.txt> [--parts 4] | [--byte-split (--max-bytes N | --max-bytes-from-parts [min|max])]' ); } return args; } /** * Read every line (readline semantics, CRLF-safe) without mixing in slow consumers. * @param {string} filePath * @returns {Promise<string[]>} */ async function readAllLines(filePath) { const lines = []; const rl = createInterface({ input: createReadStream(filePath, { encoding: 'utf8' }), crlfDelay: Infinity }); for await (const line of rl) { lines.push(line); } return lines; } function computeChunkSizes(totalDataLines, parts) { const base = Math.floor(totalDataLines / parts); const rem = totalDataLines % parts; const sizes = []; for (let i = 0; i < parts; i += 1) { sizes.push(base + (i < rem ? 1 : 0)); } return sizes; } /** * @param {string} baseName basename without ext, e.g. export-part-04-of-04 * @param {string} ext * @param {string} dir * @param {'min' | 'max'} agg */ async function resolveMaxBytesFromReferenceParts(baseName, ext, dir, agg) { const re = /^export-part-(\d+)-of-(\d+)$/; const m = re.exec(baseName); if (!m) { throw new Error( '--max-bytes-from-parts requires input basename like export-part-NN-of-TT (e.g. export-part-04-of-04.txt)' ); } const totalParts = m[2]; const sizes = []; for (let i = 1; i <= 3; i += 1) { const name = `export-part-${String(i).padStart(2, '0')}-of-${totalParts}${ext}`; const p = path.join(dir, name); const st = await fs.stat(p); sizes.push(st.size); } return agg === 'min' ? Math.min(...sizes) : Math.max(...sizes); } /** * @param {number} subIdx * @param {number} subTotal * @param {string} baseName * @param {string} sourcePathRel * @param {string} exportHeaderLine */ function buildSubchunkHeader(subIdx, subTotal, baseName, sourcePathRel, exportHeaderLine) { return [ `# SUBCHUNK ${String(subIdx).padStart(2, '0')}/${String(subTotal).padStart(2, '0')} — split from ${baseName}`, `# source_path=${sourcePathRel}`, exportHeaderLine ].join('\n') + '\n'; } /** * @param {string[]} dataLines * @param {number} maxBodyBytes * @returns {string[][]} */ function packGroupsByBodyBudget(dataLines, maxBodyBytes) { const groups = []; let cur = []; let body = 0; for (const line of dataLines) { const lineB = Buffer.byteLength(`${line}\n`, 'utf8'); if (cur.length > 0 && body + lineB > maxBodyBytes) { groups.push(cur); cur = []; body = 0; } cur.push(line); body += lineB; } if (cur.length) { groups.push(cur); } return groups; } /** * @param {string[]} dataLines * @param {number} maxBytes * @param {string} baseName * @param {string} sourcePathRel * @param {string} exportHeaderLine */ function packSubchunksWithinBudget(dataLines, maxBytes, baseName, sourcePathRel, exportHeaderLine) { const worstHeader = Buffer.byteLength( buildSubchunkHeader(99, 99, baseName, sourcePathRel, exportHeaderLine), 'utf8' ); let maxBodyBytes = maxBytes - worstHeader; if (maxBodyBytes < 512) { throw new Error('--max-bytes is too small to fit the subchunk header'); } for (let iter = 0; iter < 80; iter += 1) { const groups = packGroupsByBodyBudget(dataLines, maxBodyBytes); const subTotal = groups.length; let allOk = true; for (let i = 0; i < groups.length; i += 1) { const h = buildSubchunkHeader(i + 1, subTotal, baseName, sourcePathRel, exportHeaderLine); const b = groups[i].map((l) => `${l}\n`).join(''); if (Buffer.byteLength(h + b, 'utf8') > maxBytes) { allOk = false; break; } } if (allOk) { return { groups, maxBodyBytes }; } maxBodyBytes -= 8192; } throw new Error( 'Could not pack subchunks within --max-bytes. Increase the limit, or a single data line may exceed the budget.' ); } /** * @param {{ input: string, maxBytes: number | null, maxBytesFromParts: boolean, referencePartsAgg: 'min' | 'max' }} args */ async function byteSplitMain(args) { if (!args.maxBytes && !args.maxBytesFromParts) { throw new Error('byte-split requires --max-bytes <n> or --max-bytes-from-parts [min|max]'); } const abs = path.resolve(args.input); const dir = path.dirname(abs); const baseName = path.basename(abs, path.extname(abs)); const ext = path.extname(abs) || '.txt'; let maxBytes = args.maxBytes; if (args.maxBytesFromParts) { maxBytes = await resolveMaxBytesFromReferenceParts(baseName, ext, dir, args.referencePartsAgg); } if (maxBytes == null || maxBytes < 2048) { throw new Error('Resolved max-bytes is invalid'); } const lines = await readAllLines(abs); if (lines.length < 4 || !lines[0].startsWith('# CHUNK')) { throw new Error( 'byte-split expects a chunk file: line 1 # CHUNK …, line 2 # source_path=…, line 3 # AI_CONTEXT_EXPORT …, then data lines' ); } const sourcePathRel = lines[1].replace(/^#\s*source_path=/, '').trim(); const exportHeaderLine = lines[2]; const dataLines = lines.slice(3); const { groups } = packSubchunksWithinBudget( dataLines, maxBytes, baseName, sourcePathRel, exportHeaderLine ); const subTotal = groups.length; const outputs = []; for (let i = 0; i < groups.length; i += 1) { const subIdx = i + 1; const header = buildSubchunkHeader(subIdx, subTotal, baseName, sourcePathRel, exportHeaderLine); const body = groups[i].map((l) => `${l}\n`).join(''); const outName = `${baseName}-sub-${String(subIdx).padStart(2, '0')}-of-${String(subTotal).padStart(2, '0')}${ext}`; const outPath = path.join(dir, outName); await fs.writeFile(outPath, header + body, 'utf8'); outputs.push(outName); } const byteSizes = await Promise.all(outputs.map((n) => fs.stat(path.join(dir, n)).then((s) => s.size))); console.log( JSON.stringify( { mode: 'byte-split', input: path.relative(process.cwd(), abs).split(path.sep).join('/'), maxBytes, referencePartsAgg: args.maxBytesFromParts ? args.referencePartsAgg : undefined, dataLines: dataLines.length, subchunks: subTotal, outputs, outputBytes: byteSizes }, null, 2 ) ); } async function main() { const args = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2)); if (args.byteSplit) { await byteSplitMain(args); return; } const { input, parts } = args; const abs = path.resolve(input); const dir = path.dirname(abs); const baseName = path.basename(abs, path.extname(abs)); const ext = path.extname(abs) || '.txt'; const lines = await readAllLines(abs); const totalLines = lines.length; if (totalLines < 2) { throw new Error('Export file must have a header line and at least one data line'); } const headerLine = lines[0]; const dataLines = lines.slice(1); const dataLineCount = dataLines.length; const sizes = computeChunkSizes(dataLineCount, parts); const sumSizes = sizes.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0); if (sumSizes !== dataLineCount) { throw new Error(`Internal chunk size mismatch: ${sumSizes} !== ${dataLineCount}`); } let offset = 0; for (let chunkIdx = 0; chunkIdx < parts; chunkIdx += 1) { const chunkSize = sizes[chunkIdx]; const slice = dataLines.slice(offset, offset + chunkSize); offset += chunkSize; if (slice.length !== chunkSize) { throw new Error( `Chunk ${chunkIdx + 1}: expected ${chunkSize} data lines, got ${slice.length}` ); } const part = String(chunkIdx + 1).padStart(2, '0'); const outName = `${baseName}-part-${part}-of-${String(parts).padStart(2, '0')}${ext}`; const outPath = path.join(dir, outName); const header = [ `# CHUNK ${chunkIdx + 1}/${parts} — split from ${path.basename(abs)}`, `# source_path=${path.relative(process.cwd(), abs).split(path.sep).join('/')}`, headerLine ].join('\n') + '\n'; const body = slice.map((l) => `${l}\n`).join(''); await fs.writeFile(outPath, header + body, 'utf8'); } if (offset !== dataLineCount) { throw new Error(`Offset after writes ${offset} !== data lines ${dataLineCount}`); } console.log( JSON.stringify( { input: path.relative(process.cwd(), abs).split(path.sep).join('/'), totalLines, dataLines: dataLineCount, parts, chunkSizes: sizes, outputs: sizes.map((_, i) => { const part = String(i + 1).padStart(2, '0'); return `${baseName}-part-${part}-of-${String(parts).padStart(2, '0')}${ext}`; }) }, null, 2 ) ); } main().catch((e) => { console.error(`[chunk-export] ${e.message}`); process.exitCode = 1; });
===FILE:tools/ai-context/exporter.mjs===#!/usr/bin/env node import { promises as fs } from 'node:fs'; import path from 'node:path'; import process from 'node:process'; const repoRoot = process.cwd(); Use all | latest | profile`); } return args; } async function readJson(filePath) { const raw = await fs.readFile(filePath, 'utf8'); return JSON.parse(raw); } function normalizeSlashes(value) { return value.split(path.sep).join('/'); } function toRelativeOrThrow(absolutePath) { const resolved = path.resolve(repoRoot, absolutePath); const rel = path.relative(repoRoot, resolved); if (rel.startsWith('..') || path.isAbsolute(rel)) { throw new Error(`Path escapes repository root: ${absolutePath}`); } return normalizeSlashes(rel || '.'); } function resolveInputPath(inputPath) { if (!inputPath) { return null; } if (path.isAbsolute(inputPath)) { return path.resolve(inputPath); } return path.resolve(repoRoot, inputPath); } async function pathExists(targetPath) { try { await fs.access(targetPath); return true; } catch { return false; } } function matchesIgnoreFragment(rel, normalized) { if (normalized.startsWith('^') && normalized.endsWith('/')) { const rootSegment = normalized.slice(1, -1); } } for (const fragment of [...baseIgnore, ...extraIgnore]) { const normalized = normalizeSlashes(fragment); if (matchesIgnoreFragment(rel, normalized)) { return 'ignored-path'; } } return null; } function shouldSkipByType(relPath) { const ext = path.extname(relPath).toLowerCase(); if (textDenylist.has(ext)) { return 'non-text-extension'; } return null; } function minifyContent(content) { return content .replace(/\r\n/g, '\n') .replace(/\n+/g, ' ') .replace(/\t+/g, ' ') .replace(/\s{2,}/g, ' ') .trim(); } function estTimestampForFolder(date = new Date()) { const formatter = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone: 'America/New_York', year: 'numeric', month: '2-digit', day: '2-digit', hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit', second: '2-digit', hour12: false }); } if (!(await pathExists(resolvedStart))) { collector.skipped.push({ path: normalizeSlashes(startPath), reason: 'missing-path' }); return; } const relStart = toRelativeOrThrow(resolvedStart); const ignoredStart = shouldSkipByName(relStart, baseIgnore, extraIgnore); if (ignoredStart) { collector.skipped.push({ path: relStart, reason: ignoredStart }); return; } const stat = await fs.stat(resolvedStart); if (stat.isFile()) { collector.fileSet.add(relStart); return; } async function walk(currentAbs) { const entries = await fs.readdir(currentAbs, { withFileTypes: true }); for (const entry of entries) { const entryAbs = path.join(currentAbs, entry.name); const entryRel = toRelativeOrThrow(entryAbs); const skipNameReason = shouldSkipByName(entryRel, baseIgnore, extraIgnore); if (skipNameReason) { collector.skipped.push({ path: entryRel, reason: skipNameReason }); continue; } if (entry.isDirectory()) { await walk(entryAbs); continue; } if (!entry.isFile()) { collector.skipped.push({ path: entryRel, reason: 'unsupported-file-type' }); continue; } const skipTypeReason = shouldSkipByType(entryRel); if (skipTypeReason) { collector.skipped.push({ path: entryRel, reason: skipTypeReason }); continue; } const fileStat = await fs.stat(entryAbs); if (fileStat.size > maxFileBytes) { collector.skipped.push({ path: entryRel, reason: `file-too-large:${fileStat.size}` }); continue; } collector.fileSet.add(entryRel); } } await walk(resolvedStart); } function filterExcluded(filePaths, excludes) { if (!excludes.length) { return filePaths; } const normalizedExcludes = excludes.map((value) => normalizeSlashes(value)); [] }; } if (mode === 'latest') { const latestPath = path.join(profilesDir, 'latest.json'); const latest = await readJson(latestPath); return { mode, include: latest.include ?? []), ...(profile.exclude ?? [])], extraIgnore: [...(defaultIgnore.extraIgnore ?? []), ...(profile.extraIgnore ?? [])], outputFileName: profile.outputFileName ?? null, versioned: profile.versioned ?? false }; } throw new Error(`Unrecognized mode: ${mode}`); } async function readAndMinifyFile(relPath, collector) { const absPath = path.join(repoRoot, relPath); const buffer = await fs.readFile(absPath); if (buffer.includes(0x00)) { collector.skipped.push({ path: relPath, reason: 'binary-nul-byte' }); return null; } const text = buffer.toString('utf8'); return minifyContent(text); } async function ensureOutput(args, effectiveVersioned) { const outputDir = args.outputDir; await fs.mkdir(outputDir, { recursive: true }); if (!effectiveVersioned) { const latestFile = path.join(outputDir, args.outputFileName ?? 'latest.txt'); if (await pathExists(latestFile)) { await fs.rm(latestFile, { force: true }); } return { outputFile: latestFile, outputFolder: outputDir }; } const folderName = estTimestampForFolder(); const versionedFolder = path.join(outputDir, folderName); await fs.mkdir(versionedFolder, { recursive: true }); const outputFile = path.join(versionedFolder, args.outputFileName ?? 'export.txt'); return { outputFile, outputFolder: versionedFolder }; } function summarizeSkipped(skipped) { const counts = new Map(); for (const row of skipped) { const previous = counts.get(row.reason) ?? 0; counts.set(row.reason, previous + 1); } return Object.fromEntries([...counts.entries()].sort((a, b) => a[0].localeCompare(b[0]))); } async function main() { const argv = process.argv.slice(2).filter((token) => token !== '--'); const args = parseArgs(argv); const modeConfig = await resolveModeConfig(args.mode, args.profilePath); const effectiveVersioned = args.versioned || Boolean(modeConfig.versioned); if (!args.outputFileName && modeConfig.outputFileName) { args.outputFileName = modeConfig.outputFileName; } const collector = { fileSet: new Set(), skipped: [] }; const collectOptions = { baseIgnore: [...builtInIgnoreFragments, ...(modeConfig.exclude ?? [])], extraIgnore: modeConfig.extraIgnore ?? ===FILE:tools/ai-context/README.md===# AI Context Exporter Exports repository content to one minified text file for AI context submission. ## Quick Commands - `pnpm export:ai:all` - Full repository export using default safety/ignore rules. - `pnpm export:ai:latest` - Export the curated list in `tools/ai-context/profiles/latest.json`. - `pnpm export:ai:profile -- --profile <json>` - Export from a custom include/exclude profile JSON. ## Optional Flags - `--versioned`: write output into `exports/ai-context/YYYY-MM-DD_HH-mm-ss_EST/`. - `--outputDir <path>`: override output root. - `--dry-run`: print file selection summary without writing output files. - `--outputFileName <name>`: override output filename. - `--maxFileBytes <n>`: skip files larger than `n` bytes (default 524288). ## Output Behavior - Default output root: `exports/ai-context/`. - Non-versioned mode: - Deletes prior target file (`latest.txt` by default) if present. - Writes one aggregate text file and `manifest.json`. - Versioned mode: - Creates timestamped EST folder. - Writes `export.txt` (or configured name) and `manifest.json`. ## Format Each file is represented as one line: `===FILE:<relative/path>===<minified-content>` Minification collapses whitespace and removes newlines/tabs. ## Default Safety Rules Configured in `tools/ai-context/profiles/default-ignore.json`: - Skip generated/system folders (e.g. `node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `coverage`, reports, cache dirs). - Skip lockfiles. - Skip sensitive names/patterns (`.env*`, key/cert-like names, token/secret/credential patterns). - Skip known binary extensions and NUL-byte files. - Skip imported ecosystems/projects by default (`iterative-development-storage`, repo-root `ralph/` via `^ralph/`, etc.). ## Example: `Example AI Agent Pipelines` only Profiles (one folder per export): - `tools/ai-context/profiles/example-agent-pipelines-ralph.json` - `tools/ai-context/profiles/example-agent-pipelines-ruflo.json` ```bash pnpm export:ai:profile -- --profile tools/ai-context/profiles/example-agent-pipelines-ralph.json --outputDir exports/ai-context/example-agent-pipelines/ralph pnpm export:ai:profile -- --profile tools/ai-context/profiles/example-agent-pipelines-ruflo.json --outputDir exports/ai-context/example-agent-pipelines/ruflo ``` ## Profile JSON Schema ```json { "include": ["apps", ".cursor", "README.md"], "exclude": ["apps/some-large-project/", "docs/3rd-party/"], "extraIgnore": ["*.snap", "tmp/"], "mode": "include-only", "versioned": false, "outputFileName": "custom-export.txt" } ``` Notes: - `include` is required for profile mode. - Paths can be relative to repo root or absolute paths within repo root. ## Generate a Profile JSON (AI-assisted helper) Use helper script: `pnpm export:ai:profile:generate -- --out tools/ai-context/profiles/my-profile.json --include .cursor --include apps --exclude apps/legacy --prompt "focus on SDLC orchestration"` The helper writes a valid profile JSON and reports unresolved paths in metadata.
